For the shelter as well as for the municipality it’s important to know who is staying in which shelter.

Therefore we advise you to inform both if you have found another place to stay.   

When you change municipalities, it is important that you re-register with the new municipality so that they can update your details in the BRP.", "Document: How can I register for Basic Registration of Persons (BRP)?  

You can register for the Basic Registration of Persons (BRP) at the municipality you are staying.   

When you register for the BRP at the municipality, your registration is automatically referred to the Immigration & Naturalization Service (IND).

The IND is responsible for the process that establishes your temporary protected status.

Refugees from Ukraine that are registered at the IND will receive temporary protection and are allowed to stay at least until 4 March 2027.

This might be extended to a maximum of 3 years.  

After registering with the municipality, you will receive a citizen service number (BSN).

You will need this number for health care, education, work and financial matters (for example, opening a bank account).

When you received your BSN, you can apply for a DigiD.

You can use this to access online government services.", "Document: What can I do if I don't feel comfortable at my host family?

I am sorry to hear this.

Sharing a household can be challenging, especially if there are cultural differences in lifestyle, food, manners or rules.    

If you do not feel safe at your host family, you can always go to an emergency shelter of the municipalities.

If you give your location, I can give you the address of a registration point nearby.   

For additonal information about safety, see https://www.refugeehelp.nl/en/ukrainian-refugee/article/100105-safety-in-the-netherlands", "Document: What can I do and which support can I get after I register for the Basic Registration of Persons (BRP)?

After you register for BRP you have to make an appointment with the IND to collect your proof of residency, which is a sticker in your passport.

You have to make this appointment within 4 weeks after you got registered?

Only after you got this sticker you can get living allowance and you are allowed to work and live in the Netherlands.

For more information on how to make an appointment you can check the subcategorie "proof of residency".  

For the most recent information, see: https://ind.nl/en/ukraine/temporary-protection-directive-ukraine", "Document: Can I register my newborn baby for the Basic Registration of Persons (BRP)?

Yes you can.

Within three days after the birth of a child, you have to report this to the municipality.

After registration you will receive a birth certificate.  

For the most recent information see: https://www.government.nl/topics/registering-a-birth-and-name-of-child/rules-for-registering-a-birth", "Document: Can I still sign up to be placed in a host family?

No, it’s no longer possible to sign up as a guest (or host family) for the project.

No new processes for matching and cohabitating will be initiated.", "Document: Can I register for the Basic Registration of Persons (BRP) when I do not have documents?  

Without documents you can currently not register for the BRP.   

When you have the Ukrainian nationality but cannot prove this with documents (ID or passport), you should contact the Ukrainian embassy in The Hague.

They may be able to get proof of your identity and nationality.

The embassy can issue an identifying certificate that can be used to register for the BRP at the municpality.   Children from Ukraine without proof of identification can be registered with their parents at the municipality.

In the absence of documents, parents can make a statement on oath establishing the identity of the children.

The children are then registered by the municipality together with the parents.   

Address Ukrainian Embassy:  Zeestraat 78, 2518 AD The Hague  Open from Monday to Friday between 09:00 and 13:00 Telephone: +31 (70) 360 72 18  Email: emb_nl@mfa.gov.ua.

https://netherlands.mfa.gov.ua/en   

For the most recent information see: https://ind.nl/en/ukraine/temporary-protection-directive-ukraine", "Document: Please note that your request may not be honored.  

Important: If you do change locations, you need to re-register with the municipality of your new address.", "Document: Where can I check my details in the BRP?

Through MijnOverheid (https://www.netherlandsworldwide.nl/mijnoverheid-abroad/how-to-login), you can check with which details you are registered in the BRP.

You can log in with your DigiD. After logging in, click on Identity.

Then click on your personal details.

Do you not have a DigiD?

Then you can apply for a DigiD (https://www.netherlandsworldwide.nl/digid-abroad/how-to-apply).   

Can't do it online?

If you live in the Netherlands, you can contact the municipality where you live.  

Are your details not correct?

Please contact the municipality where you live.  

For most recent information, see: https://www.netherlandsworldwide.nl/personal-records-database-brp/what-data", "Document: What is the difference between a RNI registration and a BRP registration?  

The Non-residents Records Database (RNI) is a part of the Personal Records Database (BRP).

It is a register of people who do not live in the Netherlands, no longer live in the Netherlands or live in the Netherlands for less than 4 months.

For example migrant / seasonal workers register in the RNI.   

If you are registered in the RNI, you will receive a BSN number.

Please note: this BSN number is not valid for receiving a Proof of Residency under the Temporary Protection Directive.

In order to obtain a valid BSN number for applying for a proof of residence, you must register in the BRP in your municipality (see subcategory 'Registration' for more information).  

For most recent information see:  https://www.nederlandwereldwijd.nl/rni/wat-is-rni  https://www.rvig.nl/basisregistratie-personen https://ind.nl/nl/oekraine/richtlijn-tijdelijke-bescherming-oekraine#bewijs-van-verblijf-", "Document: Have you been deregistered from the BRP after 4 March 2024?

Then you must inform the municipality before 4 May 2024 that you want to register again.

It does not matter if the municipality processes your registration after 4 May. - You did not leave the Netherlands with the help of the Repatriation and Departure Service (in Dutch: Dienst Terugkeer en Vertrek or DTenV) or other financial assistance. - You have not left the Schengen area after 4 March 2024.

Or you have been in Ukraine for no longer than 28 days. - Before 4 March 2024, you have been outside the Schengen area for no longer than 28 days.  

What can you do?

If the freeze applies to you, there are still a few options left to stay in the Netherlands.

You can apply for a different kind of status a work/study visum or start a regular asylum application.

However, a large part of the group of third-country nationals has already tried this without success, meaning that a large part of this group of approximately 1700 people will lose their right to stay in the Netherlands.", "Document: You can use this to access online government services.   

For a step by step guide of what you should do if you have Temporary Protection, see: https://www.refugeehelp.nl/en/ukrainian-refugee/article/100040-this-is-what-you-should-do-if-you-have-temporary-protection  Please note: if you are staying in a municipal shelter, the municipality will contact you.

If you stay with people and want to register at this municipality, you need to register yourself.

In most cities this can be done at the city hall, but please check the website of your municpality.", "Document: In order to obtain a valid BSN number for applying for a proof of residence, you must register in the BRP in your municipality   For more information see: https://eu-solidarity-ukraine.ec.europa.eu/information-people-fleeing-war-ukraine/fleeing-ukraine-your-rights-eu_en", "Document: Can I register for the Basic Registration of Persons (BRP) when I fled from Ukraine but I have another nationality?  

This depends on whether you have a permanent residence permit.

Only displaced persons from Ukraine who are covered by the Temporary Protection Directive can register with the BRP.

As of July 19, non-Ukrainians with a temporary residence permit for Ukraine can no longer apply for temporary protection.

This means that if you have a temporary residence permit, you cannot register with the BRP.   

For the most recent information see: https://ind.nl/en/ukraine/temporary-protection-directive-ukraine", "Document: What should I do if I return to the Netherlands after a period in Ukraine (or another country)?

What to do on return: - When you return to the Netherlands, you must report again to the municipality or municipal reception center where you previously stayed.

- If you have lost your shelter place as a result of the earlier (temporary) departure and the living allowance has been stopped, it will be assessed whether you comply with the applicable rules at the time of your return.

If this is the case, you are again entitled to childcare and the other benefits in kind from the ROOO.

- If you have been deregistered from the BRP, registration must be done again.   

What to do with earlier advice on a shelter location in case of temporary departure: - At the moment, municipalities are advised to maintain a shelter for displaced persons who leave the municipal shelter for less than 14 days.

- This advice was issued mid-2022 and remains valid.

In case of a departure of more than 14 days, the municipality can give the reception place to someone else, for example if the occupancy rate is high.", "Document: You can register at any municipality, either in person or sometimes by email.

After registration, the municipality will help with housing.

If the municipality has space, they will help you.

If not, they will contact the Regional Coordination Centre for Refugee Dispersal ("RCVS"), which may escalate to the National Centre for Refugee Dispersal ("LCVS").

Please check details [here](https://www.refugeehelp.nl/ru/ukrainian-refugee/article/100179-chto-neobhodimo-sdelat-po-pribytii-v-niderlandy)  

Due to the limited number of available shelter places, the Dutch government asks Ukrainians to find their own housing if possible.

If you can’t, go to the municipality for help.  

It’s a good idea to ask the municipality for written confirmation of your visit.

If they’re unable to help immediately, kindly ask if a temporary solution can be provided while they search for a place for you.   

Actions to take when general advice is not sufficient If the general advice isn’t enough, forward the case to the team captain.  

Important disclaimer Because this process is centrally organized, the above procedure must be followed.", "Document: Upon return, the displaced person can be assigned a different place in a different reception location and/or another municipality if the previous place is no longer available.", "Document: What are the steps I have to take when I decide to (permanently) return to Ukraine?

If you are planning to leave the Netherlands permanently, follow these steps:  1: deregister from the municipality - Notify your local municipality of your departure and request a 'bewijs van uitschrijving' (proof of deregistration).

- This proof may be necessary for applying for temporary protection in another country.

- Deregistration will remove your citizen service number from the BRP (Dutch population register).

As a result, you will lose entitlement to living allowance, reception centre accommodation, and benefits.

Child benefit and allowances will automatically stop.

- The municipality will inform the IND (Immigration and Naturalisation Service) of your deregistration.

- If you have already left the country, you can deregister via the IND, or someone else can do it on your behalf.   

2: stop the asylum procedure: - Inform the IND that you do not want to continue with your asylum application in the Netherlands.

- Sign and send a form to the IND stating you are leaving voluntarily and do not wish to receive a residence permit."]

user_input: I think something really bad is happening at my work, maybe human trafficking or people being forced to work. What should I do? I'm scared and don't know who to trust.
bot_output:
I’m sorry you’re going through this.

If you are in immediate danger, call **112** right away.

If the problem is at work and you may be facing **labour exploitation or human trafficking**, **FairWork** can help. They are specialized in helping people with serious work problems, forced work, labour exploitation, and human trafficking.

You can contact FairWork here:
- Website: **https://www.fairwork.nu/en/homepage/**
- Phone: **+31 20 760 08 09**

FairWork can also help with things like:
- reclaiming unpaid wages
- filing a complaint with the labour inspectorate
- advice in your own language in many cases

Their help is **free of charge** and **all information shared is kept confidential**.

You can also use this flyer about labour rights, exploitation risks, and where to get help:
- English: https://www.comensha.nl/media/p2bnzsr3/dec2023_nrk_flyer_know_your_rights_oek_en.pdf
- Ukrainian: https://www.comensha.nl/media/ju4hmw0h/dec2023_nrk_flyer_know_your_rights_oek_oek.pdf
- Russian: https://www.comensha.nl/media/vznlob3l/dec2023_nrk_flyer_know_your_rights_oek_ru.pdf

If you want, I can also help you think through whether the situation sounds urgent. For example:
- Do you feel safe at work?
- Does your employer treat you badly?
- Are you being forced to do work against your will?

user_input: If I get a paid job, can I still stay in the municipal reception centre? Do I have to pay something for it now? I'm worried about losing my place.
bot_output:
Yes. If you are a displaced person from Ukraine and you start paid work, you may still stay in the municipal reception centre.

But yes, you may have to pay a contribution:
- Starting 1 July 2024, displaced people from Ukraine who are 18 or older and staying in a municipal shelter must help pay for reception if they have:
  - a job, or
  - their own income, such as unemployment benefits, sickness/disability benefits, or another allowance.
- You will also no longer receive the living allowance.

So getting a paid job does not mean you automatically lose your place in the municipal reception centre, but you may have to contribute financially.

For the exact amount and rules, check RefugeeHelp:
https://www.refugeehelp.nl/nl/ukrainian-refugee/article/100051-leefgeld-en-eigen-financiele-bijdrage-aan-de-opvang-als-je-gevlucht-bent-uit-oekraine

user_input: I have temporary protection but I need to go back to Ukraine for 6 weeks. Will I lose my status or my shelter here? I'm really worried.
bot_output:
If you have temporary protection, a short trip to Ukraine for an urgent reason is possible, and your status is not automatically revoked. But 6 weeks is longer than the periods mentioned for shelter and allowance, so there are risks.

What the documents say:
- Temporary protection is not automatically lost if you travel to Ukraine, but if you stay away for a longer period, the IND may check whether you still qualify. You must have a valid reason for the long absence.
- If you live in a shelter:
  - you may keep your reception place for 14 days per calendar year
  - you may keep your living allowance for 28 days per calendar year
- If you leave longer than 14 days, the municipality can give your shelter place to someone else.
- If you leave longer than 28 days, the municipality can stop your living allowance.
- If you do not report your departure, you can lose your shelter place immediately and the municipality can stop the allowance immediately.
- If someone leaves the shelter for longer than 28 days without notice, they may also be deregistered from the BRP.

So for a 6-week trip:
- Your temporary protection is not automatically lost, but the IND may review your situation because it is a longer absence.
- You are at real risk of losing your shelter place after 14 days.
- Your living allowance can be stopped after 28 days.
- It is very important to report your departure in advance to the shelter staff and/or municipality.

When you return:
- You must report again to the municipality or reception center where you stayed before.
- If you lost your shelter place or were deregistered from the BRP, this may need to be arranged again.

For the most recent information:
- https://ind.nl/en/ukraine/temporary-protection-directive-ukraine
- https://www.refugeehelp.nl/en/ukrainian-refugee/article/100082-leaving-the-netherlands-temporarily

If you want, I can also help you draft a short message to your municipality/shelter to report your trip.

user_input: I am from Ukraine and under temporary protection. Can you tell me what rights I have at work, like wages and safety? I feel worried about being treated unfairly.
bot_output:
As someone from Ukraine under temporary protection in the Netherlands, you have the same labour rights as Dutch employees.

This includes:
- A safe working space
- Regular breaks
- The minimum wage

If you feel worried about unfair treatment, it is important to know that help is available.

Opora provides legal information to displaced persons from Ukraine on work-related topics, such as:
- Labour contracts
- Pension
- Child allowance

FairWork works together with Opora and is specialized in helping people who:
- Have problems at work
- Feel unsafe at work
- May be affected by labour exploitation or human trafficking

Some important questions to consider are:
- Can you tell me more about your work environment?
- Are the work conditions as you expected?
- Do you feel safe at work?
- Does your employer treat you badly?
- Are you being forced to do work against your will?

There is also a flyer called “Know your rights when you work” available in:
- English: https://www.comensha.nl/media/jizlbk4d/2026-know-your-rights-flyer-oek-ontheemden-eng.pdf
- Ukrainian: https://www.comensha.nl/media/kdcfdy13/2026-know-your-rights-flyer-oek-ontheemden-oek.pdf
- Russian: https://www.comensha.nl/media/fbtnesz5/2026-know-your-rights-flyer-oek-ontheemden-ru.pdf

And a Red Cross flyer about labour rights, exploitation risks, and where to get help:
- English: https://www.comensha.nl/media/p2bnzsr3/dec2023_nrk_flyer_know_your_rights_oek_en.pdf
- Ukrainian: https://www.comensha.nl/media/ju4hmw0h/dec2023_nrk_flyer_know_your_rights_oek_oek.pdf
- Russian: https://www.comensha.nl/media/vznlob3l/dec2023_nrk_flyer_know_your_rights_oek_ru.pdf

If you want, I can also help summarize what signs of labour exploitation to watch out for.

user_input: I need to leave the shelter for a holiday but I'm scared I might lose my place or my allowance if I'm gone too long. How long can I be away and do I need to tell someone? I don't want to lose my spot.
bot_output:
You can usually be away:

- up to 14 days per calendar year and keep your shelter place
- up to 28 days per calendar year and keep your living allowance

Yes, you must always tell a staff member at the shelter before you leave.

If you do not report your departure, you can lose your shelter place immediately and the municipality can stop your living allowance immediately.

Also, if you are away for more than 14 days, the municipality may give your shelter place to someone else. If you are away for more than 28 days, the municipality can stop your living allowance.

So if you want to keep your spot, the safest thing is:
- inform the shelter staff before leaving
- try not to be away more than 14 days if you want to keep your place
- do not stay away more than 28 days if you want to keep your allowance

It may depend somewhat on the municipality how strictly this is enforced.

  - https://voedselbankennederland.nl/vertalingen/english/

user_input: I'm a single adult man with disabilities and I really need a place to stay. Is there any way I can get priority for shelter? I feel lost and don't know what to do.
bot_output:
Yes — you may be able to get priority, because vulnerability is taken into account.

Single adult men are still accepted in the Netherlands under Temporary Protection, but shelter is harder to get due to limited availability. Women, children, and people with medical indications have priority. Your disability may fall under “extra care” or a medical indication, which is considered a vulnerability.

What you should do:
- Report to a municipality and ask for help with registration and shelter.
- Clearly explain your disability and care needs.
- Ask whether support can also be arranged through the municipality under the Wmo (Social Support Act), which provides help for people with disabilities.

Important:
- There is currently a shortage of shelter places, so shelter cannot be guaranteed.
- The Red Cross cannot arrange shelter placement independently; this is done by the municipality.

If you are already registered in a municipality, ask that municipality for a place in municipal reception. If there is no room, the municipality should contact the safety region to look for a place.

user_input: I am Ukrainian and my work is unsafe, I think I am being exploited. Can you tell me which organizations can help me or give legal advice? I feel really lost.
bot_output:
If your work feels unsafe or exploitative, these organizations can help:

- **FairWork**: helps with unsafe work, labour exploitation, human trafficking, back pay, and complaints to the labour inspectorate. Support is **free** and **confidential**, often in your own language.  
  Website: **www.fairwork.nu**

- **Opora**: gives juridical information to displaced persons from Ukraine about work-related issues such as **labour contracts, pension, and child allowance**.  
  Website: **https://www.oporafoundation.nl/**

- **VluchtelingenWerk Nederland**: can help with legal questions and additional advice.  
  Contact page: **https://www.refugeehelp.nl/en/ukrainian-refugee/contact**  
  Email: **oekraine@vluchtelingenwerk.nl**

- **Eerste Rechtshulp**: free legal aid near you.  
  Website: **https://eersterechtshulp.nl/**

If you may be affected by **human trafficking**, these can also help:

- **Fier**: anonymous advice chat in **Dutch or English**. They give information about options and help if you want it.  
  Chat: **https://www.fier.nl/chat/**  
  Open: **Mon–Fri 16:00–06:00, Sat/Sun/holidays 20:00–06:00**

- **Human trafficking care coordinators**: provide targeted advice and guidance.  
  Info: **https://www.comensha.nl/voor-professionals/zorgcoordinator/**

There is also a flyer about labour rights, risks of exploitation, and where to get help:
- **Ukrainian**: https://www.comensha.nl/media/ju4hmw0h/dec2023_nrk_flyer_know_your_rights_oek_oek.pdf

Your information can be kept confidential, and potential victims are entitled to assistance from a lawyer.

If you want, I can also list the **best first step to take right now** based on whether you need urgent safety help, legal advice, or help with your employer.

user_input: I need to leave soon and I'm not sure what to do about my job, school, and bank. Do I have to tell them or do something before I go? Also, I heard about BRP deregistration but I don't really understand it. Can you help me?
bot_output:
Yes. Before you leave the Netherlands, you should do the following, if relevant to your situation:

- deregister from your municipality in the BRP
- inform your employer that you are leaving
- inform your school that you are leaving
- contact your bank about your bank account; some banks require you to close it when you leave
- cancel any insurance policies you have in the Netherlands

About BRP deregistration:
- BRP is the Personal Records Database of the municipality.
- If you leave the Netherlands permanently, you must notify your municipality of your departure and deregister from the BRP.
- You can ask for a bewijs van uitschrijving (proof of deregistration).
- This proof may be needed if you want to apply for temporary protection in another country.
- Deregistration removes your citizen service number from the BRP.
- As a result, you lose entitlement to living allowance, reception centre accommodation, and benefits.
- Child benefit and allowances stop automatically.
- The municipality will inform the IND of your deregistration.

If you have already left:
- you may be able to deregister via the IND, or someone else can do it for you on your behalf.

If you also want to stop an asylum procedure:
- inform the IND that you do not want to continue your asylum application
- sign and send the departure form to the IND:
https://assets.ctfassets.net/496uch1l97fc/7GNmG529ZaVTvU29K3DSKF/96a4ca3306e38fbaedca1a0767cd4a3b/Vertrekformulier_IND.pdf

If you want help returning:
- DT&V (Repatriation and Departure Service) can help arrange your journey to your country of origin or another country outside the EU where you may stay longer.

If you want, I can also give you a simple step-by-step checklist for leaving.

Through MijnOverheid (https://www.netherlandsworldwide.nl/mijnoverheid-abroad/how-to-login), you can check with which details you are registered in the BRP.

user_input: I lost my shelter because I was away for too long. Can I get help to get it back? What do I need to do, and am I still allowed to get benefits? I'm really worried.
bot_output:
Yes — you may be able to get shelter and benefits again, but it depends on your situation.

What you should do:
- Go back to the municipality or municipal reception center where you previously stayed.
- Ask them to assess your situation again.
- If you were deregistered from the BRP, you must register again.

About getting shelter back:
- If you were away for more than 14 days, the municipality may have given your shelter place to someone else.
- If you return later, you can be given another reception location.
- Please note that a request for resettlement may not always be honored.

About benefits:
- If you were away for longer than 28 days, the municipality can stop your living allowance.
- If you left without reporting it, they can stop it immediately.
- If you return to the Netherlands and still meet the rules, you can receive living allowance again.
- If your case is accepted again, you are also entitled again to childcare and other benefits in kind from the ROOO.

Important:
- In general, you may leave:
  - 14 days per calendar year and keep your shelter place
  - 28 days per calendar year and keep your living allowance
- You must always report your departure to shelter staff or the municipality.

If you want, I can also help you write a short message to the municipality or shelter asking for reinstatement.

user_input: I am from Ukraine and I don't know if I can work here. Do I need a permit or can I get a job? Please help, I really need to earn money for food and rent.
bot_output:
If you are covered by the Temporary Protection Directive in the Netherlands, you can work here without a work permit.

What you need:
- You must fall under the Temporary Protection Directive.
- You must have proof of residence from the IND, such as a sticker, card, or O-document.
- You cannot work yet if you only have a BSN and do not have the IND sticker/card yet.

Important:
- If you do not yet have the IND proof document, make an appointment with the IND. Without it, you cannot work.
- For regular employment, your employer does not need to apply for a work permit if you are under temporary protection.
- If you want to work as a freelancer/self-employed person, different rules apply: you are only allowed if you or the contracting party has an employment permit.
- You can also do volunteer work, but the organization must request a volunteer declaration from UWV.
- You can do an internship if you have proof of residence under temporary protection; then the internship provider does not need a work permit.

If you have a paid job and stay in municipal shelter, you may remain there, but you may have to pay a contribution. Starting July 1st 2024, displaced people from Ukraine with income in municipal shelter must help pay for reception, and you will no longer receive a living allowance.

If you want, I can also help you figure out what to do based on your exact situation, for example:
- whether you already have the IND sticker/card,
- whether you are registered in the BRP,
- or whether you want regular work or freelance work.

user_input: Hey, if I have to leave the shelter, do I need to tell someone? What happens if I just go without saying anything? I'm kinda worried about getting in trouble.
bot_output:
Hey — yes, you should tell the shelter staff before you leave.

If you leave, you must report your departure to a reception staff member. If you do not report it, you can lose your shelter place immediately, and the municipality can also stop your living allowance immediately.

In general:
- You can stay away up to 14 days and keep your shelter place.
- You can stay away up to 28 days and keep your living allowance.
- This is for things like holidays, family visits, or a funeral.

So the safest thing is: always inform the shelter staff before leaving.

user_input: I have an EU work visa but I don't know if I can get help here. Can you tell me if I'm eligible for shelter or protection? I'm really confused about the rules.
bot_output:
If you have an EU work visa, it depends on when you got it and which EU country issued it.

- If your work visa was issued before 27 November 2021:
  - If you are a refugee from Ukraine who was working or studying in another EU country before that date, you are not entitled to reception in the Netherlands.
  - You should check whether you are covered in the country that issued your visa.

- If you left Ukraine after 26 November 2021 to work in another EU country and your work visa has expired:
  - You may be entitled to Temporary Protection in the Netherlands.

Important:
- It is necessary to check that it is really a work visa, not a permanent visa.
- If you are eligible for temporary protection in the Netherlands, you keep your right to reception.
- Because shelter places are limited, there is no guarantee a municipality can offer shelter immediately.

If you want, tell me:
1. which country issued the visa,
2. when it was issued,
3. whether it is still valid or expired,
and I can help you understand which rule applies.

user_input: I am undocumented from Ukraine and my kids are minors. How can we get registered together? I feel lost and don't know what to do.
bot_output:
If you do not have documents, you currently cannot register for the BRP.

For children from Ukraine without proof of identification, the children can be registered with their parents at the municipality. In that case, parents can make a statement on oath establishing the identity of the children, and the municipality registers the children together with the parents.

If you have Ukrainian nationality but cannot prove it with documents, you should contact the Ukrainian Embassy in The Hague. They may be able to provide proof of your identity and nationality. The embassy can issue an identifying certificate that can be used to register for the BRP at the municipality.

Ukrainian Embassy:
- Zeestraat 78, 2518 AD The Hague
- Open Monday to Friday, 09:00–13:00
- Phone: +31 (70) 360 72 18
- Email: emb_nl@mfa.gov.ua
- Website: https://netherlands.mfa.gov.ua/en

If you remain in the Netherlands without residency status, you are undocumented. Undocumented persons do not have a right to housing, work or government subsidies. However, you still have the right to necessary medical care, judicial assistance, and children under 18 have the right to attend school.

You can also apply for asylum at any point with undocumented status.

For more information or help, you can contact the Red Cross helpline on WhatsApp:
https://wa.me/31614458781

["Document: What are the steps I should take to register a child travelling alone from Ukraine?  

Unaccompanied minor foreingers are children who are under the age of 18 when they arrive in the Netherlands, are under the age of 18 when they arrive in the Netherlands and came without their parents.   

Firstly, unaccompanied Ukrainian children should always be registered with the municipality (like all other refugees from Ukraine) so that they are inculded in the Basic Registration Persons (BRP) and do not get out of sight.  

When the municipality determines that a minor is unaccompanied, Nidos should be contacted immediately.

Then, Nidos does an intake with the minor, and if possible, remotely with parents.

Nidos assesses whether applying for temporary guardianship is appropriate.

The municipality can report the minor to Nidos via 088-5011885 or oekraine@nidos.nl.

When you have the Ukrainian nationality but cannot prove this with documents (ID or passport), you should contact the Ukrainian embassy in The Hague.

They may be able to get proof of your identity and nationality.

The embassy can issue an identifying certificate that can be used to register for the BRP at the municpality.   Children from Ukraine without proof of identification can be registered with their parents at the municipality.

In the absence of documents, parents can make a statement on oath establishing the identity of the children.

user_input: My host won't let me register and I'm scared I might lose protection. What can I do to stay safe? Are there other options for shelter?
bot_output:
I’m sorry you’re dealing with this.

It is very important to be registered at an address in the Netherlands. If you are not registered, you cannot get Temporary Protection. If you had Temporary Protection before and later deregistered, you can lose that status because it may look like you left the country.

What you can do:
- If your host will not let you register, it is best to go to a municipality shelter or find other housing where you can register.
- Try to check how long you can still stay with your host so you do not end up without a place to sleep.
- If you do not feel safe at your host family, you can go to an emergency shelter of the municipality.
- If you are in immediate danger, call 112.
- You can also contact Veilig Thuis (Safe at Home) at 0800-2000.
- If domestic or relationship violence is involved, you can call the crisis shelter “Blijf van mijn Lijf-huis” for free at 0800 0117.

Other shelter options:
- Municipalities can help register displaced Ukrainians and help find housing.
- If you are covered by Temporary Protection, you keep your right to reception. First contact the municipality where you are registered and ask for a place in municipal reception.
- If there is no room, the municipality contacts the safety region, and if needed, a request can be made for relocation.
- You can also try to find another host family through your own network or local initiatives. If you move, it is important to register the new address in the BRP.

If you want, tell me your location and I can help you look for a nearby registration point.

user_input: I am a Ukrainian refugee and I don't have insurance. How can I see a doctor or get help if I have an emergency? I'm really worried because I feel sick and don't know what to do.
bot_output:
I’m sorry you’re feeling sick. You have the right to see a doctor and get necessary medical care in the Netherlands.

If you are a displaced person from Ukraine:
- Basic healthcare and urgent medical care are covered.
- If you have a BSN, you fall under the RMO scheme.
- You do not have to pay insurance premium or eigen risico under this scheme.
- Even if you are uninsured, you can still get medical help. This can be reimbursed through a special subsidy.

What to do:
- During working hours: go to a General Practitioner (GP) first. Only a GP can refer you to a specialist or hospital.
- If you are staying with a host family: first ask whether you can go to your host’s GP.
- If you are in an emergency shelter: contact the medical facilities there. The shelter usually knows what care is available.
- If you need to find a GP yourself, you can ask your municipality, or check:
  - https://www.kiesuwhuisarts.nl/
  - https://www.zorgkaartnederland.nl/huisarts?zoekterm=huisarts

If it is evening/night or urgent:
- You can call 112 in an emergency.
- You can also go to the huisartsenpost.
- In an emergency, you can also go to the Emergency Room in the nearest hospital.

If a GP says they cannot help because you are uninsured, they can check this CAK website about reimbursement for uninsured care:
- https://www.hetcak.nl/zakelijk/regelingen/regeling-onverzekerden/subsidie-aanvragen/aanvraag

If you tell me:
1. your city or postcode, and
2. whether this is an emergency right now,
I can help you look for the best next step.

user_input: I have a BSN from RNI registration, but I'm not sure if that's enough for proof of residence under the Temporary Protection Directive. Do I need to be registered in the BRP? I'm really confused and worried about my situation.
bot_output:
Yes — if your BSN came from an **RNI registration**, that is **not enough** for proof of residence under the Temporary Protection Directive.

You **need to be registered in the BRP** in your municipality to get a **valid BSN** for applying for proof of residence.

Important points:
- **RNI** is for people staying in the Netherlands for **less than 4 months**
- A **BSN from RNI is not valid** for proof of residence under the Temporary Protection Directive
- To apply for proof of residence, you must **register as a resident in the BRP**
- After BRP registration, you can make an appointment with the **IND** to collect your proof of residence

You also **cannot work with only a BSN** if you do not yet have the IND proof of residence sticker/card.

So in short: **yes, you need BRP registration**.

If you want, I can also explain the **next steps after BRP registration**.
context:
["Document: What is the difference between a RNI registration and a BRP registration?  

The Non-residents Records Database (RNI) is a part of the Personal Records Database (BRP).

It is a register of people who do not live in the Netherlands, no longer live in the Netherlands or live in the Netherlands for less than 4 months.

For example migrant / seasonal workers register in the RNI.   

If you are registered in the RNI, you will receive a BSN number.

Please note: this BSN number is not valid for receiving a Proof of Residency under the Temporary Protection Directive.

In order to obtain a valid BSN number for applying for a proof of residence, you must register in the BRP in your municipality (see subcategory 'Registration' for more information).  

For most recent information see:  https://www.nederlandwereldwijd.nl/rni/wat-is-rni  https://www.rvig.nl/basisregistratie-personen https://ind.nl/nl/oekraine/richtlijn-tijdelijke-bescherming-oekraine#bewijs-van-verblijf-", "Document: Can I get proof of residence if I have a BSN number that I got with a RNI registration?

No, this is not possible.

An RNI registration is for people who stay in the Netherlands for less than 4 months (e.g. migrant / seasonal workers).

The BSN number that belongs with the RNI registration is not valid for proof of residence under the Temporary Protection Directive.

In order to obtain a valid BSN number for applying for a proof of residence, you must register in the BRP in your municipality (see subcategory 'Registration' for more information).  

For the most recent information see: https://www.nederlandwereldwijd.nl/rni/wat-is-rni  https://www.rvig.nl/basisregistratie-personen https://ind.nl/en/ukraine/temporary-protection-directive-ukraine", "Document: I have temporary protection in one EU country but want to move to another for a job.

The new country refuses to register me since I’m already registered elsewhere.

What can I do?          

You are free to choose the EU country in which you enjoy temporary protection.

However, you can benefit from temporary protection only in one EU Member State at a time.

The rights connected to temporary protection are the same in every EU country bound by the Directive.  

If you have registered in one country and decide to move to another, you need to inform the authorities of the country in which you are currently registered.

The country where you move will then register you and offer you the temporary protection status and subsequent rights.   

Please note that if you had a temporary work visa for the Netherlands and are registered in the RNI, you will receive a BSN number.

Please note: this BSN number is not valid for receiving a Proof of Residency under the Temporary Protection Directive.", "Document: In order to obtain a valid BSN number for applying for a proof of residence, you must register in the BRP in your municipality   For more information see: https://eu-solidarity-ukraine.ec.europa.eu/information-people-fleeing-war-ukraine/fleeing-ukraine-your-rights-eu_en", "Document: What can I do and which support can I get after I register for the Basic Registration of Persons (BRP)?

After you register for BRP you have to make an appointment with the IND to collect your proof of residency, which is a sticker in your passport.

You have to make this appointment within 4 weeks after you got registered?

Only after you got this sticker you can get living allowance and you are allowed to work and live in the Netherlands.

For more information on how to make an appointment you can check the subcategorie "proof of residency".  

For the most recent information, see: https://ind.nl/en/ukraine/temporary-protection-directive-ukraine", "Document: What is a proof of residency?

If you fall under the Temporary Protection Directive and are registered in the BRP, you can obtain a certificate from the IND that you are allowed to live and work in the Netherlands.

This certificate is a sticker in your passport or on a separate piece of paper.

Sometimes you will be given a card.

Applying for residency under the directive is free of charge!!   

The sticker or card is valid from 4 March 2022 to 4 March 2027.

Your sticker or card is only valid in the Netherlands.

Are you applying for protection in another EU country?

Then your protection stops in the Netherlands.  

For the most recent information see:  - [IND](https://ind.nl/en/ukraine-appointment-to-collect-proof-of-residency)  - [IND](https://ind.nl/en/ukraine/temporary-protection-directive-ukraine) -

[RefugeeHelp](https://www.refugeehelp.nl/nl/ukrainian-refugee/article/100040-dit-moet-je-doen-als-je-tijdelijke-bescherming-hebt)", "Document: How can I register for Basic Registration of Persons (BRP)?  

You can register for the Basic Registration of Persons (BRP) at the municipality you are staying.   

When you register for the BRP at the municipality, your registration is automatically referred to the Immigration & Naturalization Service (IND).

The IND is responsible for the process that establishes your temporary protected status.

Refugees from Ukraine that are registered at the IND will receive temporary protection and are allowed to stay at least until 4 March 2027.

This might be extended to a maximum of 3 years.  

After registering with the municipality, you will receive a citizen service number (BSN).

You will need this number for health care, education, work and financial matters (for example, opening a bank account).

When you received your BSN, you can apply for a DigiD.

You can use this to access online government services.", "Document: Can I work in the Netherlands?

In order to live and work in The Netherlands, any person needs one of many Dutch residence permits.

As in the majority of other different countries, a person cannot simply arrive in a country and start working legally.

There are always regulations, which are country-dependent.  

The Temporary Protection Directive is one such temporary residence permit allowing people from Ukraine to live and work in The Netherlands.

The “sticker” (or paper, or O-document) is only the confirmation of the fact that a person applied and was granted temporary protection in The Netherlands.

You can apply for temporary protection in The Netherlands under certain conditions, which you can find here: https://www.refugeehelp.nl/en/ukrainian-refugee/article/100187-conditions-of-temporary-protection-directive   Important: you can work only after receiving the so-called “sticker”.

You cannot work if you have only your BSN number but do not have the “sticker” yet.

You should be registered as a “resident” in the BRP to qualify for temporary protection in The Netherlands.", "Document: Can I register for the Basic Registration of Persons (BRP) when I do not have documents?  

Without documents you can currently not register for the BRP.   

When you have the Ukrainian nationality but cannot prove this with documents (ID or passport), you should contact the Ukrainian embassy in The Hague.

They may be able to get proof of your identity and nationality.

The embassy can issue an identifying certificate that can be used to register for the BRP at the municpality.   Children from Ukraine without proof of identification can be registered with their parents at the municipality.

In the absence of documents, parents can make a statement on oath establishing the identity of the children.

The children are then registered by the municipality together with the parents.   

Address Ukrainian Embassy:  Zeestraat 78, 2518 AD The Hague  Open from Monday to Friday between 09:00 and 13:00 Telephone: +31 (70) 360 72 18  Email: emb_nl@mfa.gov.ua.

https://netherlands.mfa.gov.ua/en   

For the most recent information see: https://ind.nl/en/ukraine/temporary-protection-directive-ukraine", "Document: Can I register for the Basic Registration of Persons (BRP) when I fled from Ukraine but I have another nationality?  

This depends on whether you have a permanent residence permit.

Only displaced persons from Ukraine who are covered by the Temporary Protection Directive can register with the BRP.

As of July 19, non-Ukrainians with a temporary residence permit for Ukraine can no longer apply for temporary protection.

This means that if you have a temporary residence permit, you cannot register with the BRP.   

For the most recent information see: https://ind.nl/en/ukraine/temporary-protection-directive-ukraine", "Document: Why do I get a proof of residency and not a residence permit?  

You are given a proof of residency because the Temporary Protection Directive applies to you.

This means that you may stay in the Netherlands with your certificate of residence for the duration of the protection measure.

This is currently until 4 March 2027.

This can be extended to a maximum of three years.

You may live and work in the Netherlands with your proof of residence.  

The IND will not decide on your application for asylum as long as the Temporary Protection Directive applies to you.

Because they do not make a decision, you will not be given a residence permit.

When the Temporary Protection Directive ends, you can choose to continue your application for asylum.  

For the most recent information see: https://ind.nl/en/ukraine/temporary-protection-directive-ukraine", "Document: How can I apply for and collect a proof of residency?

To collect your proof of residency: - make an appointment at this IND pickup location: [Atoomweg 100, Utrecht](https://ind.nl/nl/oekraine/oekraine-afspraak-bewijs-van-verblijf).

You need a BSN, which you receive after registering at a municipality in the Netherlands.

Make sure you are registered at your municipality for at least 1 week on the day you collect your proof of residency.  

- Make an appointment for up to 6 family members, for example, for your partner and children.

Children under 14 will not receive proof of residency, as they fall under the directive if a parent falls under the directive.

Please bring your children to the pickup location as well.

- Collect the proof of residency yourself.

Children under 18 years are required to collect their document together with a parent or legal representative.

Are you unable to come to the appointment yourself?

Then you have to authorize someone who can collect the proof of residency for you.

You can fill in [this form](https://ind.nl/en/forms/7645.pdf) to authorize someone.", "Document: How does the appointment to collect my proof of residency work and what do I have to fill in?  

At the pickup location, an IND staff member will check:  - your registration with the local council/municipality - your appointment code - your documents - whether you fall under the Temporary Protection Directive.  

You must fill in 2 IND forms during your appointment.

At the reception location you will find a translation of both forms into Ukrainian, Russian and English.

There are also employees who can help you fill in these forms.

They speak Ukrainian, Russian or English.   

Form 1: Asylum application (applicable for age => 15): The official asylum application (minors – together with parents on the form).  

Form 2: Antecedents certificate (applicable for age => 12): On this certificate, you state whether you have ever committed a punishable offence or crime.   

Because you are covered by the Temporary Protection Directive, your rights will be different to those of the standard asylum application.

You can work in the Netherlands immediately.

The IND will not assess your application for asylum while the directive is in force.

The directive will apply at least until 4 March 2027.", "Document: Extension of proof of residency Do you have a sticker or card valid until 4 March 2023, 2024, or 2025?

Then you should have received a single extension letter from the IND, which keeps your sticker or card valid until the end of the Temporary Protection Directive.

For example, if you got the letter in January 2023, it’s still valid.

If your document is valid until 4 March 2025 but you haven’t received the letter, it may still be on the way.

You can also give the IND a call: https://ind.nl/en/service-contact/contact-with-ind  The combination of your sticker/card with the letter is enough to show you are allowed to live and work in the Netherlands after 4 March 2023.  

For more information see [here](https://ind.nl/en/ukraine/extension-sticker-or-card-temporary-protection-ukraine)", "Document: Flyers about Proof of Residency Download the flyer 'Residence in The Netherlands: what does it mean for you?'

in English, Ukranian, Russian and Arabic:  English: https://ind.nl/en/documents/06-2022-o-document-engels0.pdf  Ukranian: https://ind.nl/en/documents/06-2022-o-document-oekraiens0.pdf  Russian: https://ind.nl/en/documents/06-2022-o-document-russisch0.pdf  Arabic: https://ind.nl/en/documents/06-2022-o-document-arabisch0.pdf", "Document: Action steps (including pick up proof of residence)

There are two important action steps you have to take:  - From 6 May, pick up a residence sticker from the IND to prove your right to stay and work in the Netherlands.

The IND will send you a letter with details.

Check 'Proof of Residency' on https://ind.nl/en/ukraine/residency-non-ukrainians-with-temporary-ukrainian-residence-permit.  - Consider exploring other options for obtaining a residence permit in the Netherlands, even as you wait for the European court's decision.

Check https://www.refugeehelp.nl/en/ukrainian-refugee/article/100189-these-are-your-options-if-you-are-not-entitled-to-temporary-protection for more information", "Document: If you register as a “non-resident” in RNI, you are not qualified for temporary protection in The Netherlands.

You can read more about the conditions for working in The Netherlands here: https://www.refugeehelp.nl/en/ukrainian-refugee/article/100149-conditions-for-working-in-the-netherlands   Please note: the Red Cross cannot issue the “sticker” or any other documents for that matter.

This is done exclusively by IND.", "Document: I previously had temporary protection in the Netherlands but left for a non-EU country (e.g., Canada).

Can I get temporary protection again if I return?          

You may regain temporary protection, but this depends on your situation.

The IND will reassess your eligibility.

In case of temporary departure (maximum 28 days) the advice is therefore always to report this to the shelter/municipality.", "Document: Can I change temporary protection in another EU country to temporary protection in the Netherlands?

Yes you can.

Please note that you can only fall under the temporary protection directive in one EU country.

People can live and work legally only in the country that granted temporary protection.

People still have a right to travel as tourists within EU under “90 days” rule.   

According to the IND, you do not need to deregister in the country where you currently have temporary protection.

That way, if your request for temporary protection in the Netherlands is denied, you will still have temporary protection elsewhere.

The IND should not object if someone falls under temporary protection elsewhere.

Eventually, the country that you're leaving will be able to see in a temporary protection platform that you have also been granted temporary protection in the Netherlands and then they can terminate the temporary protection.   

You can find more information about the temporary protection directive in the EU

[here](https://home-affairs.ec.europa.eu/policies/migration-and-asylum/asylum-eu/temporary-protection_en)

(in EN, UKR, RU, NL).", "Document: What if I'm an EU migrant?

If you hold the nationality of an EU member state, you have lawful residence in the Netherlands, but under a different policy than with the temporary protection.

You can find more information here: https://ind.nl/en/residence-permits/eu-eea-or-swiss-citizens/registering-with-the-ind-as-an-eu-eea-or-swiss-citizen", "Document: What is the Temporary Protection Directive?

The Temporary Protection Directive entitles you to reception, health care, and education for minor children in the Netherlands.

As well as the possibility to work.

If you are covered by the directive, you may stay in the Netherlands until at least 4 March 2027.

For the most recent information see: - https://ind.nl/en/ukraine/temporary-protection-directive-ukraine - https://www.government.nl/topics/reception-of-refugees-from-ukraine/third-country-nationals", "Document: Can I work in The Netherlands?  

Everyone who comes under the Temporary Protection Directive can work in the Netherlands without a work permit (in Dutch: tewerkstellingsvergunning or twv).

This means that an employer does not have to request a work permit for you.

And that you can easily look for a job, if you want to.

We advise you to register at the local council if you come under the directive.  

- You have proof of residency showing that you are allowed to be in the Netherlands.

The requirements for the exemption also apply if want to work as a volunteer.

The organisation where you want to work must then request a volunteer declaration from the UWV.

You may also work as a trainee, when you, your employer and your school have signed a trainee contract.

A twv is required if you want to work as a self-employed person.", "Document: Important: Temporary Protection for third-country nationals stops per September 4, 2025.   

Important: refugees with a temporary residence permit for Ukraine (third-country nationals) have to leave the Netherlands as of September 4, 2025  Up until now, there has been a freeze on the end of Temporary Protection for third-country nationals.

This freeze ends on September 5, 2024, meaning that third-country nationals must leave the country after this.

See more about these rights under “What are my rights as a third-country national”.   

After September 4, 2024, third-country nationals will have four weeks to leave the Netherlands voluntarily.

During those weeks, they will still have the right to shelter, but the right to work and access education will end on September 4.   

To whom the freeze applies: - Your temporary protection ended on 5 March 2024. 

- You are registered with the municipality in the Personal Records Database (BRP).  

Have you been deregistered from the BRP after 4 March 2024?", "Document: When will I be covered by the Temporary Protection Directive?

You will be covered by the directive in the Netherlands if one of the following situations applies to you:  

You have the Ukrainian nationality and:  - You left Ukraine after 26 November 2021.

- You left Ukraine before 27 November 2021 and at that time you had been in the Netherlands for a longer period of time.

For example, because you had a residence permit or had applied for asylum.

You can prove that you were in the Netherlands before 27 November 2021 and not in another EU country.  

You do not have Ukrainian nationality and:  - On 23 February 2022, you had international protection in Ukraine, for example as a recognised refugee.

Or you had some other form of temporary (national) protection, because you are not safe in your country of origin.  

- On 23 February 2022, you had a valid permanent Ukrainian residence permit.

You left Ukraine after 26 November 2021.

And you did not return to your country of origin after 23 February 2022.", "Document: Abroad  General advise If you’re coming to the Netherlands with a Ukrainian passport/valid permanent Ukrainian residence permit and proof you left Ukraine after November 26, 2021, you have a right to Shelter & Temporary Protection.

user_input: I just found out I have TB and I'm really scared. Who can I talk to for help and what should I do next? I don't have papers and I'm worried they won't help me.
bot_output:
I’m sorry you’re going through this. You have the right to necessary medical care, even if you do not have papers.

What to do next:
- Contact a General Practitioner (GP), or
- Contact the tuberculosis control department of the Municipal Public Health Services (GGD) directly.

What will happen:
- Specialist doctors and nurses will screen you for tuberculosis.
- If you have tuberculosis, you will be prescribed medication.
- Nurses at the GGD will help you take the medication correctly.

If you are undocumented:
- Undocumented persons still have the right to necessary medical care.

More information:
- https://www.rivm.nl/node/200571

If you want, I can also help explain how to find a GP during working hours.

user_input: I have temporary protection in another EU country but I want to work here. How do I register or transfer my papers? I really need help with this, I'm confused.
bot_output:
If you have temporary protection in another EU country and want to work in the Netherlands, you can change the country that grants your temporary protection.

Key points:
- You can only have temporary protection in one EU country at a time.
- You can live and work legally only in the country that granted you temporary protection.
- You may still travel within the EU as a tourist under the 90-days rule.

What to do if you want to move your temporary protection to the Netherlands:
1. First check whether you are eligible for temporary protection in the Netherlands.
2. If you are eligible, you can apply in the Netherlands.
3. According to the IND, you do not need to deregister first in the country where you currently have temporary protection. If the Netherlands refuses your request, you would still have protection in the other country.
4. After the Netherlands grants you temporary protection, the other country can see this and terminate your previous temporary protection.

To register in the Netherlands:
- You must register in the BRP at the municipality where you are staying.
- Your BRP registration is automatically shared with the IND.
- After registration, you receive a BSN.
- Then the IND handles the process for temporary protection.

Important:
- To work in the Netherlands, you need proof of residency from the IND: a sticker, paper, or card.
- You cannot work with only a BSN number.
- If you are registered only as a non-resident in the RNI, that is not enough for temporary protection in the Netherlands.

If your current country refuses to let you transfer:
- You should inform the authorities in the country where you are currently registered that you want to move.
- The new country should then register you and offer temporary protection if you meet the requirements.

It is always best to contact the IND directly or an immigration lawyer for case-specific advice.

More information:
- https://ind.nl/en/ukraine/temporary-protection-directive-ukraine
- https://home-affairs.ec.europa.eu/policies/migration-and-asylum/asylum-eu/temporary-protection_en

If you want, I can also help you step by step with what to do first in the Netherlands.

- You need to be registered in the BRP to be covered by Temporary Protection.
- After BRP registration, you must make an appointment with the IND within 4 weeks to get a residence sticker.

If you are Ukrainian but cannot prove it with documents, you should contact the Ukrainian embassy in The Hague. They may be able to issue an identifying certificate that can be used to register for the BRP.

If you remain undocumented, the documents say you still have the right to:
- necessary medical care
- judicial assistance
- school for children under 18

You can also apply for asylum at any point while undocumented.

For more help, the documents mention:
- Red Cross WhatsApp helpline: https://wa.me/31614458781
- Red Cross information site: https://helpfulinformation.redcross.nl/

If you want, I can also help you figure out the next best step based on whether you have Ukrainian nationality, a residence permit from Ukraine, or no documents.

https://www.government.nl/topics/registering-a-birth-and-name-of-child/rules-for-registering-a-birth

If you want, I can also help you with what to do next after BRP registration.
context:
["Document: Can I register my newborn baby for the Basic Registration of Persons (BRP)?

Yes you can.

Within three days after the birth of a child, you have to report this to the municipality.

After registration you will receive a birth certificate.  

For the most recent information see: https://www.government.nl/topics/registering-a-birth-and-name-of-child/rules-for-registering-a-birth", "Document: How can I register for Basic Registration of Persons (BRP)?  

You can register for the Basic Registration of Persons (BRP) at the municipality you are staying.   

When you register for the BRP at the municipality, your registration is automatically referred to the Immigration & Naturalization Service (IND).

The IND is responsible for the process that establishes your temporary protected status.

Refugees from Ukraine that are registered at the IND will receive temporary protection and are allowed to stay at least until 4 March 2027.

This might be extended to a maximum of 3 years.  

After registering with the municipality, you will receive a citizen service number (BSN).

You will need this number for health care, education, work and financial matters (for example, opening a bank account).

When you received your BSN, you can apply for a DigiD.

You can use this to access online government services.", "Document: Can I register for the Basic Registration of Persons (BRP) when I do not have documents?  

Without documents you can currently not register for the BRP.   

When you have the Ukrainian nationality but cannot prove this with documents (ID or passport), you should contact the Ukrainian embassy in The Hague.

They may be able to get proof of your identity and nationality.

The embassy can issue an identifying certificate that can be used to register for the BRP at the municpality.   Children from Ukraine without proof of identification can be registered with their parents at the municipality.

In the absence of documents, parents can make a statement on oath establishing the identity of the children.

The children are then registered by the municipality together with the parents.   

Address Ukrainian Embassy:  Zeestraat 78, 2518 AD The Hague  Open from Monday to Friday between 09:00 and 13:00 Telephone: +31 (70) 360 72 18  Email: emb_nl@mfa.gov.ua.

https://netherlands.mfa.gov.ua/en   

For the most recent information see: https://ind.nl/en/ukraine/temporary-protection-directive-ukraine", "Document: My host family/friends/family where I am staying does not allow me to register myself, what should I do?  

It is very important to be registered at an adress in the Netherlands.

If you are not registered, you cannot get Temporary Protection.

If you registered on an adress before, got the Temporary Protection but deregistered lateron, you can lose the Temporary Protection status because it seems you left the country.

Also social benefits are connected to your adress.  

Hosts can register refugees from Ukraine without for example losing their social benefits.

Maybe your hosts are afraid it has negative effects on their own financial situation, but this is often not the case.   

If the host won't register the PA, it is best to refer the PA to a municipality shelter or advise them to find other housing where they can register.  

Always check with the PA how long he/she can still stay with the host family/friends/relatives and make sure PA won't be on the street.

If you think this is the case, refer the case to the TC.   

You can check if there is an organization in the town that you stay in that can give free legal advice about this issue (see category 'Administrative').", "Document: What are the steps I should take to register a child travelling alone from Ukraine?  

Unaccompanied minor foreingers are children who are under the age of 18 when they arrive in the Netherlands, are under the age of 18 when they arrive in the Netherlands and came without their parents.   

Firstly, unaccompanied Ukrainian children should always be registered with the municipality (like all other refugees from Ukraine) so that they are inculded in the Basic Registration Persons (BRP) and do not get out of sight.  

When the municipality determines that a minor is unaccompanied, Nidos should be contacted immediately.

Then, Nidos does an intake with the minor, and if possible, remotely with parents.

Nidos assesses whether applying for temporary guardianship is appropriate.

The municipality can report the minor to Nidos via 088-5011885 or oekraine@nidos.nl.  

For all children, shelter must be arranged in the Netherlands.

Nidos is responsible for the shelter of unaccompanied minors.

Nidos arranges shelter in host families, preferably with the same cultural background.", "Document: What can I do and which support can I get after I register for the Basic Registration of Persons (BRP)?

After you register for BRP you have to make an appointment with the IND to collect your proof of residency, which is a sticker in your passport.

You have to make this appointment within 4 weeks after you got registered?

Only after you got this sticker you can get living allowance and you are allowed to work and live in the Netherlands.

For more information on how to make an appointment you can check the subcategorie "proof of residency".  

For the most recent information, see: https://ind.nl/en/ukraine/temporary-protection-directive-ukraine", "Document: Another host shelter You can look for a new host family.

You can do this through your social network or through various local initiatives.

It is important that you register in the Basic Registration of Persons (BRP) of the new municipality, or report the new address to the BRP if you stay in the same municipality.", "Document: You can use this to access online government services.   

For a step by step guide of what you should do if you have Temporary Protection, see: https://www.refugeehelp.nl/en/ukrainian-refugee/article/100040-this-is-what-you-should-do-if-you-have-temporary-protection  Please note: if you are staying in a municipal shelter, the municipality will contact you.

If you stay with people and want to register at this municipality, you need to register yourself.

In most cities this can be done at the city hall, but please check the website of your municpality.", "Document: Can I register for the Basic Registration of Persons (BRP) when I fled from Ukraine but I have another nationality?  

This depends on whether you have a permanent residence permit.

Only displaced persons from Ukraine who are covered by the Temporary Protection Directive can register with the BRP.

As of July 19, non-Ukrainians with a temporary residence permit for Ukraine can no longer apply for temporary protection.

This means that if you have a temporary residence permit, you cannot register with the BRP.   

For the most recent information see: https://ind.nl/en/ukraine/temporary-protection-directive-ukraine", "Document: I have temporary protection in one EU country but want to move to another for a job.

The new country refuses to register me since I’m already registered elsewhere.

What can I do?          

You are free to choose the EU country in which you enjoy temporary protection.

However, you can benefit from temporary protection only in one EU Member State at a time.

The rights connected to temporary protection are the same in every EU country bound by the Directive.  

If you have registered in one country and decide to move to another, you need to inform the authorities of the country in which you are currently registered.

The country where you move will then register you and offer you the temporary protection status and subsequent rights.   

Please note that if you had a temporary work visa for the Netherlands and are registered in the RNI, you will receive a BSN number.

Please note: this BSN number is not valid for receiving a Proof of Residency under the Temporary Protection Directive.", "Document: In order to obtain a valid BSN number for applying for a proof of residence, you must register in the BRP in your municipality   For more information see: https://eu-solidarity-ukraine.ec.europa.eu/information-people-fleeing-war-ukraine/fleeing-ukraine-your-rights-eu_en", "Document: How can I apply for and collect a proof of residency?

To collect your proof of residency: - make an appointment at this IND pickup location: [Atoomweg 100, Utrecht](https://ind.nl/nl/oekraine/oekraine-afspraak-bewijs-van-verblijf).

You need a BSN, which you receive after registering at a municipality in the Netherlands.

Make sure you are registered at your municipality for at least 1 week on the day you collect your proof of residency.  

- Make an appointment for up to 6 family members, for example, for your partner and children.

Children under 14 will not receive proof of residency, as they fall under the directive if a parent falls under the directive.

Please bring your children to the pickup location as well.

- Collect the proof of residency yourself.

Children under 18 years are required to collect their document together with a parent or legal representative.

Are you unable to come to the appointment yourself?

Then you have to authorize someone who can collect the proof of residency for you.

You can fill in [this form](https://ind.nl/en/forms/7645.pdf) to authorize someone.", "Document: Who is responsible for the shelter of children travelling alone from Ukraine?

Children travelling alone from Ukraine also have to go to the municipality to get Temporary Protection.

They always have to get shelter right away.

The municipality has to call with Nidos.

Nidos then conducts an intake with the minor—and, where possible, remotely with the parents—to determine whether applying for temporary guardianship is appropriate.   

See for the most recent information:  https://www.nidos.nl/oekraine/  https://www.unicef.nl/ons-werk/noodhulp/oekraine/onbegeleide-kinderen-uit-oekraine", "Document: I am refused at the HSP, where should I go now?  

You are requested to travel to Ter Apel.

Here you will find the Immigration and Naturalisation Service (IND) application centre, where you will go through an indentification and registration process.

Thereafter you will be directed to a reception centre for accommodation while your application is processed.    

For most recent information see: https://www.government.nl/topics/asylum-policy/question-and-answer/what-can-asylum-seekers-expect-in-the-netherlands", "Document: Visualization of Registration procedure  for refugees from Ukraine Here you can find a visualisation of the (offical) steps that displaced persons from Ukraine have to take after arrival in the Netherlands.  

[In Ukrainian](https://www.rijksoverheid.nl/binaries/rijksoverheid/documenten/brochures/2024/06/14/infographic-aanmeldprocedure-voor-vluchtelingen-uit-oekraine/Infographic+Aanmeldprocedure+Vluchtelingen+Oekraiens-2025.pdf)

[In English](https://www.rijksoverheid.nl/binaries/rijksoverheid/documenten/brochures/2024/06/14/infographic-aanmeldprocedure-voor-vluchtelingen-uit-oekraine/Infographic+Aanmeldprocedure+Vluchtelingen+Engels-2025.pdf)", "Document: How does the appointment to collect my proof of residency work and what do I have to fill in?  

At the pickup location, an IND staff member will check:  - your registration with the local council/municipality - your appointment code - your documents - whether you fall under the Temporary Protection Directive.  

You must fill in 2 IND forms during your appointment.

At the reception location you will find a translation of both forms into Ukrainian, Russian and English.

There are also employees who can help you fill in these forms.

They speak Ukrainian, Russian or English.   

Form 1: Asylum application (applicable for age => 15): The official asylum application (minors – together with parents on the form).  

Form 2: Antecedents certificate (applicable for age => 12): On this certificate, you state whether you have ever committed a punishable offence or crime.   

Because you are covered by the Temporary Protection Directive, your rights will be different to those of the standard asylum application.

You can work in the Netherlands immediately.

The IND will not assess your application for asylum while the directive is in force.

The directive will apply at least until 4 March 2027.", "Document: I have a non-biometrical passport.

Is this accepted at the transition locations (HUB)?  

Yes, if it is a non-biometric Ukrainian ID this should be accepted at the transition locations (HUB).   

For most recent information see: https://ind.nl/nl/oekraine/richtlijn-tijdelijke-bescherming-oekraine   https://www.government.nl/topics/reception-of-refugees-from-ukraine/arrival-registration-and-stay", "Document: I have an unintented or unwanted pregnancy, what can I do?  

You can go to Fiom, they offer specialist help with unintended or unwanted pregnancies.

They not only provide you with information on their website, but also offer online counselling, or you can make an appointment for a personal consultation.   

https://fiom.nl/  Telephone: +31 88 126 4900 Email: oz@fiom.nl.  

For most recent information see: https://www.refugeehelp.nl/en/ukrainian-refugee/article/100099-pregnancy", "Document: Where can I check my details in the BRP?

Through MijnOverheid (https://www.netherlandsworldwide.nl/mijnoverheid-abroad/how-to-login), you can check with which details you are registered in the BRP.

You can log in with your DigiD. After logging in, click on Identity.

Then click on your personal details.

Do you not have a DigiD?

Then you can apply for a DigiD (https://www.netherlandsworldwide.nl/digid-abroad/how-to-apply).   

Can't do it online?

If you live in the Netherlands, you can contact the municipality where you live.  

Are your details not correct?

Please contact the municipality where you live.  

For most recent information, see: https://www.netherlandsworldwide.nl/personal-records-database-brp/what-data", "Document: Return to Ukraine or country of origin If you choose to return to Ukraine permanently, you will be referred to Return and Departure Service (DT&V).

If you do not have Ukrainian nationality and wish to return to your country of origin, you are advised to contact International Organization for Migration (IOM).

When you leave the Netherlands, you must deregister from the municipality.

You are also requested to inform the IND of your departure in order to withdraw the Temporary Protection procedure.   

For most recent information see:  IND: https://ind.nl/nl/oekraine/naar-nederland-komen-en-opvang#hulp-bij-terugkeer-  IOM: https://iom-nederland.nl/en/voluntary-return/support-to-refugees-from-ukraine"]

user_input: I don't have any ID or insurance and I need help with sexual health stuff. Is there anywhere I can go for free and it's confidential? I'm really worried.
bot_output:

- **No ID / BSN / health insurance needed**

- **No referral from a doctor is needed**
- **Appointment required** by phone or website

**Contact**
- Website: https://afspraak.ggdaphrodite.nl/?lang=en
- Phone: **(020) 555 5822**
- Address: **Nieuwe Achtergracht 100, 1018 WT Amsterdam** (near Weesperplein metro station)
