context:
["Document: I want advice about sexual health / STI / contraception / pregnancy, where can I go?

There are different websites that provide al lot of information about these topics.  -

At [soaaids.nl](https://www.soaaids.nl/en) you can find information about sexual health, HIV and STIs. -

[Sense.info](https://sense.info/en) answers all your questions about sex – especially if you are between the ages of 12 and 25, this site may be useful for you to check out.

- [Centrum Sexueel Geweld (sexual assault centre)](https://centrumseksueelgeweld.nl/en/) offers professional help to anyone who has experienced an unpleasant sexual experience - online or offline.

It does not matter whether it happened a short or long time ago.", "Document: GGD Center for Sexual Health in Amsterdam You can talk to the GGD about every topic concerning your body, your relations and sex.

They can provide care regarding your sexual health, sexual orientation, gender issues,  sexwork or sexual violence.

Come in to talk about ways to protect yourself with  PEP/PrEP, contraception and vaccinations.

This is a LHBT-friendly centre.

You don't need  ID / BSN / health-insurance.  

You have to call or use the website link to make an appointment.   

Everyone is welcome, the care is free of charge.

You do not need a referral by a doctor.   

All healthcare workers have professional secrecy.  

https://afspraak.ggdaphrodite.nl/?lang=en   Phone: (020) 555 5822  Address: GGD Amsterdam Centrum voor Seksuele Gezondheid Nieuwe Achtergracht 100 1018 WT Amsterdam (near Weesperplein metro station)", "Document: My child needs a vaccine, where can I go?  

The vaccinations of the National Vaccination Programme for children are free.

These vaccinations can be obtained from the child health care centre, the GGD or other youth care institutions in your area.

The Dutch government is taking measures to increase the number of vaccinated people.   

A national overview of JGZ locations can be found on Zorgkaart Nederland: https://www.zorgkaartnederland.nl/jeugdgezondheidszorg", "Document: It does not matter whether it happened a short or long time ago.  

If you need to get tested on a STD, you can do a free test - You can do this at the GGD, check the nearest GGD Soapoli in your region - You can also do a STD test at the General Practioner  - If you test postive for an STD, you can get free medicine from the GGD or the GP  Find below the information details of the GGD in Amsterdam", "Document: Sexual Assault Center Centrum Seksueel Geweld (Sexual Assault Center) offers professional help for anyone who has experienced any form of rape or sexual assault.

At the Sexual Violence Center, a team of doctors, nurses, police officers, psychologists, social workers and sexologists work together to provide specialized care to victims.  

Available day and night (24/7) at the free number 0800-0188.

You can also chat with them on their website: https://centrumseksueelgeweld.nl/en/  

For most recent information and an overview of organisations that offer help with sexual or domestic violence see:  https://www.refugeehelp.nl/en/ukrainian-refugee/article/100109-help-in-cases-of-violence-and-human-trafficking", "Document: What can I do if I am not feeling safe at my host family?

Sorry to hear this.

There are a few options:     Are you in immediate danger?

Call 112.     

Contact a support organisation for assistance, information, mediatiation and more.

See for most recent information: www.refugeehelp.nl/get-help/category/safety    You can always contact Veilig Thuis (Safe at home) at 0800-2000.     

You can always go to an emergency shelter of the municipalities if you no longer want to stay with your host family.

If you give your location, I can give you a registration point nearby.    

See for most recent information: https://www.refugeehelp.nl/get-help/housing/regional-initiatives", "Document: I need an orthodontist, where can I go and is it reimbursed?  

In principle, the orthodontist will not be reimbursed.

The 16 orthodontic practices of TopOrtho in the Netherlands offer orthodontic emergency care up to €250 free of charge to refugees.     

For most recent information and to maken an appointment see: https://www.toportho.nl/emergency-dental-care-for-ukrainian-refugees-in-the-netherlands/", "Document: I need help with my pregnancy, where can I go?  

In the Netherlands you go to a midwife.

You can contact a midwife directly, you don’t have to go to the doctor first.   

You can google and see which midwife is close to you or check this website https://deverloskundige.nl/zoek-een-verloskundige   Read the flyer about (health care during) pregnancy in the Netherlands (in Ukrainian): https://assets.ctfassets.net/496uch1l97fc/2KF2tVsvf4WhqVUuSYS91s/9fe1a79f178ec9ef6a814fa85389b19c/Folder-geboortezorg-Oekraiens-Nederlands-CPZ-14-juni-2022-1.pdf      On this website you can find general information about the support you receive in the Netherlands when you are pregnant in English: https://www.kennisnetgeboortezorg.nl/wp-content/uploads/2022/03/Pregnant-aug-2021_0.pdf.", "Document: I have HIV, where can I get support?

You can contact Service point of the Hiv Association and a volunteer from the association can answer your questions.   

https://www.hivvereniging.nl/blog/belangenbeschijning/13701-hoe-zit-het-met-hiv-zorg-voor-vluchtelingen-uit-oekraine  Phone: 020 - 689 25 77 (Monday, Tuesday and Thursday from 14:00 to 22:00)   

Email: servicepunt@hivvereniging.nl", "Document: I want to go to a doctor, can you help me?  

When you get a question from someone in need of medical assistance, always make sure to follow these steps:  - Show empathy when somebody is contacting you with a medical issue - Always explain someones rights and the Dutch healthcare system.

Stress that somebody always has the right to see a doctor and get necessary medical care.

For Ukrainians with TP this means that they should visit a General Practitioner (GP) first.

Only the GP van refer to a specialist/hospital.

- If asked, make it clear that as the Red Cross we don’t provide medical services, we only refer people.

- If asked, explain that you cannot give medical advice on what somebody should do (for example; should I go to the emergency post), but you can explain the system and options.

- Check where somebody lives, and always try to find a GP most close by – so in a bigger city, also check this on neighborhood level.  - It can sometimes be quicker to find a doctor if they contact the doctor of their housemate / friend.  

-

In the evening / office hours; check urgency and if it can wait for the next day.", "Document: Where can I find healthcare for my child?  

The JGZ (youth healthcare) is responsible for preventive care for children, including those of refugees.

The JGZ provides physical, cognitive and psychosocial screenings and provides vaccinations in accordance with the National Vaccination Programme.   

Displaced persons from the Ukraine in the Netherlands can make use of this care free of charge.

Please contact the youth healthcare department of the regional GGD or JGZ organisation.  

An overview of JGZ locations can be found on Zorgkaart Nederland: https://www.zorgkaartnederland.nl/jeugdgezondheidszorg", "Document: I want to go to a dentist, can you help me?  

If you need to go to the dentist or need other oral care you can go to the service desk of your municipality.

They can refer you to a practitioner.  

In case of acute emergencies you can, in principle, go to any dental practice in the Netherlands.

This usually costs a maximum of €250.  

If you give us your location we can check if we have any information on dentists close to you that offer help to displaced persons from Ukraine and contact them directly.  

For an overview of all the important information on dental care for displaced persons from Ukraine see: https://knmt.nl/praktijkzaken/bijzondere-doelgroepen/vluchtelingen-uit-oekraine  Please note: if you stay in a crisis emergency shelter (CNO), the dental visit is sometimes postponed until you are placed somewhere where you can stay for longer.

If you have fever, an attempt is made to urgently schedule an appointment near the CNO.", "Document: Crisis shelter "Stay away from my Body" (Blijf van mijn Lijf-huis) Did you flee because of domestic or relational violence?

The crisis shelter of "Stay away from my body" can help you.

Call for free: 0800 0117.", "Document: How do I find a General Practitioner during working hours?

For people who are staying at a host (family):   First check whether you can go to the host's General Practitioner (GP).

Sometimes GPs no longer accept patients, so you have to look for another GP.

Do you not know how to find a general practitioner?

Then you can ask the municipality that you are staying in where the closest general practitioner is that can help you.    

For people who are in an emergency shelter:    We advise you to contact the medical facilities that are present there.

For example, Doctors of the World visits various emergency shelters.

The shelters themselves are better aware of this.   

You can get medical help if you are uninsured.

This is reimbursed by means of a special subsidy.

Sometimes GPs don't know this.

You can refer them to [the website of the CAK](https://www.hetcak.nl/zakelijk/regelingen/regeling-onverzekerden/subsidie-aanvragen/aanvraag).

However, this website is difficult to understand, so explain that they can show this website to the GP

but they don't need to understand it themselves.", "Document: I have an unintented or unwanted pregnancy, what can I do?  

You can go to Fiom, they offer specialist help with unintended or unwanted pregnancies.

They not only provide you with information on their website, but also offer online counselling, or you can make an appointment for a personal consultation.   

https://fiom.nl/  Telephone: +31 88 126 4900 Email: oz@fiom.nl.  

For most recent information see: https://www.refugeehelp.nl/en/ukrainian-refugee/article/100099-pregnancy", "Document: Where can I go when I have special care needs?

To receive specialist care, you often first need a referral from your General Practitioner (GP).

So you can often not just go to the hospital itself for your medical problems.

Do you need specialist care?

Then make sure that you first visit a GP so that you can be referred.

See the questions under 'Doctor' for more information on how to find a GP.   

In the subquestions you can find an overview of organisations that help people with special needs and disabilities.  

For most recent information see: https://www.refugeehelp.nl/en/ukrainian-refugee/article/100098-care-for-people-with-disabilities", "Document: Where can I get legal aid?  

Juridisch Loket The Legal Desk provides free first-line legal advice.

Displaced people from Ukraine can receive legal advice during walk-in consultation hours, by telephone (0900-8020 €0.10 p/min) or by e-mail, and make an appointment if necessary.

Advice is available in both Dutch and English.  

https://www.juridischloket.nl/      Rechtswinkel The Rechtswinkel provides free legal advice in areas such as work, rent, purchases and social security.

If costs are incurred (for example for starting a procedure), you will be informed as soon as possible.  

For opening hours and contact details, see the website:   - [Rechtswinkel Amsterdam](http://www.rechtswinkelamsterdam.nl/)   -

[Rechtswinkel Arnhem](https://www.rechtswinkelarnhem.nl/) -

[Rechtswinkel Baarn](https://www.pitbaarn.nl/is/organisatie/189768/invis2/rechtswinkel-baarn)    -

[Rechtswinkel Best](https://www.rechtswinkelbest.nl/) -", "Document: I am a transperson, where can I get support?

If you need trans care, you can contact the Trans United trans clinic, a community initiative with support from the GGD Amsterdam:  https://transunitedeurope.eu/?page_id=255  

For more information see:  - https://www.refugeehelp.nl/en/ukrainian-refugee/article/100298-living-in-the-netherlands-as-an-lgbtqia-individual - https://www.refugeehelp.nl/en/ukrainian-refugee/article/100299-activities-for-the-lgbtqia-community", "Document: I need medical treatment and I am in the Netherlands.

What can I do?

For most recent information on cancer treatment see: https://www.kanker.nl/nieuwsberichten/gratis-kankerzorg-voor-oekraiense-vluchtelingen", "Document: Huisartsenpost Amsterdam When you are in Amsterdam you can call or visit this place if you feel very sick outside of times that regular health services are open.

user_input: My host kicked me out and won't let me register for BRP. What can I do now? I need somewhere safe to stay.
bot_output:
I’m sorry this happened.

If you are in immediate danger, call **112**.

What you can do now:
- You can go to an **emergency shelter of the municipality** if you no longer want to stay with your host family or have been kicked out.
- If a host will not let you register, it is very important to find **other housing where you can register**, or go to a **municipal shelter**.
- Being registered in the **BRP** is very important. Without registration, you cannot get **Temporary Protection**. Social benefits are also connected to your address.
- If you find a new place to stay, you must **register in the BRP of the new municipality**, or report your new address if you stay in the same municipality.
- You can also contact **Veilig Thuis (Safe at Home)** at **0800-2000** for help with an unsafe situation.
- You may be able to get **free legal advice** from a local organization about the registration problem.

If you tell me **your location**, I can help you find a **registration point nearby**.

user_input: I am Ukrainian and confused about BRP registration. Is it different for me if I have a temporary residence permit? I need help with finding a place to stay too.
bot_output:
If you are **Ukrainian**, the BRP rules in the documents are different from the rule for **non-Ukrainians with a temporary Ukrainian residence permit**.

- **Ukrainians can register for the BRP** at the municipality where they are staying.
- The rule saying that people with a **temporary residence permit cannot register for the BRP** refers to **non-Ukrainians with a temporary residence permit for Ukraine**.

About staying in the Netherlands and BRP:
- You register for the **BRP at the municipality** where you are staying.
- Your registration is then automatically referred to the **IND**.
- After BRP registration, you receive a **BSN**.
- You should make an appointment with the **IND within 4 weeks** to get your proof of residence sticker.
- Only after you receive this sticker can you get **living allowance** and are allowed to **work and live** in the Netherlands.

About finding a place to stay:
- The Dutch government asks refugees from Ukraine to **find accommodation themselves if possible**, because shelter places are limited.
- If you cannot find a place to stay, you should **report to a municipality** to ask for help and to register.
- You can register at **any municipality**.
- If the municipality has space, they will help with housing.
- If not, they may contact the regional or national coordination system for refugee shelter.

Important note from the documents:
- In some guidance, it says you need a **local address (accommodation)** to apply for temporary protection.

If you want, I can also help you with the **step-by-step order** of what to do first: shelter, BRP, BSN, and IND.

I’m sorry you’re in pain and worried.

In the Netherlands, you usually need to see a General Practitioner (GP) first. The GP is the one who can refer you to a specialist or hospital. So in most cases, you cannot go directly to a hospital for specialist care without a GP referral.

If it is urgent:
- In the evening, night, or weekend, contact the GP emergency post: the huisartsenpost.
- If it is an emergency, call 112 or go to the Emergency Room in the nearest hospital.

If it is not life-threatening but you need help quickly:
- Try to contact a GP as soon as possible.
- If you are staying with a host family, first check whether you can go to your host’s GP.
- You can also ask the municipality where you are staying which GP nearby can help you.

You always have the right to see a doctor and get necessary medical care.

If you want, tell me:
- which city you are in, and
- whether it is daytime or evening/night/weekend,

and I can help you find the right option.

I’m sorry you’re worried. In the Netherlands, you can get language help for a hospital or doctor’s appointment.

- You can bring a Dutch-speaking friend or a translator.
- The doctor can also use a professional interpreter, and this is free for you.
- Every medical professional can use a translator.

How to arrange it:
- Tell them when you make the appointment that you need a translator.
- You can also say if you prefer a man or a woman.
- The doctor arranges the interpreter service.
- During the appointment, the doctor can call the interpreter so the conversation is translated.
- In difficult situations, an interpreter can sometimes be there in person instead of by phone. The doctor decides if that is necessary.

More information:
- https://www.zoschakeltueentolkin.nl/
- https://www.refugeehelp.nl/en/ukrainian-refugee/article/100398-what-you-need-to-know-if-you-have-a-healthcare-appointment-and-do-not-speak-dutch

Also, to see a specialist in the Netherlands, you usually first need a referral from a General Practitioner (GP).

user_input: I don't have a BSN and I need to open a bank account so I can get paid for work and buy food. Is it even possible? I'm really stressed about this.
bot_output:
I don't know.

From the information I have, I can only confirm:
- if you are registered in the RNI or BRP, you receive a BSN number;
- before leaving the Netherlands, some people may need to close their bank account, depending on the bank.

I don’t have reliable information here about whether a bank account can be opened without a BSN.

Assistance with returning to your country of origin: If you wish to receive assistance, register with the Repatriation and Departure Service (DT&V).

DT&V can help you arrange your journey to your country of origin or another country outside the EU where you are permitted to stay for a longer period.", "Document: Can I work in The Netherlands?  

Everyone who comes under the Temporary Protection Directive can work in the Netherlands without a work permit (in Dutch: tewerkstellingsvergunning or twv).

This means that an employer does not have to request a work permit for you.

And that you can easily look for a job, if you want to.   

The work permit exemption applies to all work in employment.

You will need an employment contract with an employer.

You must also meet the following requirements:  - You come under the Temporary Protection Directive.

We advise you to register at the local council if you come under the directive.  

- You have proof of residency showing that you are allowed to be in the Netherlands.

As proof, you will receive a sticker or card from the IND.  

The requirements for the exemption also apply if want to work as a volunteer.

The organisation where you want to work must then request a volunteer declaration from the UWV.

You may also work as a trainee, when you, your employer and your school have signed a trainee contract.

A twv is required if you want to work as a self-employed person.", "Document: Can I get proof of residence if I have a BSN number that I got with a RNI registration?

user_input: If I register at my friend's address for BRP, will it mess up their benefits? I really need a place to stay but I'm worried about causing problems for them.
bot_output:
Usually, no. Hosts can register refugees from Ukraine at their address without, for example, losing their social benefits.

It is very important that you are registered at an address in the Netherlands, because without registration you cannot get Temporary Protection. Also, if you were registered before, got Temporary Protection, and later deregistered, you can lose that status because it may look like you left the country.

If your friend is worried about financial consequences, that is often not the case. If they still do not want to register you, the best option is to look for other housing where you can register, or ask for a municipality shelter.

Also make sure you do not end up without a place to stay. If needed, you can look for free legal advice in your town about this issue.

Also social benefits are connected to your adress.  

Hosts can register refugees from Ukraine without for example losing their social benefits.

Maybe your hosts are afraid it has negative effects on their own financial situation, but this is often not the case.   

If the host won't register the PA, it is best to refer the PA to a municipality shelter or advise them to find other housing where they can register.  

Always check with the PA how long he/she can still stay with the host family/friends/relatives and make sure PA won't be on the street.

If you think this is the case, refer the case to the TC.   

You can check if there is an organization in the town that you stay in that can give free legal advice about this issue (see category 'Administrative').", "Document: How can I register for Basic Registration of Persons (BRP)?  

You can register for the Basic Registration of Persons (BRP) at the municipality you are staying.   

When you register for the BRP at the municipality, your registration is automatically referred to the Immigration & Naturalization Service (IND).

The IND is responsible for the process that establishes your temporary protected status.

Refugees from Ukraine that are registered at the IND will receive temporary protection and are allowed to stay at least until 4 March 2027.

This might be extended to a maximum of 3 years.  

After registering with the municipality, you will receive a citizen service number (BSN).

You will need this number for health care, education, work and financial matters (for example, opening a bank account).

When you received your BSN, you can apply for a DigiD.

You can use this to access online government services.", "Document: Can I register my newborn baby for the Basic Registration of Persons (BRP)?

Yes you can.

Within three days after the birth of a child, you have to report this to the municipality.

After registration you will receive a birth certificate.  

For the most recent information see: https://www.government.nl/topics/registering-a-birth-and-name-of-child/rules-for-registering-a-birth", "Document: Can I register for the Basic Registration of Persons (BRP) when I do not have documents?  

Without documents you can currently not register for the BRP.   

When you have the Ukrainian nationality but cannot prove this with documents (ID or passport), you should contact the Ukrainian embassy in The Hague.

They may be able to get proof of your identity and nationality.

The embassy can issue an identifying certificate that can be used to register for the BRP at the municpality.   Children from Ukraine without proof of identification can be registered with their parents at the municipality.

In the absence of documents, parents can make a statement on oath establishing the identity of the children.

The children are then registered by the municipality together with the parents.   

Address Ukrainian Embassy:  Zeestraat 78, 2518 AD The Hague  Open from Monday to Friday between 09:00 and 13:00 Telephone: +31 (70) 360 72 18  Email: emb_nl@mfa.gov.ua.

https://netherlands.mfa.gov.ua/en   

For the most recent information see: https://ind.nl/en/ukraine/temporary-protection-directive-ukraine", "Document: Another host shelter You can look for a new host family.

You can do this through your social network or through various local initiatives.

It is important that you register in the Basic Registration of Persons (BRP) of the new municipality, or report the new address to the BRP if you stay in the same municipality.", "Document: Please note that your request may not be honored.  

Important: If you do change locations, you need to re-register with the municipality of your new address.", "Document: What is the difference between a RNI registration and a BRP registration?  

The Non-residents Records Database (RNI) is a part of the Personal Records Database (BRP).

It is a register of people who do not live in the Netherlands, no longer live in the Netherlands or live in the Netherlands for less than 4 months.

For example migrant / seasonal workers register in the RNI.   

If you are registered in the RNI, you will receive a BSN number.

Please note: this BSN number is not valid for receiving a Proof of Residency under the Temporary Protection Directive.

In order to obtain a valid BSN number for applying for a proof of residence, you must register in the BRP in your municipality (see subcategory 'Registration' for more information).

For the shelter as well as for the municipality it’s important to know who is staying in which shelter.

Therefore we advise you to inform both if you have found another place to stay.   

When you change municipalities, it is important that you re-register with the new municipality so that they can update your details in the BRP.", "Document: Can I register for the Basic Registration of Persons (BRP) when I fled from Ukraine but I have another nationality?  

This depends on whether you have a permanent residence permit.

Only displaced persons from Ukraine who are covered by the Temporary Protection Directive can register with the BRP.

As of July 19, non-Ukrainians with a temporary residence permit for Ukraine can no longer apply for temporary protection.

This means that if you have a temporary residence permit, you cannot register with the BRP.   

For the most recent information see: https://ind.nl/en/ukraine/temporary-protection-directive-ukraine", "Document: What can I do and which support can I get after I register for the Basic Registration of Persons (BRP)?

After you register for BRP you have to make an appointment with the IND to collect your proof of residency, which is a sticker in your passport.

You have to make this appointment within 4 weeks after you got registered?

Only after you got this sticker you can get living allowance and you are allowed to work and live in the Netherlands.

For more information on how to make an appointment you can check the subcategorie "proof of residency".  

For the most recent information, see: https://ind.nl/en/ukraine/temporary-protection-directive-ukraine", "Document: Where can I check my details in the BRP?

Through MijnOverheid (https://www.netherlandsworldwide.nl/mijnoverheid-abroad/how-to-login), you can check with which details you are registered in the BRP.

You can log in with your DigiD. After logging in, click on Identity.

Then click on your personal details.

Do you not have a DigiD?

Then you can apply for a DigiD (https://www.netherlandsworldwide.nl/digid-abroad/how-to-apply).   

Can't do it online?

If you live in the Netherlands, you can contact the municipality where you live.  

Are your details not correct?

Please contact the municipality where you live.  

For most recent information, see: https://www.netherlandsworldwide.nl/personal-records-database-brp/what-data", "Document: You can use this to access online government services.   

For a step by step guide of what you should do if you have Temporary Protection, see: https://www.refugeehelp.nl/en/ukrainian-refugee/article/100040-this-is-what-you-should-do-if-you-have-temporary-protection  Please note: if you are staying in a municipal shelter, the municipality will contact you.

If you stay with people and want to register at this municipality, you need to register yourself.

In most cities this can be done at the city hall, but please check the website of your municpality.", "Document: In order to obtain a valid BSN number for applying for a proof of residence, you must register in the BRP in your municipality   For more information see: https://eu-solidarity-ukraine.ec.europa.eu/information-people-fleeing-war-ukraine/fleeing-ukraine-your-rights-eu_en", "Document: I previously had temporary protection in the Netherlands but left for a non-EU country (e.g., Canada).

Can I get temporary protection again if I return?          

You may regain temporary protection, but this depends on your situation.  

On returning to the Netherlands, you must re-register in the BRP and book a new IND appointment, even if you have a valid sticker or document, as your protection may have been withdrawn.

The IND will reassess your eligibility.

The new country refuses to register me since I’m already registered elsewhere.

What can I do?          

You are free to choose the EU country in which you enjoy temporary protection.

However, you can benefit from temporary protection only in one EU Member State at a time.

The rights connected to temporary protection are the same in every EU country bound by the Directive.  

If you have registered in one country and decide to move to another, you need to inform the authorities of the country in which you are currently registered.

The country where you move will then register you and offer you the temporary protection status and subsequent rights.   

Please note that if you had a temporary work visa for the Netherlands and are registered in the RNI, you will receive a BSN number.

Please note: this BSN number is not valid for receiving a Proof of Residency under the Temporary Protection Directive.", "Document: Can I get proof of residence if I have a BSN number that I got with a RNI registration?

No, this is not possible.

An RNI registration is for people who stay in the Netherlands for less than 4 months (e.g. migrant / seasonal workers).

The BSN number that belongs with the RNI registration is not valid for proof of residence under the Temporary Protection Directive.

In order to obtain a valid BSN number for applying for a proof of residence, you must register in the BRP in your municipality (see subcategory 'Registration' for more information).  

For the most recent information see: https://www.nederlandwereldwijd.nl/rni/wat-is-rni  https://www.rvig.nl/basisregistratie-personen https://ind.nl/en/ukraine/temporary-protection-directive-ukraine", "Document: Have you been deregistered from the BRP after 4 March 2024?

Then you must inform the municipality before 4 May 2024 that you want to register again.

It does not matter if the municipality processes your registration after 4 May. - You did not leave the Netherlands with the help of the Repatriation and Departure Service (in Dutch: Dienst Terugkeer en Vertrek or DTenV) or other financial assistance. - You have not left the Schengen area after 4 March 2024.

Or you have been in Ukraine for no longer than 28 days. - Before 4 March 2024, you have been outside the Schengen area for no longer than 28 days.  

What can you do?

If the freeze applies to you, there are still a few options left to stay in the Netherlands.

You can apply for a different kind of status a work/study visum or start a regular asylum application.

However, a large part of the group of third-country nationals has already tried this without success, meaning that a large part of this group of approximately 1700 people will lose their right to stay in the Netherlands.", "Document: What is a proof of residency?

If you fall under the Temporary Protection Directive and are registered in the BRP, you can obtain a certificate from the IND that you are allowed to live and work in the Netherlands.

This certificate is a sticker in your passport or on a separate piece of paper.

Sometimes you will be given a card.

Applying for residency under the directive is free of charge!!   

The sticker or card is valid from 4 March 2022 to 4 March 2027.

Your sticker or card is only valid in the Netherlands.

Are you applying for protection in another EU country?

Then your protection stops in the Netherlands.  

For the most recent information see:  - [IND](https://ind.nl/en/ukraine-appointment-to-collect-proof-of-residency)  - [IND](https://ind.nl/en/ukraine/temporary-protection-directive-ukraine) -

[RefugeeHelp](https://www.refugeehelp.nl/nl/ukrainian-refugee/article/100040-dit-moet-je-doen-als-je-tijdelijke-bescherming-hebt)", "Document: Will I still receive care if I have received a residence permit?

If you receive a regular residence permit, you will need to apply for health insurance yourself once you are housed by the municipality as a permit holder.", "Document: If you register as a “non-resident” in RNI, you are not qualified for temporary protection in The Netherlands.

You can read more about the conditions for working in The Netherlands here: https://www.refugeehelp.nl/en/ukrainian-refugee/article/100149-conditions-for-working-in-the-netherlands   Please note: the Red Cross cannot issue the “sticker” or any other documents for that matter.

user_input: I need urgent medical help but I don't have a GP. What can I do? I'm really scared and don't know where to go.
bot_output:
I’m sorry you’re going through this. You have the right to see a doctor and get necessary medical care in the Netherlands.

If this is life-threatening or you are in immediate danger, call 112 right now. Everyone has the right to call.

If it is urgent but not life-threatening:
- In the evening, night, or weekend, contact the huisartsenpost (GP emergency post) for urgent questions:
  https://www.zorgkaartnederland.nl/huisartsenpost
- You can also go to the Emergency Room in the nearest hospital in an emergency.

If it is during working hours and you do not have a GP:
- If you stay with a host family, first ask whether you can go to your host’s GP.
- If you are in an emergency shelter, contact the medical facilities there. The shelter usually knows what is available.
- You can also ask the municipality where you are staying which GP nearby can help you.
- You can search for a GP here:
  - https://www.kiesuwhuisarts.nl/
  - https://www.zorgkaartnederland.nl/huisarts?zoekterm=huisarts.

If you are uninsured, you can still get medical help. This is reimbursed through a special subsidy.

I can’t give medical advice about whether you personally should go to the emergency post or hospital, but I can explain your options and help you find the closest place.

If you tell me:
1. your city or postcode, and
2. whether it is life-threatening right now,
I can help you look for the nearest urgent care option.

bot_output:
Yes. If you need a safe place to sleep tonight, here’s what to do:

- If you are in immediate danger, call 112.
- If you are not safe where you are staying now, you can go to an emergency shelter run by the municipality.
- If you need help, information, or mediation, you can contact support organisations via:
  - www.refugeehelp.nl/get-help/category/safety
- You can also contact Veilig Thuis (Safe at Home) at 0800-2000.
- If you fled because of domestic or relationship violence, you can contact the crisis shelter “Blijf van mijn Lijf-huis” for free at 0800 0117.

If you are arriving in the Netherlands and need shelter, visit a municipality. Municipalities register displaced Ukrainians and help find housing.

If you share your location, I can help point you to a nearby registration point.

bot_output:
Yes. You always have the right to medically necessary care in the Netherlands, even if you do not have papers or insurance.

If you are in the Netherlands and need a doctor:
- First go to a General Practitioner (GP).
- If you are staying with a host family, first ask whether you can go to your host’s GP.
- If you are in an emergency shelter, contact the medical facilities there, because they often know what care is available.

If you are uninsured, you can still get medical help. This can be reimbursed through a special subsidy. Sometimes a GP may not know this, and they can check the CAK information here:
https://www.hetcak.nl/zakelijk/regelingen/regeling-onverzekerden/subsidie-aanvragen/aanvraag

If it is evening or outside normal office hours:
- If it is urgent, you can call the huisartsenpost.
- In a life-threatening emergency, call 112 or go to the nearest hospital Emergency Room.

If you tell me which city or area you are in, I can help explain how to find a GP nearby.

user_input: I got kicked out of my house and I don't know what to do now. Is it different if I left on my own? Can you help me find somewhere to stay?
bot_output:
If you were **evicted from a shelter** or **had to leave your host family/house**, what you can do depends on the situation.

### If you were evicted or transferred from a municipal shelter
If you were entitled to a place in a municipal reception centre but were evicted or transferred, you should:
- collect information about your case:
  - how long you stayed there
  - the reason for eviction
- contact RefugeeHelp’s online consultation:  
  https://www.refugeehelp.nl/nl/ukrainian-refugee/appointment

### If you left a municipal shelter on your own
A displaced person may leave reception:
- for **up to 14 days** and keep their shelter place
- for **up to 28 days** and keep their living allowance

But you must **always report your departure** to shelter staff.  
If you do **not** report it, you can lose your shelter place immediately and the municipality can stop your living allowance.

If you return, you may be given:
- a different place
- in a different shelter
- and possibly in another municipality if your old place is no longer available

### If you left or were asked to leave a host family
If your stay in a private shelter ends, you can:
- look for **another host family**
- ask the **municipality** for help with shelter
- look for **independent housing** yourself

If you do not feel safe, you can always go to an **emergency shelter of the municipality**.

### Can I help you find somewhere to stay?
I can help with the next step, but I need your **location** first.  
If you send me your **city or municipality in the Netherlands**, I can help point you to a nearby registration point or municipality option.

### If you are in immediate danger
Call **112**.

If you are not safe at home, you can also contact **Veilig Thuis (Safe at Home)**: **0800-2000**.

You always have the right to medically necessary care in the Netherlands.

If you are undocumented, you still have the right to necessary medical care. You can also get emergency healthcare. You should not be turned away just because you do not have papers.

If you cannot pay, the healthcare provider may be able to use a special subsidy scheme for uninsured people.

If you want, I can also help explain how to find a GP or huisartsenpost near you.

user_input: I need a place to stay for a few months, but I have trouble moving around and need somewhere accessible. Can you help me find shelter?
bot_output:
If you need help finding shelter, you should go to a municipality (“gemeente”). Municipalities register displaced Ukrainians and help find housing.

Because you have difficulty moving around, you can also contact the Wmo-loket of the municipality where you are staying. The municipality usually helps with permanent medical aid devices, such as a wheelchair.

I don’t know from the documents whether municipalities can specifically arrange an accessible shelter place, but they are responsible for shelter placement.

Useful information:
- Shelter help: go to the municipality
- Medical aid devices/accessibility support: contact the municipality’s Wmo-loket

["Document: General Info and Basic Instructions for TP & shelter Links to the Red Cross Website  On the Red Cross Website you can now find updated information regarding the shelter process for Ukrainian refugees.

Click on the following links for the [English](https://www.rodekruis.nl/english-information/), [Ukrainian](https://www.rodekruis.nl/ukrainian/) and the [Russian](https://www.rodekruis.nl/russian/) version of this webpage.

You can always share these links with the PA as well.

See also below what the general explanation is.   

General Information  TP is valid until March 2027.

In principle, this means that displaced people from Ukraine should be helped during this time.

However, the housing situation is difficult, especially within municipal shelters.

Therefore:  1.

If PA does not need help with shelter, and can afford a place to stay (even for a few days): PA can look for a place themselves.

PA has to check if they can register at the accommodation and also at the municipality.  

2.

If PA needs help with finding shelter, please know that the situation is currently very difficult and becoming more restricted.   

3.", "Document: Can I change a shelter (because conditions are not nice, or to be closer to work, or to be closer to family and friends, or because I want to live in the city/in the countryside/in a different place, etc.)?

The Red Cross does not influence the placement in the shelters.

This is done by the municipalities.

Therefore, the Red Cross cannot assist you with changing locations.  

Unfortunately, the housing situation is really tough in the Netherlands.

If you live in a municipal shelter already, it is nearly impossible to change from one municipal shelter to a different municipal shelter.   

You could always try to arrange new accommodation by yourself.

Although this is very difficult, you could check this website for example: https://www.funda.nl/en/huur/. You could also register with the housing corporation in the municipality of your choice to find housing.

Hopefully, you will find some suitable options for you.  

If you do have urgent reasons for relocating (e.g. medical reasons), you could request to change shelters.

First, check if there is a place available in the shelter of your choice.

If this is the case, you can request resettlement at the municipality.", "Document: Where can I find shelter when arriving in the Netherlands?

The Red Cross does not influence the placement in the shelters.

This is done by the municipalities.

Therefore, the Red Cross cannot assist you with changing locations.  

Unfortunately, the housing situation is really tough in the Netherlands.

If you live in a municipal shelter already, it is nearly impossible to change from one municipal shelter to a different municipal shelter.   

You could always try to arrange new accommodation by yourself.

Although this is very difficult, you could check this website for example: https://www.funda.nl/en/huur/. You could also register with the housing corporation in the municipality of your choice to find housing.

Hopefully, you will find some suitable options for you.  

If you do have urgent reasons for relocating (e.g. medical reasons), you could request to change shelters.

First, check if there is a place available in the shelter of your choice.

If this is the case, you can request resettlement at the municipality.

For more information, talk with the management of your shelter location, or go to the municipality.

Please note that your request may not be honored.", "Document: Abroad  General advise If you’re coming to the Netherlands with a Ukrainian passport/valid permanent Ukrainian residence permit and proof you left Ukraine after November 26, 2021, you have a right to Shelter & Temporary Protection.

To apply, visit the municipality office in the city where you will arrive.  

Please note that the housing situation here is challenging and becoming more restricted.

Note that you need a local address (accommodation) to apply for temporary protection.   

Actions to take when general advise was not sufficient NO referrals for cases outside of the Netherlands.

Advise the PA to contact us upon arrival.", "Document: What facilities should be available at a Crisis Emergency Shelter?

The following facilities must be present at a crisis emergency shelter: - Goods hygiene - Beds, mattresses, pillows, blankets, etc. - Marker materials, potester materials, printer, markers - Wifi (very strong network for residents) - Plenty of charging stations phones residents - Recreational activities - Clothes (seasonal) young and old - Cleaning supplies - Meals (or dining money) -

Access to medical care - Third party insurance  Based on Red Cross standards, the following are specifically added: - Clothing and shoes - Shower gel - Shampoo - Toothbrush & toothpaste - Menstural hygiene - Razor - Bath Towel - Hairbrush - Diapers - Space for children  For more information see:  - https://vng.nl/sites/default/files/2021-10/handreiking-crisisnoodopvang.pdf - https://wetten.overheid.nl/BWBR0017959/2022-01-01#HoofdstukIV", "Document: If this is the case, you can request resettlement at the municipality.

What to do on return: - When you return to the Netherlands, you must report again to the municipality or municipal reception center where you previously stayed.

- If you have lost your shelter place as a result of the earlier (temporary) departure and the living allowance has been stopped, it will be assessed whether you comply with the applicable rules at the time of your return.

If this is the case, you are again entitled to childcare and the other benefits in kind from the ROOO.

- If you have been deregistered from the BRP, registration must be done again.   

What to do with earlier advice on a shelter location in case of temporary departure: - At the moment, municipalities are advised to maintain a shelter for displaced persons who leave the municipal shelter for less than 14 days.

- This advice was issued mid-2022 and remains valid.

Below you will find more information on what facilities should be present at the different types of reception.   

Please note: this overview is based on information from COA, COA arranges reception for refugees not covered by the Temporary Protection Directive.

Therefore, the facilities for displaced persons from Ukraine may differ in practice.", "Document: Can I travel to Ukraine without losing the temporary protection status?   

Ukrainians who already have a temporary protection and have an urgent reason can travel to Ukraine for urgent matters, such as picking up relatives, transporting belongings, or medical issues, and return to the Netherlands within a few days or weeks.

However, if you stay in Ukraine or another country for an extended period, the IND may look whether you still qualify for temporary protection.

user_input: I don't feel safe at my host family's place. Where can I go and how do I sign up for somewhere else?
bot_output:
I’m sorry to hear this.

If you are in immediate danger, call 112.

If you no longer feel safe at your host family, you can go to an emergency shelter of the municipality. To get a place somewhere else, you should register with a municipality. You can register at any municipality, sometimes in person or sometimes by email. After registration, the municipality will help with housing. If that municipality has no space, they contact the regional coordination system to find a place.

If you are already registered in a municipality, first ask that municipality for a place in municipal reception. If there is no room, they will contact the safety region, and if needed the national coordination office.

You can also contact:
- Veilig Thuis (Safe at Home): 0800-2000
- If you fled domestic or relationship violence: Blijf van mijn Lijf-huis: 0800 0117

If you give me your location, I can help point you to a nearby registration point.

bot_output:
Yes — if you are a displaced person from Ukraine in the Netherlands, urgent and necessary medical care is covered under the RMO if you have a BSN.

For dental care, coverage depends on the situation:

- Adults: reimbursement is limited to €250 per year, and treatment is focused on relieving urgent pain at minimal cost.
- Children under 18: treatment is not limited in amount, except orthodontics and prosthetics with implants or porcelain-ceramic crowns.

Covered dental care includes:
- Non-periodic consultation
- Endodontic treatment for complications of caries (such as pulpitis or periodontitis), with a maximum of 2 canals

Not covered:
- Treatment of molars 16, 17, 26, 27, 36, 37, 46, 47
- Crowns, bridges, and orthodontics
- Erosion and attrition of teeth

Important conditions:
- The clinic can help patients living within 50 km of the clinic
- You must make an appointment through Tandartslijn: 0881122112
- In urgent cases, the clinic may need to prove the urgency

If you need a dentist now:
- You can go to the service desk of your municipality for a referral
- In acute emergencies, you can in principle go to any dental practice in the Netherlands; this usually costs a maximum of €250

If you want, tell me your location and I can help you check the best next step based on the information above.

user_input: I am Ukrainian and thinking about going back home, but I don't know what to do or who can help me. Can you tell me about travel options and if there is any support for people like me? Also, I am worried about legal stuff and if I can get help with starting over. Please help.
bot_output:
If you want to return to Ukraine, there is support available.

**Return support**
- The **Repatriation and Departure Service (DT&V)** can help displaced persons from Ukraine who want to return or continue their migration.
- Depending on your nationality and country of return, they may provide **return and/or reintegration support**.
- More information in English and Ukrainian:
  https://english.dienstterugkeerenvertrek.nl/latest/news/2022/07/01/assistance-for-those-returning-to-ukraine
- You can also use the **contact form at the bottom of that DT&V page** to ask for help with your return.

**Travel**
- The Dutch government currently has a **negative travel advice for Ukraine**.
- Returning to Ukraine is **at your own risk and responsibility**.
- If you want to leave the Netherlands only temporarily, this is possible in some cases:
  - For urgent matters, Ukrainians with temporary protection can travel to Ukraine and return within a few days or weeks.
  - If you stay away for a longer period, the IND may assess whether you still qualify for temporary protection.
- If you live in a shelter:
  - you may leave for **14 days per calendar year** and keep your reception place
  - and **28 days per calendar year** with retention of living allowance
  - you must always report your departure to shelter staff
- If you leave the Netherlands **permanently**, you must **deregister from the municipality**.
- You are also requested to **inform the IND** of your departure so the Temporary Protection procedure can be withdrawn.

**Can you come back later?**
Yes, according to the information provided, you can come back to the Netherlands after returning to Ukraine if:
- you deregistered in the Netherlands
- you have a passport stamp for entry to Ukraine
- you have a passport stamp for exit from Ukraine

If these conditions are met, you can be re-registered in the Netherlands.
This does **not** apply if you left Ukraine before **27 November 2021**.

**Legal help**
For legal questions, you can contact:
- **VluchtelingenWerk**: https://www.refugeehelp.com/get-help  
  Email: **oekraine@vluchtelingenwerk.nl**
- Free legal aid near you: https://eersterechtshulp.nl/
- More legal aid information: https://www.refugeehelp.nl/en/ukrainian-refugee/article/100044-legal-aid-in-the-netherlands
- **Opora** can help with migration law, family law, housing law, civil law, administrative and criminal law, and labour law:
  https://www.oporafoundation.nl/our-projects

**Starting over / reintegration**
The documents say that DT&V may provide **reintegration support**, depending on nationality and/or country of return. For return to Ukraine, the best next step is to contact DT&V directly through their page:
https://english.dienstterugkeerenvertrek.nl/latest/news/2022/07/01/assistance-for-those-returning-to-ukraine

There is also a Red Cross information video about return:
- EN: https://youtu.be/PV-PJv-oCDw
- UA: https://youtu.be/5YsAYFqYsjM
- RUS: https://youtu.be/n_otbQncTHs

If you want, I can also help you make a simple step-by-step plan for returning to Ukraine.

I’m sorry you’re dealing with this.

In the Netherlands, you have the right to necessary medical care, even if you do not have papers or insurance. For eye treatment and medicine, the best first step is usually to contact a General Practitioner (GP). A GP can assess your problem and refer you to a specialist or hospital if needed.

If you need help specifically with an eye condition, you can also contact the Eye Association. They advise and refer people to the right authorities for:
- eye care such as eye drops, injections, or other treatments
- support for living with a visual impairment in the Netherlands

Contact details:
- Phone: 030-2945444
- Email: ooglijn@oogvereniging.nl
- More information: https://www.oogvereniging.nl/standpunten/steunpunt-migranten/steunpunt-oekraiense-vluchtelingen/

How to find a GP during working hours:
- If you are staying with a host family, first ask whether you can go to the host’s GP.
- If that is not possible, ask the municipality where you are staying which GP nearby can help you.
- You can also search here:
  - https://www.kiesuwhuisarts.nl/
  - https://www.zorgkaartnederland.nl/huisarts?zoekterm=huisarts.

If you are in an emergency shelter, contact the medical facilities there. The shelter usually knows what care is available.

If it is evening, night, or weekend and the problem is urgent, contact the huisartsenpost:
- https://www.zorgkaartnederland.nl/huisartsenpost

If this is an emergency, call 112 or go to the nearest Emergency Room.

If you want, tell me your location in the Netherlands and I can help you think through the best next step.

user_input: I keep getting threatened in the shelter and I feel unsafe. Is there any special help for people like me? I really need protection.
bot_output:
I’m sorry you’re going through this.

If you are in immediate danger, call 112.

There is special help if you feel unsafe:
- You can contact Veilig Thuis (Safe at Home): 0800-2000
- You can go to an emergency shelter of the municipality if you no longer feel safe at your host family or shelter
- If you fled because of domestic or relationship violence, the crisis shelter “Blijf van mijn Lijf-huis” can help. Call free: 0800 0117

You can also contact a support organisation for assistance, information, and mediation:
- www.refugeehelp.nl/get-help/category/safety

If you share your location, I can help you find a registration point nearby.
context:
["Document: Tips for Applying for Temporary Protection (Email, WhatsApp)

Please ask the  PAs to write a formal request to the municipality.  

Please do not just "I need help".

Please write and  explain that :   - This is Application for Temporary Protection, -

In need fo accommodation, (if applicable, include where you are staying currently and how long you can stay there) - Full Name, - Date of Birth, -

Date you left Ukraine ( to the EU or to NL), - Ukrainian documents ( photo of passport in attachement),  - Details of each person requesting help, including family relations, - Special needs, if applicable (e.g. medical conditions, senior citizens, unaccompanied minor..)

- Offer to provide more infromation if request by the municipality", "Document: Public shelter If you are covered by the Temporary Protection Directive, you keep your right to reception.

The reception is a joint responsibility of all Dutch municipalities and Safety Regions.

In the first place you report to the municipality in which you are registered with a request for a place in the municipal reception facilities.

If there is no room (or no longer any room), the 'registering municipality' will contact the safety region.

The safety region will see if there is a place available in the region.

If that is not the case, the safety region submits a request for trans-regional relocation to the KCIO (Ukraine Coordination Information Office).", "Document: What can I do if I don't feel comfortable at my host family?

I am sorry to hear this.

Sharing a household can be challenging, especially if there are cultural differences in lifestyle, food, manners or rules.

If you give your location, I can give you the address of a registration point nearby.

user_input: Hi, I'm in Amsterdam and I don't have anywhere to sleep or eat. Is there a place where I can get food and rest from the Red Cross? I'm really tired and hungry.
bot_output:

user_input: I need a wheelchair but I can't afford a new one. Is there anywhere I can get a cheap or second-hand electric wheelchair? I'm disabled and it's really hard to move around without it.
bot_output:
If you need a permanent aid like a wheelchair, you will usually receive this from the municipality where you live. You can contact the Wmo-loket of your municipality.

If you want a cheaper option yourself, the information I have says:
- you can buy or rent a walker via a thuiszorgwinkel
- you can find cheap second-hand wheelchairs or walkers on Marktplaats

I don’t have specific information about second-hand electric wheelchairs.
context:
["Document: I need a wheelchair or another permanent medical aid device If you need permanent aids, such as a wheelchair, for example because of a disability, you will usually receive these from your municipality.   

You can contact the Wmo-loket of the municipality you are residing in.   

You can also buy or rent a walker yourself, for example via the thuiszorgwinkel.

On Marktplaats you can also find cheap second-hand wheelchairs or walker.", "Document: I need a dentist for my child.

Where do I find one?  

If your child needs to go to the dentist or needs other oral care you can go to the service desk of your municipality.

They can refer you to a practitioner.  

In case of acute emergencies you can, in principle, go to any dental practice in the Netherlands.

This usually costs a maximum of €250.  

If you give us your location we can check if we have any information on dentists close to you that offer help to displaced persons from Ukraine and contact them directly.", "Document: I need glasses, where can I get one and is it reimbursed?

You can get glasses at Pearle Opticians and Specsavers.

But please note: glasses are only covered/reimbursed if you are registered at RMO for more than 8 weeks!  

Further requirements for reimbursement are:  - deviation of one or both eyes higher than (plus or minus) 1.50 diopters - Additional condition for reading glasses is a strength difference of at least 0.75 diopters  For the purchase or replacement of glasses, RMO has an agreement with Pearle Opticians and Specsavers.

Pearle and Specsavers do the eye measurement and check if you are entitled to glasses.

They can check with your BSN if you are a refugee and registered with RMO, so there is no need to pay the glasses upfront.   

Please note: from 18 years of age or older: from 8 weeks after registration with the RMO, a claim can be made for 1 pair of glasses every 3 years.

Under 18 years of age: claim can be made for 1 pair of glasses every 2 years.", "Document: I have HIV, where can I get support?

You can contact Service point of the Hiv Association and a volunteer from the association can answer your questions.   

https://www.hivvereniging.nl/blog/belangenbeschijning/13701-hoe-zit-het-met-hiv-zorg-voor-vluchtelingen-uit-oekraine  Phone: 020 - 689 25 77 (Monday, Tuesday and Thursday from 14:00 to 22:00)   

Email: servicepunt@hivvereniging.nl", "Document: See for most recent information: https://www.rmoekraine.nl/Verzekerden/Vergoedingen/Hulpmiddelen (under 'brillen')", "Document: How can I get medicine?  

You can only buy prescription medicines at a pharmacy.

Your general practitioner (GP) or specialist will prescribe the medicines.   

You can buy over-the-counter medicines (like paracetamol) at drugstores (like Etos or Kruidvat) and supermarkets without a prescription.  

You can find additional information on the website from the Dutch government: https://www.government.nl/topics/medicines/question-and-answer/where-can-i-buy-medicines-in-the-netherlands", "Document: How can I get support with clothes?  

The Red Cross Helpful Information website provides an overview of clothing options available in different cities.

You can always refer the PA to this website or share the list of options found there directly.  

https://helpfulinformation.redcross.nl/  For most recent information on initiatives that provide support in clothes or offer clothes for a small price see: https://www.refugeehelp.nl/en/marketplace", "Document: Where can I get legal aid?  

Juridisch Loket The Legal Desk provides free first-line legal advice.

Displaced people from Ukraine can receive legal advice during walk-in consultation hours, by telephone (0900-8020 €0.10 p/min) or by e-mail, and make an appointment if necessary.

Advice is available in both Dutch and English.  

https://www.juridischloket.nl/      Rechtswinkel The Rechtswinkel provides free legal advice in areas such as work, rent, purchases and social security.

If costs are incurred (for example for starting a procedure), you will be informed as soon as possible.  

For opening hours and contact details, see the website:   - [Rechtswinkel Amsterdam](http://www.rechtswinkelamsterdam.nl/)   -

[Rechtswinkel Arnhem](https://www.rechtswinkelarnhem.nl/) -

[Rechtswinkel Baarn](https://www.pitbaarn.nl/is/organisatie/189768/invis2/rechtswinkel-baarn)    -

[Rechtswinkel Best](https://www.rechtswinkelbest.nl/) -", "Document: Where can I go when I have special care needs?

To receive specialist care, you often first need a referral from your General Practitioner (GP).

So you can often not just go to the hospital itself for your medical problems.

Do you need specialist care?

Then make sure that you first visit a GP so that you can be referred.

See the questions under 'Doctor' for more information on how to find a GP.   

In the subquestions you can find an overview of organisations that help people with special needs and disabilities.  

For most recent information see: https://www.refugeehelp.nl/en/ukrainian-refugee/article/100098-care-for-people-with-disabilities", "Document: I need an orthodontist, where can I go and is it reimbursed?  

In principle, the orthodontist will not be reimbursed.

The 16 orthodontic practices of TopOrtho in the Netherlands offer orthodontic emergency care up to €250 free of charge to refugees.     

For most recent information and to maken an appointment see: https://www.toportho.nl/emergency-dental-care-for-ukrainian-refugees-in-the-netherlands/", "Document: Can I rent a house?  

You can rent a house from private individuals.

In general, houses are expensive, because there is a large housing shortage in the Netherlands, especially in the larger cities.   

As a displaced person from Ukraine, you will receive living allowance when you stay at a shelter location, both in the municipal shelter and in the private shelter.

If you rent your own independent accommodation, you are no longer entitled to living allowance.  

Places where private homes are offered: Funda, AirBNB, Marktplaats website, Facebook groups per city (search for 'I'm looking for a home').   

For most recent information see: [RefugeeHelp](https://www.refugeehelp.nl/en/ukrainian-refugee/article/100045-permanent-housing)  and [renting a house](https://www.refugeehelp.nl/en/ukrainian-refugee/article/100047-this-is-what-you-need-to-arrange-if-you-rent-a-house)", "Document: I want to go to a dentist, can you help me?  

If you need to go to the dentist or need other oral care you can go to the service desk of your municipality.

They can refer you to a practitioner.  

In case of acute emergencies you can, in principle, go to any dental practice in the Netherlands.

This usually costs a maximum of €250.  

If you give us your location we can check if we have any information on dentists close to you that offer help to displaced persons from Ukraine and contact them directly.  

For an overview of all the important information on dental care for displaced persons from Ukraine see: https://knmt.nl/praktijkzaken/bijzondere-doelgroepen/vluchtelingen-uit-oekraine  Please note: if you stay in a crisis emergency shelter (CNO), the dental visit is sometimes postponed until you are placed somewhere where you can stay for longer.

If you have fever, an attempt is made to urgently schedule an appointment near the CNO.", "Document: How do I find a General Practitioner during working hours?

For people who are staying at a host (family):   First check whether you can go to the host's General Practitioner (GP).

Sometimes GPs no longer accept patients, so you have to look for another GP.

Do you not know how to find a general practitioner?

Then you can ask the municipality that you are staying in where the closest general practitioner is that can help you.    

For people who are in an emergency shelter:    We advise you to contact the medical facilities that are present there.

For example, Doctors of the World visits various emergency shelters.

The shelters themselves are better aware of this.   

You can get medical help if you are uninsured.

This is reimbursed by means of a special subsidy.

Sometimes GPs don't know this.

You can refer them to [the website of the CAK](https://www.hetcak.nl/zakelijk/regelingen/regeling-onverzekerden/subsidie-aanvragen/aanvraag).

However, this website is difficult to understand, so explain that they can show this website to the GP

but they don't need to understand it themselves.", "Document: MEE Municipalities and MEE, an association of 20 social service organizations, help people with special needs.

You will be assigned a social worker who will guide not only you or your child, but the whole family.   

Please note: not all help is free.

Some aid (for example orthopedic shoes or hearing aids) must be partially paid for yourself.   

For most recent information see: https://www.mee.nl/", "Document: My child needs a vaccine, where can I go?  

The vaccinations of the National Vaccination Programme for children are free.

These vaccinations can be obtained from the child health care centre, the GGD or other youth care institutions in your area.

The Dutch government is taking measures to increase the number of vaccinated people.   

A national overview of JGZ locations can be found on Zorgkaart Nederland: https://www.zorgkaartnederland.nl/jeugdgezondheidszorg", "Document: EnableMe UA EnableMe UA is a complete, up-to-date guide on all issues of disability and a friendly community for Ukrainians with special needs, mental disorders, chronic diseases and various disability groups.   

EnableMe Ukraine offers information, advice and online support to people with physical, mental or psychological disabilities.  

For most recent information see: https://www.enableme.com.ua/ua", "Document: Social Security Act (WMO) Support for persons with disabilities is provided through the Social Security Act (Wmo).

You can also make use of more long-term care, such as care from the Wmo.

This care is provided by municipalities.

The WMO regulates help and support for citizens, so that they can live independently at home for as long as possible and continue to participate in society.", "Document: [Rechtswinkel Best](https://www.rechtswinkelbest.nl/) -

[Rechtswinkel Eindhoven](http://www.rechtswinkeleindhoven.org/)    -

[Rechtswinkel Groningen](http://www.rechtswinkel-groningen.nl/)  -

[Rechtswinkel Rotterdam](https://rechtswinkelrotterdam.nl/) -

[Rechtswinkel Schiedam](https://www.rechtswinkelschiedam.nl/)   -

[Rechtswinkel Tilburg](http://www.rechtswinkeltilburg.nl/) -

[Rechtswinkel Utrecht](http://www.rechtswinkelutrecht.nl/) - [Rechtswinkel Venlo](https://www.rechtswinkelvenlo.nl/)   -

[Rechtswinkel Zoetermeer](http://www.rechtswinkelzoetermeer.nl/)     Eersterechtshulp.nl On the First Legal Aid website you will find free legal help in your area and online.

You can find lawyers on a pro bono basis, walk-in consultations with lawyers in your area and help in applying for compensation for being wrongly detained or contesting a traffic fine.", "Document: Can you help me finding a job?  

The Red Cross does not provide help in finding a job.

You can better contact your municipality about it.

There are some useful sites or websites that can help:     

[Good website with explanation step by step of how to find a job in the Netherlands for Ukrainians, also with useful websites, not Red  Cross information](https://livinginholland.blog/rabota_ua_nl_1/)   

[This website gives general information and tips about finding works and people’s rights](https://www.fairwork.nu/en/tips-for-working-in-the-netherlands/)  https://linktr.ee/nljobguide4ua    

For most recent information, see the website of RefugeeHelp:  

[EN](https://www.refugeehelp.nl/en/ukrainian-refugee/article/100115-finding-work)

[NL](https://www.refugeehelp.nl/nl/ukrainian-refugee/article/100115-werk-vinden)", "Document: (in EN, UKR, RU, NL).  

Please note   1) Refusal of protection in one of the EU countries does not grant temporary protection in a different EU country automatically.

user_input: I am Ukrainian under temporary protection and got refused for municipal shelter. How can I try again or find somewhere to stay? I feel really lost.

I’m sorry you’re going through this.

If you are covered by the Temporary Protection Directive, you keep your right to reception. Here is what you can do:

1. Go again to the municipality where you are registered and ask for a place in the municipal shelter.

- ask whether they can offer a temporary solution while they search for a place.

- stay with a host family, friends, or relatives if possible,
- look for independent housing yourself, for example rentals,
- if you need help finding shelter on arrival, municipalities are the place to ask.

- Red Cross information pages: https://www.rodekruis.nl/english-information/
- RefugeeHelp on arrival and shelter: https://www.refugeehelp.nl/ru/ukrainian-refugee/article/100179-chto-neobhodimo-sdelat-po-pribytii-v-niderlandy

user_input: I have temporary protection in another EU country but I want to move and work here. What do I need to do? I feel lost and don't know where to start.

If you have temporary protection in another EU country and want to move to the Netherlands to live and work, here’s where to start:

1. Check if you are eligible for temporary protection in the Netherlands  
You should first check the Dutch requirements, for example:
- your nationality
- when you left Ukraine
- what kind of residence status or visa you had

You can read more here:
- https://www.refugeehelp.nl/en/ukrainian-refugee/article/100187-conditions-of-temporary-protection-directive
- https://ind.nl/en/ukraine/temporary-protection-directive-ukraine

2. Remember: you can only have temporary protection in one EU country at a time  
You can choose the EU country where you want to have temporary protection, but you can only benefit from it in one Member State at a time.  
You can only live and work legally in the country that granted you temporary protection.

3. If you want to move to the Netherlands  
According to the documents:
- you have the right to change the country that grants you temporary protection
- the IND should not object if you currently have temporary protection elsewhere
- according to the IND, you do not need to deregister first in the other country before applying in the Netherlands

If the Netherlands grants you temporary protection, the other country can later see this and terminate your previous protection there.

4. To work in the Netherlands  
You can work only if:
- you are covered by the Temporary Protection Directive in the Netherlands, and
- you have proof of residency from the IND, such as a sticker or card

Important:
- a BSN number alone is not enough to work
- you cannot work with only a BSN if you do not yet have the sticker
- you should be registered as a resident in the BRP to qualify for temporary protection in the Netherlands

5. If another country refuses to let you switch because you are already registered elsewhere  
The documents say that if you registered in one country and decide to move to another, you should inform the authorities in the country where you are currently registered. The new country should then register you and offer temporary protection and the related rights.

6. If you are not eligible for temporary protection in the Netherlands  
You may need to look at other residence options or international protection instead.

Best next step:
- first check whether you qualify in the Netherlands
- then contact the IND directly for your specific case

The documents say it is always best to contact the IND or an immigration lawyer for case-specific questions.

If you want, I can also help you go through the Dutch eligibility rules step by step.

bot_output:

- The documents say that if you are covered by the Temporary Protection Directive, you keep your right to reception.

- I don’t know from the provided information whether VWN can help move you to another shelter.

user_input: I just arrived from Ukraine after November 2021 and I don't know where to go for shelter or healthcare. How do I register for temporary protection? I'm really lost and scared.
bot_output:
I’m sorry you’re going through this. If you came from Ukraine and left after 26 November 2021, you may have a right to shelter and Temporary Protection in the Netherlands.

What to do now:
1. Go to a municipality (“gemeente”) in the city where you are now or where you will stay.
2. Ask to register for the BRP (Basic Registration of Persons) and for help with shelter.
3. If the municipality has space, they will help with housing. If not, they should contact the regional/national coordination system to look for a place.
4. After BRP registration, you need an appointment with the IND for a residence sticker. This appointment should be scheduled within 4 weeks after BRP registration.
5. Once registered and covered by Temporary Protection, you are entitled to accommodation, a living allowance, healthcare, and education for children. You may also work.

Important:
- If possible, try to arrange a place to stay yourself first, because shelter places are very limited.
- You need a local address (accommodation) to apply for Temporary Protection.
- If you cannot find a place yourself, still go to the municipality and ask for help.
- If possible, ask the municipality for written confirmation of your visit.

Healthcare:
- Basic healthcare and urgent medical care are covered for displaced persons from Ukraine.
- If you have a BSN, you are covered by the Medical Care for Displaced Persons Regulation (RMO).
- You only need Dutch health insurance if you start working in the Netherlands.

Useful links:
- Step-by-step guide: https://www.refugeehelp.nl/en/ukrainian-refugee/article/100040-this-is-what-you-should-do-if-you-have-temporary-protection

- Red Cross info: https://www.rodekruis.nl/english-information/

If you want, I can also help you with a very simple “what to say at the municipality” message in English or Dutch.

user_input: I need help with school for my 10 year old kid, we are from Ukraine and under TPD. What do I need to register her in Rotterdam? Is there any language support? I feel lost and worried.
bot_output:
Yes — your child can go to school in the Netherlands.

For a 10-year-old, this applies regardless of residence status, and children in the Netherlands have the right to education. You can register your child at any school, and the school decides on admission.

For Rotterdam:
- The Rotterdam HUB is closed for general intake due to overcrowding.
- Exception: they still assist Ukrainians with a connection to Rotterdam or the surrounding region, for example if children already go to school there.
- Address: Marten Meesweg 141B, Rotterdam
- Email: opvang@rotterdam.nl
- Opening times:
  - Monday–Tuesday: 10:00–15:00
  - Wednesday–Friday: 10:00–14:00
  - Saturday–Sunday: closed

Language support:
- Yes. There are special intermediary classes where children can first learn Dutch.
- If the municipality has not arranged school yet, this can take a few days or sometimes a few weeks depending on the municipality.

While waiting, the documents suggest starting self-study in English and Dutch. Some mentioned apps are:
- Gramaro
- LingQ
- Drops
- Busuu

Extra help in Rotterdam:
- You can also visit Vraagwijzer for free help and advice about administration, parenting, laws, money, or health.

Useful links:

  - https://www.government.nl/topics/reception-of-refugees-from-ukraine/education
  - https://www.refugeehelp.nl/en/ukrainian-refugee/article/100007-education-for-children-from-ukraine-who-cannot-speak-dutch-yet

You are not alone, and your child does have the right to education here.

user_input: I want to start an internship but I don't have proof from IND yet. Can you tell me what I need to do? Also, I am worried about where I can stay and if I can get help with food while I wait.
bot_output:
To start an internship, you first need proof from the IND that you are covered by the Temporary Protection Directive.

What you need to do:
- Register in the BRP at the municipality where you are staying.
- After that, make an appointment with the IND to collect your proof of residency.
- You should make this appointment within 4 weeks after BRP registration.
- Without an IND sticker or card, you cannot work yet. Based on the information provided, this also means you cannot start the internship yet.
- For an internship, once you have the proof, you can show the sticker or O-document from the IND. Then the internship provider does not need a work permit.
- You, the employer, and the training institution must sign an internship agreement.

About staying somewhere and getting help while you wait:
- If you cannot find a place to stay yourself, go to a municipality to ask for help and to register.
- The municipality may help with housing if there is space. If not, they can contact regional or national coordination for shelter.
- The Dutch government asks people to find their own housing if possible because shelter places are limited.
- According to the documents, refugees from Ukraine are entitled to accommodation, a subsistence allowance, healthcare and education after they are registered in the BRP and get a residence sticker from the IND.
- Another document says only after you get the IND sticker you can get living allowance and are allowed to work and live in the Netherlands.

So in short:
1. Register at the municipality (BRP).
2. Ask the municipality for shelter if you do not have a place to stay.
3. Make an IND appointment for proof of residency.
4. After you receive the IND proof, you can start your internship and may get living allowance.

If you want, I can also help you with the exact steps for making the IND appointment.
