["Document: Can I do an internship in the Netherlands?

Displaced persons covered by the Ukraine Temporary Protection Directive are allowed to do an internship for training.  

A displaced person can demonstrate that they are covered by the Temporary Protection Directive with a sticker or O document (officially: the Alien Identity Document model 2014) from the Immigration and Naturalization Service (IND).

The internship provider then does not need a work permit (officially: work permit).

Displaced persons can make an appointment to collect proof of residence from the IND.  

The intern, employer and training must conclude an internship agreement.  

For the most recent information, see: https://www.rijksoverheid.nl/onderwerpen/opvang-vluchtelingen-uit-oekraine/werk-en-inkomen", "Document: I want to work but did not yet receive a document that states that the Temporary Protection Directive applies to me, what can I do?  

Without a sticker or card from the IND as a proof of residency you cannot yet work.

If you fall under the Temporary Protection Directive but do not have a sticker or card yet, please make an appointment with the IND.   

For most recent information see: https://ind.nl/en/ukraine/temporary-protection-directive-ukraine#working-and-studying-in-the-netherlands", "Document: How does the appointment to collect my proof of residency work and what do I have to fill in?  

At the pickup location, an IND staff member will check:  - your registration with the local council/municipality - your appointment code - your documents - whether you fall under the Temporary Protection Directive.  

You must fill in 2 IND forms during your appointment.

At the reception location you will find a translation of both forms into Ukrainian, Russian and English.

There are also employees who can help you fill in these forms.

They speak Ukrainian, Russian or English.   

Form 1: Asylum application (applicable for age => 15): The official asylum application (minors – together with parents on the form).  

Form 2: Antecedents certificate (applicable for age => 12): On this certificate, you state whether you have ever committed a punishable offence or crime.   

Because you are covered by the Temporary Protection Directive, your rights will be different to those of the standard asylum application.

You can work in the Netherlands immediately.

The IND will not assess your application for asylum while the directive is in force.

The directive will apply at least until 4 March 2027.", "Document: What can I do and which support can I get after I register for the Basic Registration of Persons (BRP)?

[RefugeeHelp](https://www.refugeehelp.nl/nl/ukrainian-refugee/article/100040-dit-moet-je-doen-als-je-tijdelijke-bescherming-hebt)", "Document: Extension of proof of residency Do you have a sticker or card valid until 4 March 2023, 2024, or 2025?

user_input: I just got evicted after my protection ended and I have nowhere to stay. Is there any emergency shelter I can go to? I'm really scared and don't know what to do.
bot_output:
I’m sorry you’re going through this.

If you are in immediate danger, call 112.

From the information I have:
- You can contact Veilig Thuis (Safe at Home) at 0800-2000.
- If you no longer have a safe place to stay, you can go to an emergency shelter of the municipality.
- If you fled because of domestic or relationship violence, the crisis shelter “Blijf van mijn Lijf-huis” may help. Call 0800 0117 for free.

For more information, see the answer to the next question ("If I am Ukrainian but excluded from the tempory protection, what is the procedure?")", "Document: You can read more information about the Temporary Protection Directive and the criteria here:  - https://www.refugeehelp.nl/en/ukrainian-refugee/article/100187-conditions-of-temporary-protection-directive  - https://ind.nl/en/ukraine/temporary-protection-directive-ukraine - https://www.government.nl/topics/reception-of-refugees-from-ukraine/third-country-nationals", "Document: Where can I find shelter when arriving in the Netherlands?

Click on the following links for the [English](https://www.rodekruis.nl/english-information/), [Ukrainian](https://www.rodekruis.nl/ukrainian/) and the [Russian](https://www.rodekruis.nl/russian/) version of this webpage.

2.

If PA needs help with finding shelter, please know that the situation is currently very difficult and becoming more restricted.   

3.", "Document: When will I be covered by the Temporary Protection Directive?

You will be covered by the directive in the Netherlands if one of the following situations applies to you:

user_input: I have temporary protection and want to start freelancing, but I'm not sure what permit I need or if it's allowed. Can you help me? Also, I'm worried about finding a place to stay and food while I figure this out.
bot_output:
Yes — if you have Temporary Protection in the Netherlands, freelancing/self-employment is **not automatically allowed**.

What the documents say:
- You can work **without a work permit** only if you work **for an employer with an employment contract**.
- If you want to work as a **freelancer / self-employed person / ZZP**, a **TWV (work permit)** is required.
- You may only work as self-employed if:
  - **you have an employment permit for entrepreneurs**, or
  - **the contracting party/client has a TWV**.
- You can register a company with the **KvK** if you are registered in the **BRP**, but that does **not** mean you may start working as self-employed without the permit.
- The documents also say the **UWV rarely grants** this permit, especially for work that does not require special qualifications.
- In addition, **your client/customer must apply for a new TWV for each assignment**.

About staying somewhere and food:
- If you are covered by the Temporary Protection Directive, you have a right to **reception/shelter**.
- You should report to the **municipality where you are registered** and ask for a place in the **municipal reception facilities**.
- If there is no room there, the municipality contacts the **safety region** to look for a place.
- If you are in a **public shelter**, you can receive **living allowance** from the municipality where you are registered.
- This support may be given through a **bank account, money card, cash, or goods**.
- In some municipalities, support may partly be given **in kind**, for example through **meals**, so the amount of money can differ.

Important:
- To work in the Netherlands under Temporary Protection, you need proof of residency from the **IND** (a **sticker or card**). Without that, you cannot work yet.

If you want, I can help you figure out the next best option between:
1. working for an employer,
2. trying to register a company,
3. asking your municipality about shelter and living allowance.

Everyone who comes under the Temporary Protection Directive can work in the Netherlands without a work permit (in Dutch: tewerkstellingsvergunning or twv).

This means that an employer does not have to request a work permit for you.

(in EN, UKR, RU, NL).", "Document: If you register as a “non-resident” in RNI, you are not qualified for temporary protection in The Netherlands.

You can find a few options for you after your protection status changes below", "Document: Public shelter If you are covered by the Temporary Protection Directive, you keep your right to reception.

The reception is a joint responsibility of all Dutch municipalities and Safety Regions.

- Email: **empatia@oporafoundation.nl**
- Contact form: https://empatiaprogram.nl/looking-for-help#contact-us

If you remain in the Netherlands without residency status, you are undocumented. However, you still have the right to necessary medical care.

bot_output:

user_input: I feel really sick but I don't have any papers or insurance. Can I still get urgent medical help? I'm scared they won't help me.
bot_output:
Yes. You can still get urgent and necessary medical care in the Netherlands, even if you do not have papers or insurance.

What to do:
- If it is life-threatening, call 112 immediately.
- If it is urgent but not life-threatening, you can go to a doctor or the huisartsenpost.

Important:
- Everyone has the right to medically necessary care.
- Undocumented people still have the right to necessary medical care.
- If you are uninsured, you can still get medical help. The healthcare provider may be able to use a special subsidy for uninsured people.

If you want, I can also help explain how to find a GP or huisartsenpost near you.

user_input: I don't have insurance and I need to see a doctor. Are there clinics or places I can go? I don't have much money and I'm really worried.
bot_output:
I’m sorry you’re worried. You have the right to see a doctor and get necessary medical care.

In the Netherlands, if you need medical help, you should usually go to a General Practitioner (GP) first. The GP can refer you to a specialist or hospital if needed.

If you are staying with a host family:
- First check whether you can go to your host’s GP.
- If that is not possible, ask the municipality where you are staying which GP nearby can help you.
- You can also look for a GP in your area on:
  - https://www.kiesuwhuisarts.nl/
  - https://www.zorgkaartnederland.nl/huisarts?zoekterm=huisarts.

If you are staying in an emergency shelter:
- Contact the medical facilities there.
- The shelter may know which services are available, for example Doctors of the World sometimes visits emergency shelters.

You can get medical help even if you are uninsured. This is reimbursed through a special subsidy. Sometimes GPs do not know this, and they can be referred to the CAK website:
- https://www.hetcak.nl/zakelijk/regelingen/regeling-onverzekerden/subsidie-aanvragen/aanvraag

If it is evening or urgent:
- If it cannot wait until the next day, you can go to the huisartsenpost.
- In an emergency, call 112 or go to the nearest hospital emergency room.

If you want, tell me:
1. which city or postcode you are in, and
2. whether you are with a host family or in a shelter,

and I can help you figure out the best place to start.

bot_output:
I’m sorry to hear that.

If you are in immediate danger, call 112.

If you fled because of domestic or relationship violence:
- The crisis shelter “Stay away from my Body” can help.
- Call free: 0800 0117

About what to watch out for in different places:
The information I have says that in the Netherlands there can be different unsafe situations than you may be used to, for example:
- Near water
- Near railroad lines
- In nature, including poisonous mushrooms
- Ticks

More information:
- https://www.mycoa.nl/en/the-netherlands
- https://www.refugeehelp.nl/get-help/category/safety

user_input: It's freezing and I don't have warm clothes. What kind of clothing should I look for to stay warm? I don't know much about materials or insulation.
bot_output:
To stay warm in freezing weather, look for clothing that traps heat in layers:

- **Base layer (next to skin):** choose **wool** or **synthetic thermal materials**. These help keep warmth in.  
- **Middle layer:** look for **fleece, wool, or down/synthetic insulated sweaters or jackets**. These provide insulation.  
- **Outer layer:** choose a **windproof and waterproof coat** to protect from cold wind and wet weather.

Also important:
- **Warm socks**: wool or thermal socks
- **Hat**: a lot of heat can be lost through your head
- **Gloves**
- **Scarf**
- **Warm shoes or boots**

If you also need help finding clothes, the Red Cross Helpful Information website has clothing support options in different cities:
- https://helpfulinformation.redcross.nl/
- For recent clothing support or low-cost clothes: https://www.refugeehelp.nl/en/marketplace

If it is permitted, it is stated in the APV (general municipal bylaw) of the municipality.

In life-threatening emergencies, call the national emergency number 112 immediately.

Don't speak English or Dutch?

Then it's best to contact the front desk directly.   

What else to do in case of fire:   - If the fire is small and there is a fire extinguisher nearby, you can try to extinguish the fire yourself with it.   

- If the fire is in a pan or garbage can, you can put out the fire by putting a lid on it.   

- Keep windows and doors closed.   

- Leave the building as quickly as possible.

If the ice is thick enough you can walk and skate on it.    

If the ice is not thick enough you can fall through it.

This is very dangerous.

You can get hypothermia, drown or even die.   

Only go out on the ice if you are sure it is thick enough.

Also, never go out on the ice alone.

Call for help if someone has fallen through the ice or call 112 in a life-threatening situation.

user_input: I feel really hopeless and lost, I don't know what to do next. Can you help me with what I should do first?
bot_output:
I’m really sorry you’re feeling this way. You don’t have to figure it all out at once.

A good first step is to focus only on the next 10 minutes:
1. Move somewhere a little safer or calmer if you can.
2. Take 5 slow breaths.
3. Text or call one person you trust and say: “I’m having a really hard time and I don’t want to be alone right now.”
4. Drink a glass of water.
5. Avoid making any big decisions tonight.

If you might hurt yourself or feel like you may act on these feelings, call emergency services now or go to the nearest emergency room. If you can, contact a crisis line in your country right away.

If you want, reply with just one word:
- “safe” if you’re safe right now
- “unsafe” if you’re in immediate danger
- or tell me your country, and I’ll help you think about the next step.

If you tell me your location, I can help point you to the nearest registration point mentioned in the information.

If you remain in the Netherlands without residency status, you do not have rights to housing, work, or government subsidies, but you do still have the right to necessary medical care.

https://wa.me/31614458781

user_input: I feel so tired all the time, and it suddenly got worse. Is there anywhere I can go for help or to find out what's wrong? I don't know what to do.
bot_output:
I’m sorry you’re feeling this way.

You always have the right to see a doctor and get necessary medical care in the Netherlands. For Ukrainians with temporary protection, the usual first step is to visit a General Practitioner (GP). The GP can assess what is wrong and, if needed, refer you to a specialist or hospital.

If this is during working hours:
- If you are staying with a host family, first check whether you can go to your host’s GP.
- If that is not possible, ask the municipality where you are staying which GP nearby can help you.
- If you are in an emergency shelter, contact the medical facilities there. The shelter usually knows what care is available.

If this is in the evening, at night, or on the weekend:
- For urgent questions, contact the huisartsenpost (GP out-of-hours service):
  https://www.zorgkaartnederland.nl/huisartsenpost

If it is an emergency:
- Call 112 or go to the Emergency Room in the nearest hospital.

You can also get medical help if you are uninsured; this can be reimbursed through a special subsidy.

I can’t give medical advice about what your symptoms mean, but I can help you find the right option in the Dutch healthcare system. If you tell me:
- where you are staying, and
- whether it is urgent or during office hours,

I can help you figure out the best next step.

user_input: I am Ukrainian and just arrived after November 2021. Can you tell me how to register for shelter and if I am allowed to stay? I feel lost and don't know what to do.
bot_output:
Yes. If you have a Ukrainian passport, or a valid permanent Ukrainian residence permit, and you left Ukraine after 26 November 2021, you have the right to shelter and Temporary Protection in the Netherlands.

What to do:
1. Go to a municipality (“gemeente”) in the city where you arrive.
2. Ask to register there for shelter and Temporary Protection.
3. After registration in the BRP, you should get an appointment with the IND within 4 weeks for a residence sticker.

Important:
- You can register at any municipality, sometimes in person and sometimes by email.
- If the municipality has space, they will help with housing.
- If not, they may contact regional or national coordination to look for a place.
- Because shelter places are limited, there is no guarantee of immediate shelter.
- If possible, try to arrange accommodation yourself first.

Please note:
- You need a local address (accommodation) to apply for Temporary Protection.
- If you are staying in a municipal shelter, the municipality will contact you.
- If you stay with private people and want to register there, you usually need to register yourself at the municipality.

Once registered and covered by Temporary Protection, you are entitled to accommodation, a living allowance, healthcare, and education.

A useful step-by-step guide is here:
https://www.refugeehelp.nl/en/ukrainian-refugee/article/100040-this-is-what-you-should-do-if-you-have-temporary-protection

If you want, I can also give you a very short checklist of exactly what to do today.

user_input: I need a place to sleep but I'm confused about the difference between municipal shelters and private places. Can you explain? Which one is easier to get into if I don't have papers?
bot_output:
Municipal shelters are public shelters arranged by Dutch municipalities. If you are covered by the Temporary Protection Directive, you can ask the municipality where you are registered for a place in municipal reception. If there is no room, the municipality works with the safety region to try to find a place elsewhere.

Private places are accommodation you arrange yourself, for example with a host family, friends, family members, or by renting a place.

About “if I don’t have papers”: the information I have only says that if you remain in the Netherlands without residency status, you become undocumented. Undocumented persons do not have a right to housing, work, or government subsidies, though they still have a right to necessary medical care, legal assistance, and children under 18 have the right to attend school.

So based on the information I have, I can explain the difference, but I don’t know which option is easier to get into if you do not have papers.

I’m sorry you’re going through this.

If you are in the Netherlands and need shelter, the main advice is:

- Go to any municipality office (“gemeente”).

- After registration, the municipality will help with housing if they have space.
- If they do not have space, they can contact the regional or national coordination system for refugee shelter.

Important:
- Because shelter places are very limited, the Dutch government asks people to try to find housing themselves if possible.
- If you cannot find a place yourself, go to the municipality for help.
- It is a good idea to ask the municipality for written confirmation of your visit.
- If they cannot help immediately, ask whether they can offer a temporary solution while they look for a place for you.

You can also check updated shelter information here:
- Red Cross information page (English): https://www.rodekruis.nl/english-information/
- RefugeeHelp shelter information: https://www.refugeehelp.nl/en/ukrainian-refugee/109-shelter

user_input: I just arrived from Ukraine and I don't know what to do for shelter or how to get Temporary Protection. Can you help me with the steps? I'm really confused.
bot_output:
Yes — if you have a Ukrainian passport or a valid permanent Ukrainian residence permit, and you can prove you left Ukraine after 26 November 2021, you have the right to shelter and Temporary Protection in the Netherlands.

What to do:
1. Go to a municipality (“gemeente”) in the city where you are staying or arriving.
2. Ask to register and apply for Temporary Protection.
3. If you need shelter, tell the municipality that you need accommodation.
4. If the municipality has space, they can help you directly. If not, they may contact the regional or national coordination system for shelter.
5. You need a local address/accommodation to apply for Temporary Protection.
6. After registration in the BRP, you should get an appointment with the IND within 4 weeks to receive a residence sticker.

Important:
- The housing situation is very difficult now, and shelter places are limited.
- If possible, try to arrange a place to stay yourself, even temporarily.
- If you are staying in a municipal shelter, the municipality will contact you.
- If you are staying with private people and want to register there, you usually need to register yourself at the city hall or according to your municipality’s website.

If you contact a municipality by email or WhatsApp, your message should include:
- that this is an application for Temporary Protection
- whether you need accommodation
- your full name
- date of birth
- date you left Ukraine
- photo of your passport/documents
- details of family members traveling with you
- any special needs

- Red Cross information: https://www.rodekruis.nl/english-information/

For **crisis emergency shelters**, the documents say they should provide:
- **Cleaning supplies**
- **Clothes (seasonal)**
- **Goods hygiene**
- **Meals (or dining money)**
- **Beds and basic items**

- **Third party insurance**

One document also mentions, based on Red Cross standards for shelter, items such as:
- **Washing up liquid**
- **Washing machine detergent**
- **Locker**
- **Clothing and shoes**

user_input: I have a car from Ukraine and I don't know how to get insurance here. Can you help me? Also, is there anything I need to know about driving it safely?
bot_output:
Yes. Many cars from Ukraine are only insured within Ukraine, so if you use your car in the Netherlands, you need to take out separate car insurance here.

You can find the most recent information here:
https://www.refugeehelp.nl/en/ukrainian-refugee/article/100128-having-your-own-car-in-the-netherlands

About driving:
- You may drive in the Netherlands if you have a valid driving licence.
- Ukrainian driving licences of people covered by the Temporary Protection Directive are valid throughout the EU.
- This also applies to all licence categories (A, B, C, D).
- Expired Ukrainian two-year initial driving licences are also accepted if they were automatically renewed by the Ukrainian government during the state of emergency.
- Driving licences in Cyrillic script are also valid.

If your driving licence is lost or stolen, you are not allowed to drive at the moment.

More information:
- https://www.rijksoverheid.nl/onderwerpen/opvang-vluchtelingen-uit-oekraine/aankomst-verblijf-en-registratie
- https://www.europarl.europa.eu/news/en/press-room/20220701IPR34341/ukrainians-can-keep-their-driving-licences-in-the-eu-say-meps
- https://eu-solidarity-ukraine.ec.europa.eu/information-people-fleeing-war-ukraine_en#onward-travel-in-the-eu

If you want, I can also help you with what documents or steps to check next.

user_input: I need shoes but I'm not sure if I should ask at the crisis shelter or the Red Cross. Is there a difference in how they help with clothing? I feel embarrassed asking.
bot_output:
You can ask for help with clothing, including shoes.

From the information I have:

- In a **crisis emergency shelter**, **clothing and shoes** should be available.
- The **Red Cross Helpful Information website** also gives an overview of clothing support in different cities:  
  https://helpfulinformation.redcross.nl/
- For recent initiatives that offer clothes or low-cost clothes, you can also check:  
  https://www.refugeehelp.nl/en/marketplace

About the difference:

- The documents say that **crisis emergency shelters should have clothing and shoes available**.
- The Red Cross can also help by **connecting you to available help**, and their website lists clothing options by city.
- I do not have information saying the Red Cross directly provides clothing everywhere in the same way a shelter might.

So if you are staying in a crisis shelter, it makes sense to **ask the shelter staff first**. You can also use the Red Cross clothing information website to find other places nearby.

And please don’t feel embarrassed—asking for basic things like shoes is completely okay.

The shelters themselves are better aware of this.

This is reimbursed by means of a special subsidy.

Sometimes GPs don't know this.

but they don't need to understand it themselves.", "Document: What is the difference between crisis emergency shelters and emergency shelters?

Below you will find more information on what facilities should be present at the different types of reception.

The Red Cross does not influence the placement in the shelters.

This is done by the municipalities.

Therefore, the Red Cross cannot assist you with changing locations.  

Unfortunately, the housing situation is really tough in the Netherlands.

If you live in a municipal shelter already, it is nearly impossible to change from one municipal shelter to a different municipal shelter.   

You could always try to arrange new accommodation by yourself.

Although this is very difficult, you could check this website for example: https://www.funda.nl/en/huur/. You could also register with the housing corporation in the municipality of your choice to find housing.

Hopefully, you will find some suitable options for you.  

If you do have urgent reasons for relocating (e.g. medical reasons), you could request to change shelters.

First, check if there is a place available in the shelter of your choice.

If this is the case, you can request resettlement at the municipality.", "Document: I want to go to a dentist, can you help me?  

If you need to go to the dentist or need other oral care you can go to the service desk of your municipality.

They can refer you to a practitioner.  

In case of acute emergencies you can, in principle, go to any dental practice in the Netherlands.

This usually costs a maximum of €250.  

If you give us your location we can check if we have any information on dentists close to you that offer help to displaced persons from Ukraine and contact them directly.  

For an overview of all the important information on dental care for displaced persons from Ukraine see: https://knmt.nl/praktijkzaken/bijzondere-doelgroepen/vluchtelingen-uit-oekraine  Please note: if you stay in a crisis emergency shelter (CNO), the dental visit is sometimes postponed until you are placed somewhere where you can stay for longer.

If you have fever, an attempt is made to urgently schedule an appointment near the CNO.", "Document: If this is the case, you can request resettlement at the municipality.

For more information, talk with the management of your shelter location, or go to the municipality.

Please note that your request may not be honored.", "Document: What to do (as a receptionist/aid worker) when a displaced person from Ukraine reports at an NLRC office?  

Explanation of situation: Since the end of February 2024, the shelters for displaced people from Ukraine are (almost) full.

Most of the registration locations are closed, which makes it confusing for people arriving to the Netherlands where to go.

It might happen that someone therefore is going to an office of the Red Cross to ask for help.

Below, you can find the most important steps to take in order to help someone on their way.   

Step 1: try to find out:  - If the person has Ukrainian nationality or a permanent residence permit for Ukraine?

- Check where this person has already been, did they just arrive?  

- Are they already registered in a municipality (BRP)?  

- Did they try another option to find shelter before going to NLRC office?   

Step 2: contact CHV shelter / someone from the shelter program: - If you are in an office in the district: contact the CHV specifically for shelter.

You can find a list of the CHV'ers", "Document: What is the stance of the Red Cross when somebody is not helped at HSP?  

We do our best to ensure that people arriving at an Humanitarian Service Point (HSP) are directed to the most appropriate form of assistance for them.

This could mean that people are directed to Ter Apel, rather than assistance being provided at the HSP.

However, we try to ensure that all refugees have their basic needs met, i.e. they can have some food and a drink, rest and charge mobile devices before travelling onwards.", "Document: Will I receive medical care if I have an asylum application pending?

Per 4 March 20224, the Regulation on Medical Care for Displaced Persons from Ukraine (RMO) expires for the third-country nationals.

The group with an asylum application will then fall under the Asylum seekers Medical Care Arrangement (RMA).

The content of these schemes is similar.", "Document: Are medical costs reimbursed?

Displaced persons from Ukraine are entitled to necessary medical care.  

From 1 July 2022 displaced persons with a "BSN" (a citizen service number) fall under a scheme called "Regeling Medische zorg Ontheemden (RMO)".

They do not have to pay insurance premium.

Also, they do not have to pay the initial part of medical costs ("eigen risico").   -

For a factsheets about healthcare costs see [here](https://assets.ctfassets.net/496uch1l97fc/5hVD9GrO4bXepzCtI08NRJ/7a95dd80fe66b727d4951adc3e6ad28c/factsheet-zorgkosten-oekrainers-oekraiens.pdf) -

For an overview of terms and forms about the insurance see [here](https://www.rmoekraine.nl/Verzekerden/formulieren) -

For more information about RMO see [here](https://www.rmoekraine.nl/Zorgverleners/over-RMO) -", "Document: Do I need health insurance?

For displaced persons from Ukraine, basic healthcare and urgent medical care are covered.

As of 1 July 2022, displaced persons from Ukraine with a BSN will be covered by the Medical Care for Displaced Persons Regulation (RMO).

For more information about RMO see: https://www.rmoekraine.nl/Zorgverleners/over-RMO  You do need to take out health insurance when you start working in the Netherlands.   

For most recent information see:  https://www.refugeehelp.nl/en/ukrainian-refugee/article/100084-you-are-entitled-to-healthcare-through-the-rmo  https://www.rijksoverheid.nl/actueel/nieuws/2022/06/29/zorgverzekering-ontheemden-oekraine-verandert", "Document: Requesting shelter upon arrival in the NL as required by Dutch law.

*Cited directly from the Dutch government website*:  It is very difficult at the moment for local authorities to arrange accomodation.

The authorities’ priority is to ensure accommodation for the most vulnerable refugees.

Refugees from Ukraine who are able to, are being asked to make every effort to find a place of residence by themselves.

This applies to both refugees who have been in the Netherlands for some time and new arrivals.

If not possible to find a place of residence, please report to a municipality to ask for help and to register.  

In order to be covered by the Temporary Protection Directive, refugees from Ukraine need to be registered in the Personal Records Database (BRP) and get a residence sticker from the Immigration and Naturalisation Service (IND).

The appointment with the IND should be scheduled within 4 weeks from the date of the registration in the BRP.

Refugees from Ukraine are then entitled to accommodation, a subsistence allowance, healthcare and education.   

[*Dutch Government website*](https://www.government.nl/topics/reception-of-refugees-from-ukraine/arrival-registration-and-stay)", "Document: Is dental care reimbursed?  

This depends on your situation.  

Below is an overview of dental services that are covered by the insurance for Ukrainian displaced persons (RMO):   Conditions for providing dental care to Ukrainian displaced persons:  i.

The clinic can help patients living (registered) within a radius of 50 km from the clinic.  ii.

The patient must make an appointment through the special organization Tandartslijn (tel. 0881122112).  

iii.

If necessary, the clinic must provide proof of the record and argue the urgency (urgent necessity) of providing assistance.  

iv.

These conditions apply to adults and children.  

v. Compensation for adults

is limited to an amount of 250 euros per year and the choice of treatment - elimination of emergency pain with minimal costs.  

vi.

The amount of treatment is not limited to children under 18 years of age.

The only limitation is the exclusion of orthodontic treatment and prosthetics with implants and porcelain-ceramic crowns.   

The following types of dental services are covered by the RMO scheme:  i. Non-Periodic Review Consultation  ii.", "Document: Who is helped at Humanitarian Service Points?  

Below you will find an overview of who is helped at the different HSPs.

There will also be a more in-depth explanation for special cases.", "Document: How can I get financial support while I'm in a public shelter?

You get your living allowance from the municipality where you are registered.

You receive the money in their bank account, on a money card, in cash or in goods.  

Living allowance may be payed out in kind by local authorities (for example when meals are offered).

As a result, it is possible that displaced persons in some municipalities receive (much) less living allowance.   

For most recent information see:  https://www.government.nl/topics/reception-of-refugees-from-ukraine/work-and-income", "Document: Can I stay in the shelter with my pet?  

Yes, you can.

However, please note that centers are overcrowded, and space for pets is very limited.

Availability depends on the municipality.

Therefore it is very possible that there is no place for you and the pet together.  

For most recent information see: https://www.refugeehelp.nl/en/ukrainian-refugee/article/100049-pets"]

user_input: I am Ukrainian and need to find a place to rent, but I don't have much money. Are there any cheap private rentals? Will this change my living allowance? I'm really worried about losing support.
bot_output:
Yes, you can rent a house from private individuals.

But in general, housing in the Netherlands is expensive because there is a large housing shortage, especially in bigger cities. I don’t have information saying there are specific cheap private rentals available.

Places where private homes are offered:
- Funda
- Airbnb
- Marktplaats
- Facebook groups per city, for example by searching “I’m looking for a home”

About your living allowance:
- If you stay in a shelter location, including a municipal shelter or private shelter/host family, you can receive living allowance.
- If you rent your own independent accommodation, you are no longer entitled to living allowance.

So yes, renting your own place can change your support: it means your living allowance stops.

For the most recent information:
- RefugeeHelp on permanent housing: https://www.refugeehelp.nl/en/ukrainian-refugee/article/100045-permanent-housing
- RefugeeHelp on renting a house: https://www.refugeehelp.nl/en/ukrainian-refugee/article/100047-this-is-what-you-need-to-arrange-if-you-rent-a-house

If you want, I can also help you compare the difference between staying with a host family, municipal shelter, and renting your own place.

["Document: Can I rent a house?  

You can rent a house from private individuals.

In general, houses are expensive, because there is a large housing shortage in the Netherlands, especially in the larger cities.   

As a displaced person from Ukraine, you will receive living allowance when you stay at a shelter location, both in the municipal shelter and in the private shelter.

If you rent your own independent accommodation, you are no longer entitled to living allowance.  

Places where private homes are offered: Funda, AirBNB, Marktplaats website, Facebook groups per city (search for 'I'm looking for a home').   

For most recent information see: [RefugeeHelp](https://www.refugeehelp.nl/en/ukrainian-refugee/article/100045-permanent-housing)  and [renting a house](https://www.refugeehelp.nl/en/ukrainian-refugee/article/100047-this-is-what-you-need-to-arrange-if-you-rent-a-house)", "Document: What financial arrangements are there for displaced persons from Ukraine?  

You get the living allowance from the municipality where you are registered.

You get the money in your bank account, on a money card, in cash or in goods (this means it is possible that in some municipalities you will get (much) less living allowance if you are provided with food and goods in a public shelter).  

- The specific amounts per family situation can be found here: https://www.rijksoverheid.nl/onderwerpen/opvang-vluchtelingen-uit-oekraine/nieuws/2023/08/31/indexering-financiele-toelages-vluchtelingen-uit-oekraine-per-1-oktober  - A factsheet is available in Dutch, English and Ukrainian explaining the main points of the subsistence allowance, including amounts and conditions.", "Document: How can I get financial support while I'm at a host family?  

You receive your living allowance from the municipality where you are registered.

You get the money in their bank account, money card, cash or goods.  

This money can be used for things like public transport, family visits or sports.

You can also use the money to contribute to the costs of the host family, but this is not an obligation.  

If a host family takes in more than one refugee, they are each entitled to a living allowance.

There is no maximum amount per host family.  

For the most recent information see: https://www.government.nl/topics/reception-of-refugees-from-ukraine/work-and-income   https://www.refugeehelp.nl/en/ukrainian-refugee/article/100051-living-allowance", "Document: How can I get financial support while I'm in a public shelter?

You get your living allowance from the municipality where you are registered.

Starting July 1st 2024, displaced people from Ukraine with a job or their own income must help pay for their reception in a municipality.

You will no longer receive a living allowance.   

Displaced people from Ukraine who have to pay:   -are 18 years old and above.

Your living allowance will stop on the first day of the month after you move out or start working.

Members of your family who do not have paid work will still get the subsistence allowance.

You must inform the municipality if you move out of your accommodation or start a paid job.   

For most recent information see:  https://www.government.nl/topics/reception-of-refugees-from-ukraine/work-and-income  https://www.refugeehelp.nl/en/ukrainian-refugee/article/100051-living-allowance", "Document: Do I have to pay for shelter if I have an income?  

Starting July 1st 2024, displaced people from Ukraine with a job or their own income must help pay for their reception in a municipality.

You will no longer receive a living allowance.   

Check the exact amount and rules on [RefugeeHelp](https://www.refugeehelp.nl/nl/ukrainian-refugee/article/100051-leefgeld-en-eigen-financiele-bijdrage-aan-de-opvang-als-je-gevlucht-bent-uit-oekraine)", "Document: Can I travel to Ukraine without losing the temporary protection status?   

Ukrainians who already have a temporary protection and have an urgent reason can travel to Ukraine for urgent matters, such as picking up relatives, transporting belongings, or medical issues, and return to the Netherlands within a few days or weeks.

However, if you stay in Ukraine or another country for an extended period, the IND may look whether you still qualify for temporary protection.

While your status won’t be automatically revoked, you must provide a valid reason for your long absence.  

Important note: If you live in a shelter you may leave the shelter for 14 days per calander year with retention of the reception place and 28 days per calander year with retention of living allowance.

The displaced person must always report his or her departure to a reception staff member.

If the displaced person does not report the departure, they can lose the reception place immediately and the municipality can stop the living allowance immediately.

If you don't live in a shelter, it is still good to always report to the municipality that you are going to Ukraine for a period of time.", "Document: I or a family member is coming to the Netherlands for a temporary visit, can I use the municipal shelter and services for displaced persons from Ukraine?

Are you or your family member passing through the Netherlands or visiting relatives?

Then you cannot make use of the municipal shelter for Ukrainian displaced persons and you are not entitled to an allowance.

You cannot spend the night in the municipal shelter.

However, you can visit or receive visitors at the shelter.

Make sure you are familiar with the location's visitor rules.  

You or your family member can, of course, make arrangements with the host family if you make use of private reception.

A host family is not obliged to accommodate family visits.", "Document: Website about financial support for Ukrainians during the war https://www.enableme.com.ua/ua/article/grosova-dopomoga-ukraincam-pid-cas-vijni-7738", "Document: What does this mean for Ukrainian individuals seeking a place to live?

The housing for Ukrainian individuals seeking a place to live will now be managed through municipalities.

RefugeeHomeNL will refer people who want to register from this point onward to the government or a municipality (the GOO).", "Document: ) - Facebook group Ukraine - NL Werk En aanbod / Work

And Offer (you can post job ads in any language) - https://banenvooroekrainers.nl/uk/  (in Ukrainian) - https://randstad.talent-pool.com/  (there is a version of the site in Ukrainian) - a special platform for Ukrainians that can help you find a job in Europe.

You register, define your skills, knowledge, and then they try to find a job for you.

- www.refugeestartforce.eu is an agency with a small number of vacancies, but with the maximum desire to help Ukrainians in their plight.", "Document: Abroad  General advise If you’re coming to the Netherlands with a Ukrainian passport/valid permanent Ukrainian residence permit and proof you left Ukraine after November 26, 2021, you have a right to Shelter & Temporary Protection.

To apply, visit the municipality office in the city where you will arrive.

Actions to take when general advise is not sufficient If the PA shares challenges in finding a place to stay, please consult with the Team Captain.", "Document: For more information in Ukrainian, see: https://open.overheid.nl/repository/ronl-4907d802ea0f813cf0ca978d64d3e64735a071ed/1/pdf/Kinderopvang%20voor%20vluchtelingen%20uit%20Oekra_ne%20_Ukrainian_.pdf", "Document: For most recent information see: https://www.refugeehelp.nl/en/ukrainian-refugee/article/100099-pregnancy", "Document: Can I stay in the public shelter while I have a paid job?  

Displaced persons from Ukraine that are doing paid work may remain at the municipal reception centre.

However, you will have to pay a contribution.

You can also move to other accommodation, for instance with a host family, friends or family members, or at a hotel.  

For most recent information see: https://www.government.nl/topics/reception-of-refugees-from-ukraine/work-and-income", "Document: Can I receive child benefit?  

If you are a displaced person from Ukraine, you are entitled to supplementary child benefit.

Child benefit is a financial contribution to help cover the costs of raising a child.

Whether you are eligible for a benefit and, if so, to what amount, depends on your situation.

If you have one or more children under the age of 18, you may be eligible for child benefit.

The amount you receive depends on the age of your child, not on your income.

You are only eligible for healthcare benefit and supplementary child benefit when you are working.

This is an additional condition for displaced persons from Ukraine.

Because you hold temporary protection status, you are allowed to work in the Netherlands.  

For most recent information see:  https://www.refugeehelp.nl/en/ukrainian-refugee/article/100264-allowances-when-you-have-children", "Document: https://www.refugeehelp.nl/en/ukrainian-refugee/article/100008-studying", "Document: How long can I stay away from the shelter?

Ukrainians may leave reception for 14 days in a calander year with retention of the reception place and 28 days in a calander year with retention of living allowance.

For example, for holidays, family visits or a funeral.

It depends on the municipality how strictly this is enforced.

The PA must always report his or her departure to a reception staff member.

If the PA does not report the departure but leaves longer than 28 days, they can lose the reception place and the municipality can stop the living allowance immediately.", "Document: If the displaced person later returns to the Netherlands, he or she can be given another reception location.

The municipality can stop the living allowance from the Regulations for the Reception of Displaced Persons from Ukraine if the displaced person has left for longer than 28 days.

If refused, contact VluchtelingenWerk Nederland (VWN) for assistance or to file a complaint.   

For more information see:  - https://ind.nl/en/ukraine/residency-non-ukrainians-with-temporary-ukrainian-residence-permit - https://www.refugeehelp.nl/en/ukrainian-refugee/news/100372-you-can-still-stay-in-the-netherlands-if-your-temporary-protection-ended-on-4-march", "Document: How long can I stay away from the shelter?

If you have fled Ukraine, but do not have Ukrainian citizenship, you can no longer make use of the remigration support of the Repatriation & Departure Service (DT&V).

This financial support stopped March 4, 2024.   

Are you a third-country national from Ukraine and do you still want to return to your country of origin or another country outside the European Union?

IOM can assist you with REAN-return support and depending on your nationality you might be eligible for additional reintegration assistance offered by IOM and several non-gouvernemental organisations.  

The IOM offers the following REAN-support and assistance for voluntary return: - Support before, during and after departure consists of return counselling and support to obtain a travel document.

user_input: I am Ukrainian and have kids with me. Is there any crisis shelter where we can stay, with things for children? I really need somewhere safe for us.
bot_output:
Yes. If you do not feel safe, you can go to an emergency shelter of the municipality.

If you fled because of domestic or relationship violence, the crisis shelter “Stay away from my Body” (Blijf van mijn Lijf-huis) can help you. Call for free: 0800 0117.

I don’t have information in the documents about which crisis shelters have children’s facilities specifically. If you share your location, I can help point you to a nearby municipal registration point or emergency shelter.

["Document: Who is responsible for the shelter of children travelling alone from Ukraine?

Children travelling alone from Ukraine also have to go to the municipality to get Temporary Protection.

They always have to get shelter right away.

The municipality has to call with Nidos.

- You can register at any municipality, sometimes in person and sometimes by email.
- After registration, the municipality will help with housing if they have space.
- If the municipality has no space, they contact the regional coordination system, which may be escalated nationally.
- Because there are not enough shelter places, the Dutch government asks Ukrainians to find housing themselves if possible.
- If you cannot find housing yourself, report to the municipality to ask for help and to register.
- It is a good idea to ask the municipality for written confirmation of your visit.
- If they cannot help immediately, ask whether they can offer a temporary solution while they look for a place for you.

- To be covered by the Temporary Protection Directive, you need to be registered in the BRP.
- After BRP registration, your details are automatically shared with the IND.
- You then receive a BSN, which you need for healthcare, education, work, and financial matters.
- The IND appointment for a residence sticker should be scheduled within 4 weeks after BRP registration.

If you are already registered somewhere else in the Netherlands and need public shelter:
- First contact the municipality where you are registered and ask for a place in municipal reception.
- If there is no room, that municipality contacts the safety region.

user_input: I fell through ice and now I'm freezing and scared. What should I do? I feel numb and can't stop shivering.
bot_output:
I’m really sorry this is happening. **This is an emergency. Call emergency services now** or shout for help from anyone nearby.

**Do this immediately:**
- **Get out of the cold/wet** if you can: move to shelter, a car, building, or anywhere out of wind.
- **Remove wet clothes** if possible.
- **Warm the center of your body first**: chest, neck, head, groin.
- **Wrap yourself in dry blankets, coats, towels, or sleeping bags.**
- If you have them, use **warm compresses** on the chest/neck/groin.
- If you are awake and able to swallow, **sip warm sweet drinks**. **Do not drink alcohol.**
- **Do not use hot water, a hot bath, or direct heat** on hands/feet first.
- **Handle yourself gently** and avoid overexertion.

**Get urgent medical help now** because **numbness and uncontrollable shivering can be signs of hypothermia.**

If you’re **still in the water or on weak ice**:
- **Call for help immediately.**
- Try to **kick and pull yourself onto the ice horizontally**.
- Once out, **roll away from the hole** instead of standing up.

If you want, send me your country and I can tell you the emergency number.

user_input: My host won't let me register at their address. What happens now? Is there any other way I can get registered? I'm really worried about losing my shelter.

You can also check whether there is an organization in your town that offers free legal advice about this registration issue.

If you want, tell me your location and I can help you look for a nearby registration point or municipal shelter.

user_input: I'm a minor from Ukraine and I'm alone here. Who can help me find a place to stay? I heard about Nidos but I don't really know what they do.

What they do:
- The **municipality** should first register you.
- If they see that you are **unaccompanied**, they should **contact Nidos immediately**.
- **Nidos** then does an intake with you, and if possible also remotely with your parents.
- They assess whether **temporary guardianship** is needed.
- **Nidos is responsible for arranging shelter** for unaccompanied minors.
- They usually arrange shelter in **host families**, preferably with the same cultural background.

The municipality can contact Nidos via:
- **088-5011885**
- **oekraine@nidos.nl**

Children travelling alone should also get shelter right away.

What is different:
- If you remain in the Netherlands without residency status, you become undocumented.
- Undocumented persons do not have a right to housing, work, or government subsidies.
- But you still have the right to necessary medical care and judicial assistance, and children under 18 have the right to attend school.

About seeing a doctor:
- You always have the right to medically necessary care in the Netherlands.
- First, you should usually go to a General Practitioner (GP). The GP can refer you to a specialist or hospital if needed.

For people with residency:
- If someone receives a regular residence permit, they need to apply for health insurance themselves once they are housed by the municipality as a permit holder.

If you do not apply for asylum or your asylum application is rejected:
- From 4 March 2024, you are responsible for the costs of care yourself.
- If you cannot pay for medically necessary care, the healthcare provider can apply to a support scheme:  
  https://www.hetcak.nl/zakelijk/onverzekerbare-vreemdelingen/

If you want more information, you can contact the Red Cross helpline on WhatsApp:
https://wa.me/31614458781

user_input: Crisis shelters are full and I have nowhere to stay. Where can I find a safe place to sleep and get basic things like food? I'm really worried.
bot_output:
If you are in immediate danger, call **112**.

If you need a safe place to stay, you can go to a **municipal emergency shelter**. The documents say:

- You can always go to an emergency shelter of the municipalities if you no longer want to stay with your host family.
- If you are covered by the **Temporary Protection Directive**, you keep your right to reception.
- First, report to the **municipality where you are registered** and ask for a place in the municipal reception facilities.
- If there is no room there, the municipality contacts the **safety region**.
- If there is still no place, the safety region can request relocation through the **KCIO**.

The Red Cross **cannot place you in a shelter**. Shelter placement is done by the **municipality**.

For domestic or relationship violence, the crisis shelter **“Blijf van mijn Lijf-huis”** may help. Call for free: **0800 0117**.

For safety support, you can also contact **Veilig Thuis (Safe at Home)** at **0800-2000**.

Basic things that should be available in a crisis emergency shelter include:
- **Meals (or dining money)**
- **Beds, mattresses, pillows, blankets**
- **Hygiene goods**
- **Clothes**
- **Cleaning supplies**
- **Wi‑Fi**
- **Charging stations**
- **Access to medical care**

If you share your **location/municipality**, I can help you look for the nearest registration point.

user_input: I don't have a BSN and I'm worried I can't get healthcare. Is it different for people who have a BSN? What can I do if I need a doctor?
bot_output:
You always have the right to medically necessary care in the Netherlands.

For people from Ukraine, there is a difference:
- If you have a BSN, basic healthcare and urgent medical care are covered under the RMO.
- If you do not have a BSN, you can still get medical help if you are uninsured. This is reimbursed through a special subsidy.

If you need a doctor:
- First try a General Practitioner (GP).
- If you are staying with a host family, first ask whether you can go to your host’s GP.
- If that is not possible, ask the municipality where you are staying which nearby GP can help you.
- If you are in an emergency shelter, contact the medical facilities there. The shelter usually knows what care is available.

Sometimes GPs do not know that uninsured care can be reimbursed. In that case, you can show them this CAK website:
https://www.hetcak.nl/zakelijk/regelingen/regeling-onverzekerden/subsidie-aanvragen/aanvraag

If it is urgent in the evening or outside working hours, you can contact the huisartsenpost.
In an emergency, call 112 or go to the nearest hospital emergency room.

user_input: I am Ukrainian and I don't have any ID. Can I still register for BRP? What should I do if I need shelter or help and I don't have documents? Does the embassy help with this stuff? I'm really worried.
bot_output:
Yes — but **not immediately without documents**.

What the information says:

- **Without documents, you currently cannot register for the BRP.**
- If you are **Ukrainian but cannot prove it with an ID card or passport**, you should **contact the Ukrainian Embassy in The Hague**.
- The embassy **may help confirm your identity and nationality**.
- They can issue an **identifying certificate** that can be used to **register for the BRP at the municipality**.

For **children from Ukraine without proof of identification**:
- They can be **registered with their parents at the municipality**.
- If there are no documents, parents can make a **statement on oath** about the child’s identity.

### Embassy contact details
**Ukrainian Embassy in The Hague**  
Zeestraat 78, 2518 AD The Hague  
Open: **Monday to Friday, 09:00–13:00**  
Telephone: **+31 (70) 360 72 18**  
Email: **emb_nl@mfa.gov.ua**  
Website: https://netherlands.mfa.gov.ua/en

### If you need shelter or help
The information says:

- If you **cannot find a place to stay yourself**, you should **go to a municipality and ask for help and to register**.
- You can register at **any municipality**, sometimes in person and sometimes by email.
- After registration, the municipality will help with housing **if they have space**.
- If they do not have space, they may contact the **regional or national shelter coordination system**.

It is also advised to:
- **Ask the municipality for written confirmation** of your visit.
- If they cannot help immediately, **ask whether they can offer a temporary solution** while they look for a place.

### Important note
Another document says you need a **local address (accommodation)** to apply for temporary protection, and housing is currently very limited.

### About the embassy and residence proof
If you do not have a passport or ID card but **do have a statement from the Ukrainian embassy**, that may also help with getting an **O-document** in some cases. The document says this pass **cannot be used for travel**.

For the most recent information:
- IND: https://ind.nl/en/ukraine/temporary-protection-directive-ukraine
- RefugeeHelp: https://www.refugeehelp.nl/en/ukrainian-refugee/article/100151-collecting-your-proof-of-residence

If you want, I can also help you make a **simple step-by-step plan for what to do today**.

user_input: I am from Ukraine and I don't know how to get shelter or register here. Can you help me find a place to stay and tell me how to get basic things like food and healthcare? I feel lost.
bot_output:
Yes — here’s the basic process in the Netherlands for someone displaced from Ukraine:

**1) Go to a municipality (“gemeente”) to register and ask for shelter**
- Municipalities register displaced Ukrainians and help find housing.
- You can register at **any municipality**, sometimes in person or sometimes by email.
- If the municipality has space, they will help you with shelter.
- If not, they can contact the regional/national coordination system for refugee dispersal.

**Important:** Because shelter places are limited, the Dutch government asks people to **find their own housing if possible**. If you cannot, go to the municipality and ask for help.

**2) Ask for proof of your visit**
- It is a good idea to ask the municipality for **written confirmation** of your visit.
- If they cannot help immediately, ask whether they can offer a **temporary solution** while they search for a place.

**3) Registration and Temporary Protection**
- To be covered by the Temporary Protection Directive, you need to be registered in the **BRP (Personal Records Database)** and get a **residence sticker from the IND**.
- The IND appointment should be scheduled **within 4 weeks after BRP registration**.
- Temporary Protection is valid **until at least March 2027**.

**4) Food support**
If you are staying in a **public shelter**, ask someone at the shelter where you can get extra food support.

You can also contact the **Red Cross Food Program Helpdesk**:
- **Phone / text / WhatsApp:** **+31 97010259797**
- **Hours:** **Mon–Fri, 9:00–17:00**

Also, **Voedselbank Nederland (Food Bank Netherlands)** distributes food parcels in municipalities across the country:
- Eligibility info: https://voedselbankennederland.nl/vertalingen/english/

**5) Financial support**
- If you are in a public shelter, you get your **living allowance from the municipality where you are registered**.
- This may be paid to a bank account, money card, in cash, or in goods.
- In some municipalities, if meals are provided, the allowance may be lower.

More info:
https://www.government.nl/topics/reception-of-refugees-from-ukraine/work-and-income

**6) Healthcare**
The documents say that once registered and covered by Temporary Protection, refugees from Ukraine are entitled to **healthcare**.

More official information:
https://www.government.nl/topics/reception-of-refugees-from-ukraine/arrival-registration-and-stay

More generally:
- You can register for the **Basic Registration of Persons (BRP)** at the **municipality where you are staying**.
- After you register in the BRP, your registration is **automatically sent to the IND**.
- After registration, you will receive a **BSN number**.
- With your BSN, you can then apply for a **DigiD** to access online government services.

There is also a step-by-step guide here:
https://www.refugeehelp.nl/en/ukrainian-refugee/article/100040-this-is-what-you-should-do-if-you-have-temporary-protection

user_input: I am feeling unwell and I do not have health insurance. What are my options for healthcare compared to someone who has insurance?
bot_output:
You always have the right to medically necessary care in the Netherlands.

How care is paid for depends on your situation:

user_input: Can you tell me how safety advice or resources might change depending on my personal situation or where I am staying? I want to make sure I am protected.

user_input: If my safety concern suddenly gets worse, what immediate steps can I take to protect myself?
bot_output:
If your safety concern becomes urgent or life-threatening, call 112 immediately. Everyone has the right to call.

Depending on the situation, you can also:
- Contact Veilig Thuis (Safe at Home) at 0800-2000 for advice, support, or to report domestic violence or child abuse. This can be done anonymously.
- Use the chat on the Veilig Thuis website Monday to Friday between 9:00 and 17:00.
- Go to an emergency shelter of the municipality if you no longer feel safe staying with your host family.

If you want, I can also help you find a nearby registration point if you share your location.

Yes. Based on the information I have, there are services in the Netherlands that offer confidential support and care:

1. HIV support
You can contact the Service Point of the HIV Association. A volunteer can answer your questions.

- Phone: 020 - 689 25 77
- Available: Monday, Tuesday and Thursday from 14:00 to 22:00
- Email: servicepunt@hivvereniging.nl
- Website: https://www.hivvereniging.nl/blog/belangenbeschijning/13701-hoe-zit-het-met-hiv-zorg-voor-vluchtelingen-uit-oekraine

2. Confidential sexual health care in Amsterdam
The GGD Center for Sexual Health in Amsterdam provides free care, and all healthcare workers have professional secrecy.

They can help with:
- HIV-related sexual health questions
- PEP/PrEP
- contraception
- vaccinations
- sexual violence
- gender issues
- sexual orientation
- sex work

Important for your situation:
- You do not need ID
- You do not need a BSN
- You do not need health insurance
- You do not need a referral from a doctor
- Care is free of charge

Contact:
- Appointment website: https://afspraak.ggdaphrodite.nl/?lang=en
- Phone: (020) 555 5822
- Address: GGD Amsterdam Centrum voor Seksuele Gezondheid, Nieuwe Achtergracht 100, 1018 WT Amsterdam

3. If you are undocumented
If you remain in the Netherlands without residency status, you are undocumented. Even then, you still have the right to necessary medical care and judicial assistance.

For more information, you can contact the Red Cross:
- WhatsApp: https://wa.me/31614458781
- Website: https://helpfulinformation.redcross.nl/

If you want, I can also help you choose which of these services is best for HIV treatment, testing, or emotional support.

More information:

user_input: I am a new arrival and I am trying to understand the differences between municipal shelters and host family options for Ukrainians. Can you explain how these options compare?
bot_output:
As Aidly, I can explain based on the information I have:

### Municipal shelter
- If you arrive in the Netherlands and need shelter, you should go to a **municipality (gemeente)**.
- The municipality registers displaced Ukrainians and helps find housing.
- If the municipality has space, it can place you in **municipal shelter**.
- If you stay in a municipal shelter and you are **18+ with a job or other income**, from **1 July 2024** you must **help pay for your reception**, and you will no longer receive a living allowance.
- If you have a **paid job**, you may still remain in the municipal reception centre, but you must pay a contribution.
- It is usually **very difficult to switch** from one municipal shelter to another.
- If you are only **visiting temporarily or passing through**, you **cannot use municipal shelter** and are **not entitled to an allowance**.

### Host family / private shelter
- You may also stay with a **host family**, friends, or relatives as a form of **private reception**.
- If you do not feel comfortable or safe with a host family, you can go to an **emergency shelter of the municipalities**.
- You can also **look for a new host family** through your own social network or local initiatives.
- If you move to a new host family, it is important to **register the new address in the BRP** (or update it if you stay in the same municipality).
- A host family is **not obliged** to accommodate visiting family members.
- It is **no longer possible** to sign up to be placed in a host family through the former matching project.

### Important difference
- **Municipal shelter** is arranged by the **municipality**.
- **Host family accommodation** is a **private arrangement**, often through your own network or local initiatives.

If you want, I can also give you a **simple comparison table** of municipal shelter vs host family.

user_input: Can you explain the differences between emergency municipal shelters and host family accommodations for people who feel unsafe? I want to understand which option might be better for my situation.
bot_output:
If you feel unsafe at a host family, there are a few important differences between staying with a host family and going to a municipal emergency shelter.

### If you stay with a host family
- A host family is a **private accommodation**.
- Sharing a household can be difficult, especially because of differences in:
  - lifestyle
  - food
  - manners
  - house rules
- If you **do not feel comfortable** or **do not feel safe**, you do **not have to stay there**.
- You can also **look for another host family** through your own network or local initiatives.
- If you move to a new host family, you must:
  - register in the **BRP** of the new municipality, or
  - report your new address if you stay in the same municipality.

### If you go to a municipal emergency shelter
- You can **always go to an emergency shelter of the municipality** if you no longer want to stay with your host family.
- If you are in **immediate danger**, call **112**.
- You can also contact **Veilig Thuis (Safe at Home)** at **0800-2000**.
- If you share your location, a nearby **registration point** can be found for you.

### What may be better for your situation
Based on the information available:
- **A host family** may feel more personal, but it can also create tension because you live in someone else’s home and follow their household rules.
- **A municipal emergency shelter** may be a better option if your main concern is **safety** or if you want to leave the host family quickly.

I don’t have information in the documents comparing comfort, privacy, or quality between these two options in more detail.

For more safety information:
- https://www.refugeehelp.nl/en/ukrainian-refugee/article/100105-safety-in-the-netherlands
- www.refugeehelp.nl/get-help/category/safety

If you want, I can also help you think through your situation step by step.

user_input: I am an unaccompanied minor from Ukraine. What steps do I need to take to register and get immediate shelter?
bot_output:
If you are an unaccompanied minor from Ukraine, these are the steps mentioned in the information I have:

1. Go to a municipality in the Netherlands to register.
   - You should be registered in the BRP (Basic Registration of Persons).
   - Children travelling alone from Ukraine also have to go to the municipality to get Temporary Protection.

2. The municipality should determine that you are unaccompanied.
   - When the municipality sees that a minor is travelling without parents, they should contact Nidos immediately.

3. Nidos will do an intake.
   - Nidos speaks with the minor and, if possible, remotely with the parents.
   - Nidos then assesses whether temporary guardianship is appropriate.

4. Shelter must be arranged immediately.
   - Unaccompanied children should always get shelter right away.
   - Nidos is responsible for the shelter of unaccompanied minors.
   - Nidos arranges shelter in host families, preferably with the same cultural background.

The municipality can contact Nidos via:
- 088-5011885
- oekraine@nidos.nl

There is also a note that municipalities currently have limited shelter places in general, but for unaccompanied minors, shelter must be arranged right away.

user_input: I want to find a safe place to sleep overnight. What should I consider about the location and accessibility?

If you need a safe place to sleep overnight, these are the main things to consider based on the information I have:

- The place should be an emergency or crisis shelter arranged through the municipality.
- If you are under the Temporary Protection Directive, you should first report to the municipality where you are registered and ask for a place in municipal reception.
- If there is no space there, the municipality contacts the safety region to look for a place nearby. If needed, they can request relocation to another region.
- If you do not feel safe with your host family, you can go to an emergency shelter of the municipality instead.
- If you are in immediate danger, call 112.
- You can also contact Veilig Thuis (Safe at Home) at 0800-2000 for help and advice.

About accessibility and what should be available at the shelter, the documents say a crisis emergency shelter should have:
- beds, mattresses, pillows, and blankets
- hygiene supplies
- meals or dining money
- wifi
- charging stations
- cleaning supplies
- clothing
- access to medical care
- third-party insurance
- space for children

If you have a medical condition, use a wheelchair, are pregnant, are traveling with children, or have other vulnerabilities, this is important to mention, because vulnerable people are specifically taken into account.

If you share your location, I can help you think through what kind of registration point or municipal shelter to ask for.

user_input: My host is not allowing me to register for BRP. What options do I have for finding shelter or legal housing?
bot_output:
If your host is not allowing you to register, it is important to find a place where you can register in the Netherlands.

Your options are:

- Ask for a place in a municipal shelter.
- Look for other housing or another host family where you can register.
- Search through your own social network or local initiatives for a new host family.
- If you move, register in the BRP of the new municipality, or report your new address if you stay in the same municipality.
- If you cannot find a place yourself, report to a municipality to ask for help and to register.

Important:
- If you are not registered, you cannot get Temporary Protection.
- If you had Temporary Protection before and deregistered later, you may lose that status because it can appear that you left the country.
- Social benefits are connected to your address.
- Hosts can often register refugees from Ukraine without losing their own social benefits.

You can also check whether there is an organization in your town that offers free legal advice about this issue.

Also, make sure to check how long you can still stay with your current host so you do not end up without shelter. If you think you may be left on the street, ask the municipality for emergency shelter.

user_input: I need to leave my host family urgently. What should I do to stay safe and find shelter?
bot_output:

- Call free: 0800 0117

context:
["Document: What is the Temporary Protection Directive?

The Temporary Protection Directive entitles you to reception, health care, and education for minor children in the Netherlands.

As well as the possibility to work.

If you are covered by the directive, you may stay in the Netherlands until at least 4 March 2027.   

Please note: The Temporary Protection Directive has been extended until March 2027.

However, in the case or a durable ceasefire this might be withdrawn again.  

For the most recent information see: - https://ind.nl/en/ukraine/temporary-protection-directive-ukraine - https://www.government.nl/topics/reception-of-refugees-from-ukraine/third-country-nationals", "Document: Does The Netherlands still accept people from Ukraine?

Yes, the Netherlands is still accepting people from Ukraine.

The Temporary Protection Directive was extended to March 2027.   

The Temporary Protection Directive grants Ukrainian citizens and third-country nationals who qualify for the Temporary Protection Directive protection until the date it expires.

The duration of the Temporary Protection Directive was recently extended to March 2027.

With the Temporary Protection Directive, you can get access to a shelter location, health care, and education for children below 18 in the Netherlands.

You will also get the possibility to work.

You will receive some financial support as long as you do not have work yet.  

Please note: the Temporary Protection Directive is not valid after 4 March 2024 for 'third-country nationals' (persons without Ukrainian nationality with a temporary residence permit in Ukraine, who registered before 19 years July 2022 in the Basic Registration of Persons (BRP)).", "Document: You can read more information about the Temporary Protection Directive and the criteria here:  - https://www.refugeehelp.nl/en/ukrainian-refugee/article/100187-conditions-of-temporary-protection-directive  - https://ind.nl/en/ukraine/temporary-protection-directive-ukraine - https://www.government.nl/topics/reception-of-refugees-from-ukraine/third-country-nationals", "Document: Can I change temporary protection in another EU country to temporary protection in the Netherlands?

Yes you can.

Please note that you can only fall under the temporary protection directive in one EU country.

People can live and work legally only in the country that granted temporary protection.

People still have a right to travel as tourists within EU under “90 days” rule.   

According to the IND, you do not need to deregister in the country where you currently have temporary protection.

That way, if your request for temporary protection in the Netherlands is denied, you will still have temporary protection elsewhere.

user_input: I urgently need a job but I do not have an IND sticker or card. What can I do to find legal employment and stay safe?
bot_output:
Without an IND sticker or card, you cannot legally work yet in the Netherlands.

What you can do:
- If you fall under the Temporary Protection Directive, make an appointment with the IND as soon as possible to get your proof of residency.
- If you already registered in the BRP, you must make this IND appointment within 4 weeks after registration.
- You can only work legally after you receive the sticker, paper, or card from the IND.
- A BSN number alone is not enough to work legally.

To stay safe while looking for work:
- Opora provides legal information for displaced persons from Ukraine about work issues such as labor contracts, pension, and child allowance: https://www.oporafoundation.nl/
- FairWork helps people with problems at work, labour exploitation, or human trafficking.

If you already have a sticker or card that was valid until 4 March 2023, 2024, or 2025, the IND should have sent you an extension letter. The combination of that letter with your sticker/card is enough to show you may live and work in the Netherlands.

More information:
- IND: https://ind.nl/en/ukraine/temporary-protection-directive-ukraine#working-and-studying-in-the-netherlands
- Proof of residency: https://ind.nl/en/ukraine-appointment-to-collect-proof-of-residency

user_input: I need emergency housing and healthcare, but I haven't found a job yet. What options are available for me?
bot_output:

- Call **112** if you are in immediate danger or have a medical emergency.
- You can also go to the **Emergency Room** at the nearest hospital or the **huisartsenpost** for urgent care.

About work and income:

- The documents say that if you stay in a **municipal shelter** or **private shelter**, you receive **living allowance**.
- If you rent your own independent accommodation, you are **no longer entitled to living allowance**.

Healthcare and shelter facilities:

- Crisis emergency shelters should provide basic necessities such as beds, hygiene goods, meals or dining money, wifi, cleaning supplies, clothing, and **access to medical care**.

Useful links:
- Red Cross shelter information: https://www.rodekruis.nl/english-information/
- RefugeeHelp healthcare info: https://www.refugeehelp.nl/en/ukrainian-refugee/article/100072-this-is-how-the-dutch-healthcare-system-works
- RefugeeHelp housing/shelter info: http://www.refugeehelp.nl

user_input: I am feeling unwell but I do not have health insurance. What options or resources are available to me?
bot_output:
You always have the right to medically necessary care in the Netherlands.

If you are uninsured, you can still get medical help. This is reimbursed through a special subsidy. Sometimes GPs do not know this, so you can refer them to the CAK website:
https://www.hetcak.nl/zakelijk/regelingen/regeling-onverzekerden/subsidie-aanvragen/aanvraag

- If not, ask the municipality where you are staying which GP nearby can help you.

If you are in an emergency shelter:
- Contact the medical facilities there.
- For example, Doctors of the World visits various emergency shelters.

If you are from Ukraine and have a BSN, necessary medical care may also be covered under the RMO scheme. Under this scheme, you do not have to pay insurance premium or eigen risico.

If you want, I can also help explain how to find a GP.
