user_input: I need medical care, but I am not sure how my shelter registration and insurance status affect my access to doctors.
bot_output:
If you are a displaced person from Ukraine, your access to medical care depends mainly on your status and where you are staying:

- If you have a BSN, since 1 July 2022 you fall under the RMO (Medical Care for Displaced Persons Regulation).
  - Basic and urgent medical care are covered.
  - You do not have to pay insurance premium.
  - You do not have to pay the “eigen risico” (deductible).

- If you start working in the Netherlands, you do need to take out health insurance yourself.

- If you have received a regular residence permit, you must apply for health insurance yourself once the municipality houses you as a permit holder.

- If you have an asylum application pending, and you are a third-country national, from 4 March 2024 the RMO ends and you fall under the RMA (Asylum Seekers Medical Care Arrangement). The content is similar.

About finding a doctor:
- If you are staying with a host family:
  - First check whether you can go to the host’s GP.
  - If not, ask the municipality where you are staying which nearby GP can help you.

- If you are in an emergency shelter:
  - Contact the medical facilities present there.
  - The shelter itself can usually tell you what care is available.

- Even if you are uninsured, you can still get medical help.
  - This is reimbursed through a special subsidy.
  - If a GP is unsure, they can be referred to the CAK website:
    https://www.hetcak.nl/zakelijk/regelingen/regeling-onverzekerden/subsidie-aanvragen/aanvraag

About shelter registration:
- If you stay in a municipal shelter, the municipality will contact you.
- If you stay with people and want to register in that municipality, you need to register yourself, usually at city hall. Check your municipality’s website.

Also, municipalities are responsible for reception, shelter, allowance, and medical care.

If you want, I can also help you figure out which of these situations applies to you.

   The Dutch government asks Ukrainians who can do so to make every effort to find a place themselves.

   - Marktplaats
   - Facebook groups per city

2. **Register with a municipality**
   You can register at **any municipality**, in person or sometimes by email.

3. **Ask the municipality for housing help**
   After registration, the municipality will help with housing if they have space.

4. **If the municipality has no space**
   They can contact the **Regional Coordination Centre for Refugee Dispersal (RCVS)**, which may escalate to the **National Centre for Refugee Dispersal (LCVS)**.

5. **Ask for written confirmation**
   It is a good idea to ask the municipality for **written confirmation of your visit**.

6. **Ask for a temporary solution**
   If they cannot help immediately, ask whether they can provide a **temporary place to stay while they search**.

- If you rent your **own independent accommodation**, you are **no longer entitled to living allowance**.

user_input: My host is refusing to register my address. Will this affect my Temporary Protection status, benefits, or access to alternative housing?
bot_output:
Yes.

- It is very important to be registered at an address in the Netherlands.
- If you are not registered, you cannot get Temporary Protection.
- If you were registered before, got Temporary Protection, and later deregistered, you can lose Temporary Protection status because it may appear that you left the country.
- Social benefits are also connected to your address.

If your host refuses to let you register, the advice is to:
- ask for a place in a municipal shelter, or
- look for other housing where you can register.

Also, make sure to check how long you can still stay with your host so you are not left without housing.

If you already have Temporary Protection and need reception, you should report to the municipality where you are registered and request a place in municipal reception facilities. If there is no room, the municipality contacts the safety region to look for a place.

You can still have your child attend school in the Netherlands.

- All children in the Netherlands have to attend school, regardless of their residence status.
- In principle, children from age 4 can already attend school.
- Children must go to school until they are 18 years old and have obtained a diploma.
- You can register your child at any school, and the school decides whether your child will be admitted.
- There are special intermediary classes where children can first learn Dutch.

About missing identification documents:
- For school, the documents provided do not describe a special identification procedure for school admission.
- If your child does not have proof of identification, there is an option for municipality registration:
  - Children from Ukraine without proof of identification can be registered with their parents at the municipality.
  - In the absence of documents, parents can make a statement on oath establishing the identity of the children.
  - The children are then registered by the municipality together with the parents.

If you also do not have documents:
- Without documents, you currently cannot register for the BRP.
- If you have Ukrainian nationality but cannot prove it with an ID or passport, you should contact the Ukrainian Embassy in The Hague.
- The embassy may be able to provide proof of identity and nationality.
- The embassy can issue an identifying certificate that can be used to register for the BRP at the municipality.

Ukrainian Embassy in The Hague:
- Zeestraat 78, 2518 AD The Hague
- Open Monday to Friday, 09:00–13:00
- Telephone: +31 (70) 360 72 18
- Email: emb_nl@mfa.gov.ua
- Website: https://netherlands.mfa.gov.ua/en

Useful links:
- Education: https://www.government.nl/topics/reception-of-refugees-from-ukraine/education
- More education info: https://www.refugeehelp.nl/en/ukrainian-refugee/article/100007-education-for-children-from-ukraine-who-cannot-speak-dutch-yet

If you want, I can also help you with the BRP registration steps.

  - If you do have a job or your own income, starting from 1 July 2024 you must help pay for the shelter.

- and have a job or other income such as unemployment benefit, sickness/disability benefit, or another allowance.

You must inform the municipality if you start a paid job or move out.

user_input: Hi, I am Ukrainian but I was registered in Poland before coming here. Is the shelter options different for me than for Ukrainians who come straight here? I am a bit confused about my rights and what I can get.
bot_output:
Hi, I’m Aidly. No, the shelter process is not described as different just because you were registered in Poland before coming to the Netherlands.

Based on the information I have:

- Yes, you can still try to get shelter in the Netherlands if you were already registered in another Schengen country.
- To do this, you should make sure:
  - you have Ukrainian nationality or a valid permanent Ukrainian residence permit, and
  - you left Ukraine after 26 November 2021.
- When you arrive in the Netherlands, you should report to any municipality to try to register and receive shelter.

Important points:
- There is currently a shortage of shelter places, so there is no guarantee a municipality can offer you shelter immediately.
- If possible, you are asked to try to find a place to stay yourself.
- If you cannot find housing yourself, go to a municipality for help and registration.
- After registration, the municipality helps with housing. If they do not have space, they may contact regional or national coordination centers.
- It is a good idea to ask the municipality for written confirmation of your visit.
- If they cannot help immediately, you can ask whether a temporary solution can be provided while they search for a place for you.

About your rights:
- To be covered by Temporary Protection in the Netherlands, you need to be registered in the BRP and get a residence sticker from the IND.
- The IND appointment should be scheduled within 4 weeks after BRP registration.
- After that, refugees from Ukraine are entitled to accommodation, a subsistence allowance, healthcare, and education.

You can also check:
- Red Cross info: English: https://www.rodekruis.nl/english-information/
- RefugeeHelp: https://www.refugeehelp.nl/ru/ukrainian-refugee/article/100179-chto-neobhodimo-sdelat-po-pribytii-v-niderlandy

user_input: Hi, I am an asylum seeker and my Dutch is not good. How can I find a doctor who speaks English in the hospital? I feel lost and scared.
bot_output:

Based on the information I have:

- In the Netherlands, you usually need to go to a General Practitioner (GP) first.
- The GP can refer you to a hospital or specialist if needed.
- You often cannot directly arrange specialist care through the hospital yourself.

If your Dutch is not good:

- You can take a Dutch-speaking friend with you.
- You can ask for a translator/interpreter.
- The doctor can arrange a translator, and this is free for you.
- It is best to say this when making the appointment.
- You can also say if you prefer a man or a woman interpreter.
- Usually the doctor contacts the translator service and uses them by phone during the appointment.
- In difficult situations, an interpreter may also be present in person, but the doctor decides if this is necessary.

More information:
- https://www.zoschakeltueentolkin.nl/
- https://www.refugeehelp.nl/en/ukrainian-refugee/article/100398-what-you-need-to-know-if-you-have-a-healthcare-appointment-and-do-not-speak-dutch

To find a GP during working hours:
- First check whether you can go to your host’s GP, if you stay with a host family.
- You can ask the municipality where you are staying which GP can help you.
- You can also search here:
  - https://www.kiesuwhuisarts.nl/
  - https://www.zorgkaartnederland.nl/huisarts?zoekterm=huisarts.

If you are in an emergency shelter:
- Ask the medical facilities at the shelter, because they may already know which doctors can help.

I do not have information that explains how to find a hospital doctor specifically by English language. What I can say is that you can ask for an interpreter for your appointment.

If this is an emergency:
- Call 112
- Or go to the emergency room / huisartsenpost

If you want, I can also help you with the next step: finding a GP near where you are staying.

user_input: I am Ukrainian minor here alone, not with family. I dont know what to do for shelter and registration, and I heard about Nidos and municipality but its confusing. Can you help me, I dont speak Dutch good.
bot_output:
Yes — if you are under 18 and in the Netherlands without your parents, you should do this:

1. Go to a municipality and register there  
- Unaccompanied Ukrainian children should always be registered with the municipality.  
- This is so you are included in the BRP (Basic Registration Persons / Personal Records Database).

2. Tell the municipality clearly that you are alone and under 18  
- When the municipality sees that a minor is unaccompanied, they should contact Nidos immediately.

3. Nidos will do an intake  
- Nidos speaks with you.  
- If possible, they also contact your parents remotely.  
- Nidos decides whether temporary guardianship should be requested.

4. Shelter must be arranged right away  
- Children travelling alone must get shelter immediately.  
- Nidos is responsible for shelter for unaccompanied minors.  
- Nidos arranges shelter in host families, preferably with the same cultural background.

Nidos contact details  
- Phone: 088-5011885  
- Email: oekraine@nidos.nl

So in short: register at the municipality first, say you are a Ukrainian minor alone, and the municipality should contact Nidos for your shelter and support.

For the most recent information:
- https://www.nidos.nl/oekraine/
- https://www.unicef.nl/ons-werk/noodhulp/oekraine/onbegeleide-kinderen-uit-oekraine

If you want, I can also help you write a short English message you can show to the municipality staff.

user_input: I have Dutch nationality but I need to go back to Ukraine for more than 14 days. Will my shelter and allowance be stopped? I'm worried because I don't know all the rules.
bot_output:
If you live in a municipal shelter, the rules in the documents say:

- You may leave the shelter for up to 14 days per calendar year and keep your shelter place.
- You may leave for up to 28 days per calendar year and keep your living allowance.
- If you are away for more than 14 days, the municipality may give your shelter place to someone else.
- If you are away for more than 28 days, the municipality can stop your living allowance.
- If you leave without reporting it, the municipality can stop the allowance immediately and you can lose the shelter place immediately.

So for a trip of more than 14 days:
- your shelter is not guaranteed and may be given to someone else;
- your allowance can continue up to 28 days if your departure was reported in advance;
- after 28 days, the municipality can stop the allowance.

When you return, you must report again to the municipality or reception center where you stayed before. If you still meet the rules, you can receive living allowance again, and you may be given another reception location.

I don’t know from the documents whether having Dutch nationality changes these rules.

- **You currently cannot register for the BRP without documents.**

- Email: **emb_nl@mfa.gov.ua**

- It also says that **hosts can register refugees from Ukraine without, for example, losing their social benefits**.
- Your host may be afraid it will affect their finances, but **this is often not the case**.

If your host still does not allow registration:

- It is best to ask for a **municipal shelter** or look for **other housing where you can register**.
- Also make sure you know **how long you can still stay** there, so you do not risk ending up without housing.
- You can also check whether there is an organization in your town that gives **free legal advice** about this issue.

One more important point:

1. **Contact the Ukrainian embassy** to get proof of identity/nationality.
2. **Try to reassure your host** that registration does not necessarily mean they lose benefits.
3. If they still refuse, **ask the municipality for shelter** or find another place where you can register.

user_input: Hi, I am a third-country national and my Ukrainian permit expired. Can I still get healthcare or education now? I am worried because I don't know what rules apply for people like me after 2024.
bot_output:
Hi, I’m Aidly.

Based on the information I have:

- If you are a third-country national with a temporary residence permit in Ukraine, your temporary protection was valid until 4 March 2024.
- There was a freeze on the end of temporary protection for some third-country nationals. This freeze ends on 5 September 2024.
- Until that date, people covered by the freeze continue to have all rights under Temporary Protection.
- After 4 September 2024, third-country nationals still have the right to shelter for 4 weeks while leaving voluntarily, but the right to work and access to education end on 4 September.

For healthcare:
- If you still fall under Temporary Protection during the freeze, you keep the related rights until 5 September 2024.
- If you have an asylum application pending, from 4 March 2024 the medical care scheme changes from the RMO to the RMA, and the content is similar.

For education:
- Children under 18 always have the right to education, regardless of status, as long as they live in the Netherlands and are enrolled in school.
- Students already enrolled before 4 March 2024 may complete their studies if they had lawful residence at the time of enrolment.
- Third-country nationals who were not lawfully residing in the Netherlands on 4 March 2024 may not start a new course.

Important:
- The freeze only applies if your temporary protection ended on 5 March 2024 and you were registered in the BRP.
- If you were not registered before 19 July 2022, or you were deregistered, you may be excluded from the directive and not entitled to reception and facilities.

user_input: Hi, I have Ukrainian passport and I need to register at gemeente for shelter and temporary protection. Can you tell me what I need to do? I am not sure about the steps, my English is not so good.
bot_output:
Hi! I’m Aidly.  

If you have a Ukrainian passport, these are the steps:

1. **Go to a municipality (gemeente)** in the city where you arrive.
   - You can register at **any municipality**.
   - Sometimes this can be done **in person** or **by email**.

2. **Ask to register for shelter and temporary protection**.
   - If the municipality has space, they will help you with housing.
   - If they do not have space, they can contact the regional or national refugee coordination system.

3. **If possible, try to arrange an address yourself**.
   - The information says you need a **local address (accommodation)** to apply for temporary protection.
   - Because shelter places are limited, the Dutch government asks people to find housing themselves if possible.

4. **If you cannot find a place to stay yourself, go to the municipality for help**.
   - It is a good idea to ask for **written confirmation** of your visit.
   - If they cannot help immediately, you can ask whether they can give a **temporary solution** while they look for a place.

5. **Register in the BRP** (Basic Registration of Persons).
   - To be covered by temporary protection in the Netherlands, you need to be registered in the **BRP**.

6. **Make an appointment with the IND within 4 weeks after BRP registration**.
   - You need to get a **residence sticker/proof of residence** from the IND.

After this, you can be entitled to:
- **accommodation**
- **living allowance**
- **healthcare**
- **education**

If you are **staying in a municipal shelter**, the municipality will contact you.  
If you are **staying with private people** and want to register there, you usually need to **register yourself**, often at the **city hall**. Please check your municipality website.

Useful guides:
- https://www.refugeehelp.nl/en/ukrainian-refugee/article/100040-this-is-what-you-should-do-if-you-have-temporary-protection
- https://www.government.nl/topics/reception-of-refugees-from-ukraine/arrival-registration-and-stay

If you want, I can also give you this in **simple English** or **Ukrainian/Russian**.

bot_output:
Hi, I’m Aidly. I’m sorry you’re dealing with this.

You have the right to see a doctor and get necessary medical care in the Netherlands.

What to do:
- First, go to a General Practitioner (GP / family doctor).
- In the Netherlands, the GP is the first doctor to visit.
- Only the GP can refer you to a specialist or hospital if needed.

How to find a GP:
- https://www.kiesuwhuisarts.nl/
- https://www.zorgkaartnederland.nl/huisarts?zoekterm=huisarts.

You are not obliged to register with a GP, but it is recommended.

If you need treatment in a hospital:
- First visit a GP.
- If necessary, the GP will refer you to the hospital.
- If you have your medical file, bring it with you.

If your English or Dutch is limited:
- Having a Dutch-speaking person help can make it easier, but it is not mandatory.
- The doctor will determine whether a translator is necessary.
- If the doctor does not want to arrange a translator or does not know how, you can show this website:
  https://www.zoschakeltueentolkin.nl/

If it is urgent in the evening or outside office hours:
- You can go to the huisartsenpost.
- In an emergency, call 112 or go to the Emergency Room in the nearest hospital.

More information:
- Dutch healthcare system: https://www.refugeehelp.nl/en/ukrainian-refugee/article/100072-this-is-how-the-dutch-healthcare-system-works
- Healthcare appointment and language help: https://www.refugeehelp.nl/en/ukrainian-refugee/article/100398-what-you-need-to-know-if-you-have-a-healthcare-appointment-and-do-not-speak-dutch
- General refugee information: https://www.refugeehelp.nl/en/ukrainian-refugee

If you want, I can also help you find a GP near your area or postcode.

The authorities’ priority is to ensure accommodation for the most vulnerable refugees.

Refugees from Ukraine who are able to, are being asked to make every effort to find a place of residence by themselves.

If not possible to find a place of residence, please report to a municipality to ask for help and to register.  

In order to be covered by the Temporary Protection Directive, refugees from Ukraine need to be registered in the Personal Records Database (BRP) and get a residence sticker from the Immigration and Naturalisation Service (IND).

The appointment with the IND should be scheduled within 4 weeks from the date of the registration in the BRP.

Refugees from Ukraine are then entitled to accommodation, a subsistence allowance, healthcare and education.
